concepts.shortDefinition: An attack in which a party controlling a majority of a network's mining power (proof of work) or stake (proof of stake) rewrites recent history, for example to double-spend coins or censor transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: An attack in which a party controlling a majority of a network's mining power (proof of work) or stake (proof of stake) rewrites recent history, for example to double-spend coins or censor transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A rouble-backed stablecoin associated with the evasion of sanctions against Russia.
concepts.bodyHtml: A rouble-backed stablecoin associated with the evasion of sanctions against Russia. The EU prohibited all transactions involving it in its 19th sanctions package against Russia, adopted in October 2025.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share class that reinvests the income it receives in the fund instead of paying it out, so that the income is reflected in a rising NAV per share.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share class that reinvests the income it receives in the fund instead of paying it out, so that the income is reflected in a rising NAV per share. A distributing share class pays income out to investors as dividends.

concepts.shortDefinition: An ETF whose manager selects investments rather than tracking an index.
concepts.bodyHtml: An ETF whose manager selects investments rather than tracking an index. In Ireland an ETF may disclose its holdings quarterly rather than daily, which supports active, “semi-transparent” ETFs.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment approach in which the manager selects assets with the aim of outperforming a benchmark or achieving a target outcome, rather than tracking an index.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment approach in which the manager selects assets with the aim of outperforming a benchmark or achieving a target outcome, rather than tracking an index.

concepts.shortDefinition: A public identifier, derived from a public key or a smart contract, to which virtual assets can be sent.
concepts.bodyHtml: A public identifier, derived from a public key or a smart contract, to which virtual assets can be sent. Anyone can see an address's balance and history on a public blockchain, but not who controls it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A key, or set of keys, with special powers over a smart contract or protocol, such as to upgrade, pause, mint or change parameters.
concepts.bodyHtml: A key, or set of keys, with special powers over a smart contract or protocol, such as to upgrade, pause, mint or change parameters. Where several keys must sign (for example three of five), the arrangement is a multisig. Whoever holds the admin key effectively controls the protocol, whatever the marketing says.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm that administers a fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm that administers a fund. It keeps or controls the register, admits investors after due diligence, reconciles holdings and corrects errors, and remains responsible even where a distributed ledger or a third party supports record-keeping.

concepts.shortDefinition: A breach of an investment restriction or other rule caused by the manager’s own action, such as buying an asset above a limit.
concepts.bodyHtml: A breach of an investment restriction or other rule caused by the manager’s own action, such as buying an asset above a limit. It must be corrected immediately, investigated for its impact and may require compensation to the fund or investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: An agent acts on a client's instructions for a fee; a principal trades against the client from its own inventory and earns the spread.
concepts.bodyHtml: An agent acts on a client's instructions for a fee; a principal trades against the client from its own inventory and earns the spread. Crypto firms often act in both capacities, so the capacity on each trade matters for conflicts and client protection.

concepts.shortDefinition: Software that acts on its own within set limits, for example holding a wallet and paying for services.
concepts.bodyHtml: Software that acts on its own within set limits, for example holding a wallet and paying for services. Good practice treats it like an employee with a signing mandate, with spending caps, oversight and a named owner.

concepts.shortDefinition: The CBI rulebook that sets the conditions for Irish AIFs (RIAIFs and QIAIFs) and their AIFMs, supplementing the AIFM Regulations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The CBI rulebook that sets the conditions for Irish AIFs (RIAIFs and QIAIFs) and their AIFMs, supplementing the AIFM Regulations. The revised Rulebook, effective 5 May 2026, removed the separate L-QIAIF category, lifted the prohibition on lending and giving guarantees and requires disclosure of at least two LMTs.

concepts.shortDefinition: Directive (EU) 2024/927, which amended the AIFMD and the UCITSD from 16 April 2026.
concepts.bodyHtml: Directive (EU) 2024/927, which amended the AIFMD and the UCITSD from 16 April 2026. It introduced EU rules on loan origination, harmonised LMTs, more reporting on delegation, minimum substance for ManCos and wider permitted services; its UCITS amendments are known as UCITS VI.

concepts.shortDefinition: Keeping signing keys on devices that are never connected to a network.
concepts.bodyHtml: Keeping signing keys on devices that are never connected to a network. An air gap is a process rather than a place, and it is broken wherever a transaction, file or image crosses in or out.

concepts.shortDefinition: A free distribution of tokens to wallet addresses, often to reward early users or attract attention.
concepts.bodyHtml: A free distribution of tokens to wallet addresses, often to reward early users or attract attention.

concepts.shortDefinition: A coin that tries to hold a peg through code and incentives, usually involving a second token, rather than reserves of real-world assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A coin that tries to hold a peg through code and incentives, usually involving a second token, rather than reserves of real-world assets. TerraUSD is the leading example of failure.

concepts.shortDefinition: A collective investment undertaking that raises capital from several investors to invest it under a defined investment policy for their benefit, and which is not a UCITS.
concepts.bodyHtml: A collective investment undertaking that raises capital from several investors to invest it under a defined investment policy for their benefit, and which is not a UCITS. Its manager is regulated under the AIFMD.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal person whose regular business is managing one or more AIFs, which means at least performing portfolio management or risk management for them.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal person whose regular business is managing one or more AIFs, which means at least performing portfolio management or risk management for them. AIFMs above the size thresholds must be authorised under the AIFMD.

concepts.shortDefinition: Directive 2011/61/EU, applying since 22 July 2013, which regulates the managers of AIFs rather than the funds themselves.
concepts.bodyHtml: Directive 2011/61/EU, applying since 22 July 2013, which regulates the managers of AIFs rather than the funds themselves. It covers authorisation, capital, organisation, delegation, depositaries, valuation, leverage, disclosure and reporting, and gives authorised AIFMs a passport to manage EEA AIFs and market them to professional investors across the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: A US trading venue for securities run by a registered broker-dealer; some tokenisation platforms operate one alongside their transfer-agency business.
concepts.bodyHtml: A US trading venue for securities run by a registered broker-dealer; some tokenisation platforms operate one alongside their transfer-agency business.

concepts.shortDefinition: The two main models for regulating crypto firms.
concepts.bodyHtml: The two main models for regulating crypto firms. AML registration (the FATF Recommendation 15 baseline, as in the EU's fifth AML Directive and the UK Money Laundering Regulations) checks owners and anti-money-laundering controls. Activity authorisation (for example MiCA in the EU) adds governance, capital, custody and conduct rules for each permitted activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A valuation method under which an instrument is carried at its purchase price adjusted for the steady accrual of any discount or premium up to maturity, rather than at its market price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A valuation method under which an instrument is carried at its purchase price adjusted for the steady accrual of any discount or premium up to maturity, rather than at its market price. Public debt CNAV MMFs, and LVNAV MMFs for assets maturing within 75 days, may use it to deal at a constant NAV.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cash and bank deposits that a UCITS may hold on an ancillary basis, for example to meet redemptions, rather than as part of its investment policy.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cash and bank deposits that a UCITS may hold on an ancillary basis, for example to meet redemptions, rather than as part of its investment policy. A feeder UCITS may hold up to 15% of its assets in ancillary liquid assets and financial derivative instruments used only for hedging.

concepts.shortDefinition: The yearly meeting of a company’s shareholders, at which the accounts are presented, directors are elected and resolutions are voted on.
concepts.bodyHtml: The yearly meeting of a company’s shareholders, at which the accounts are presented, directors are elected and resolutions are voted on. A corporate fund is generally required to hold one, but the directors of an ICAV may dispense with it; a unit trust has no such requirement.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset designed to hide the sender, receiver or amount (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset designed to hide the sender, receiver or amount (e.g. Monero). Under the EU AML Regulation, regulated firms may not handle them from July 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: A charge on a subscribing or redeeming investor, paid into the fund to cover the dealing costs caused by the transaction, so that other investors are not diluted.
concepts.bodyHtml: A charge on a subscribing or redeeming investor, paid into the fund to cover the dealing costs caused by the transaction, so that other investors are not diluted. It is an anti-dilution LMT.

concepts.shortDefinition: An LMT that passes the dealing costs of subscriptions and redemptions to the investors who trade, to protect remaining investors from dilution: a redemption fee, swing pricing, dual pricing or an anti-dilution levy.
concepts.bodyHtml: An LMT that passes the dealing costs of subscriptions and redemptions to the investors who trade, to protect remaining investors from dilution: a redemption fee, swing pricing, dual pricing or an anti-dilution levy. ESMA guidelines recommend that managers select at least one.

concepts.shortDefinition: The laws, systems and controls that prevent the financial system being used to launder the proceeds of crime or to finance terrorism.
concepts.bodyHtml: The laws, systems and controls that prevent the financial system being used to launder the proceeds of crime or to finance terrorism. For funds, AML checks on investors are mainly carried out by the TA and distributors.

concepts.term: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism
concepts.sortKey: anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism

concepts.shortDefinition: The new EU authority created to coordinate national AML supervisors and to strengthen the consistency of AML supervision across the EU.
concepts.bodyHtml: The new EU authority created to coordinate national AML supervisors and to strengthen the consistency of AML supervision across the EU.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624, which will apply from 10 July 2027 and will replace much of the national AML rulebook, including the rules on beneficial ownership, with a single EU rulebook.
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624, which will apply from 10 July 2027 and will replace much of the national AML rulebook, including the rules on beneficial ownership, with a single EU rulebook.

concepts.term: Anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing
concepts.sortKey: anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing

concepts.shortDefinition: The MiFID II assessment of a client’s knowledge and experience that a firm must carry out when selling a complex product without advice.
concepts.bodyHtml: The MiFID II assessment of a client’s knowledge and experience that a firm must carry out when selling a complex product without advice. The client is warned if the product is not appropriate.

concepts.shortDefinition: Buying and selling the same or equivalent assets to profit from a price difference between them.
concepts.bodyHtml: Buying and selling the same or equivalent assets to profit from a price difference between them. APs’ arbitrage between an ETF’s market price and the value of its assets keeps the two close; some hedge fund strategies seek arbitrage opportunities.

concepts.shortDefinition: Eligible firms buy a stablecoin below par and redeem it with the issuer at par, or mint at par and sell above it.
concepts.bodyHtml: Eligible firms buy a stablecoin below par and redeem it with the issuer at par, or mint at par and sell above it. This arbitrage is what holds the peg for the many holders who cannot redeem directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the SFDR, a fund that does not promote environmental or social characteristics or have a sustainable investment objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the SFDR, a fund that does not promote environmental or social characteristics or have a sustainable investment objective. It must still disclose how sustainability risks are integrated into its investment decisions, or why they are not relevant.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the SFDR, a fund that promotes environmental or social characteristics, provided its investee companies follow good governance practices.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the SFDR, a fund that promotes environmental or social characteristics, provided its investee companies follow good governance practices. It must provide the standard pre-contractual and periodic templates. The category is a disclosure category, not a label.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the SFDR, a fund that has sustainable investment as its objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the SFDR, a fund that has sustainable investment as its objective. It must provide the standard pre-contractual and periodic templates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Deciding how to divide a portfolio between asset classes, regions and sectors.
concepts.bodyHtml: Deciding how to divide a portfolio between asset classes, regions and sectors. A strategic allocation sets the long-term mix; a tactical allocation adjusts it in the short term to take advantage of market conditions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A group of assets with similar features, such as fixed income, equities, derivatives, real assets and digital assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A group of assets with similar features, such as fixed income, equities, derivatives, real assets and digital assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Removing value from a company after acquiring it, for example through large distributions or capital reductions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Removing value from a company after acquiring it, for example through large distributions or capital reductions. The AIFMD restricts such actions for a period after an AIF acquires control of a non-listed company.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiCA, a crypto-asset that aims to keep a stable value by referencing another value, right or combination, including one or more official currencies, that is not an e-money token.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiCA, a crypto-asset that aims to keep a stable value by referencing another value, right or combination, including one or more official currencies, that is not an e-money token.

concepts.shortDefinition: The total market value of the assets a manager manages on behalf of its funds or clients.
concepts.bodyHtml: The total market value of the assets a manager manages on behalf of its funds or clients. The AIFMD applies in full only to AIFMs whose AUM exceeds the €100 million or €500 million thresholds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Delivery versus payment in which the asset and the cash move together in one step, or not at all.
concepts.bodyHtml: Delivery versus payment in which the asset and the cash move together in one step, or not at all. It removes settlement risk but requires the cash leg to be available, and pre-funded, on the same ledger.

concepts.shortDefinition: (1) A report by an accountant on a stablecoin's reserves at a point in time, narrower than an audit.
concepts.bodyHtml: (1) A report by an accountant on a stablecoin's reserves at a point in time, narrower than an audit. (2) In Ethereum proof of stake, a validator's vote on the state of the chain.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent examination of a fund’s financial statements by its external auditor, planned and performed to obtain reasonable assurance that they are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, so that the auditor can give an opinion on them.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent examination of a fund’s financial statements by its external auditor, planned and performed to obtain reasonable assurance that they are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, so that the auditor can give an opinion on them.

concepts.shortDefinition: An expert review of specific code at a point in time.
concepts.bodyHtml: An expert review of specific code at a point in time. It does not cover later changes, the compiler, integrations, economic attacks or key management.

concepts.shortDefinition: The grant by a regulator of permission for a fund, manager or service provider to operate.
concepts.bodyHtml: The grant by a regulator of permission for a fund, manager or service provider to operate. For a fund it usually follows a review of its documents and of the parties appointed to it, which may result in additional conditions or required changes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank, broker-dealer or other trading firm that has an agreement with an ETF to create and redeem its shares directly with the fund in large blocks (creation units), and so links the primary and secondary markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank, broker-dealer or other trading firm that has an agreement with an ETF to create and redeem its shares directly with the fund in large blocks (creation units), and so links the primary and secondary markets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Authorised push payment fraud: the victim is tricked into authorising a bank payment, often to an account a mule controls, and the funds are then converted to crypto.
concepts.bodyHtml: Authorised push payment fraud: the victim is tricked into authorising a bank payment, often to an account a mule controls, and the funds are then converted to crypto.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract that holds pools of two or more tokens and sets prices by formula, letting users trade against the pool rather than against another person's order.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract that holds pools of two or more tokens and sets prices by formula, letting users trade against the pool rather than against another person's order.

concepts.shortDefinition: Retail apps (business-to-consumer), institutional desks and APIs (business-to-business), and crypto services offered under another firm's brand with a crypto service provider behind it (B2B2C).
concepts.bodyHtml: Retail apps (business-to-consumer), institutional desks and APIs (business-to-business), and crypto services offered under another firm's brand with a crypto service provider behind it (B2B2C). In B2B2C models it matters who the end customer is and who performs customer due diligence.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reserves divided by tokens in issue on a reporting date (for example “102% backed”).
concepts.bodyHtml: Reserves divided by tokens in issue on a reporting date (for example “102% backed”). A solvency snapshot — it does not show how fast the reserves turn into cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests in a mix of asset classes, typically equities and bonds, to provide a combination of capital growth and income.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests in a mix of asset classes, typically equities and bonds, to provide a combination of capital growth and income. Also called a mixed fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The currency in which a fund’s NAV is calculated and its accounts are kept, as stated in its prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: The currency in which a fund’s NAV is calculated and its accounts are kept, as stated in its prospectus. Share classes in other currencies may be hedged against movements between it and the class currency.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Basel Committee's prudential standard for banks' exposures to cryptoassets, part of the Basel Framework with an implementation date of 1 January 2026.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Basel Committee's prudential standard for banks' exposures to cryptoassets, part of the Basel Framework with an implementation date of 1 January 2026. It sorts cryptoassets into Group 1a (tokenised traditional assets), Group 1b (stablecoins that meet strict criteria) and Group 2 (other cryptoassets, such as unbacked crypto), with Group 2 attracting the highest capital charges.

concepts.shortDefinition: A certificate of ownership of units or shares under which whoever holds the document is the owner.
concepts.bodyHtml: A certificate of ownership of units or shares under which whoever holds the document is the owner. Funds now generally may not issue them, for AML reasons, and use registered holdings instead.

concepts.shortDefinition: An index or other reference point against which a fund’s performance is measured, or which a passive fund seeks to track.
concepts.bodyHtml: An index or other reference point against which a fund’s performance is measured, or which a passive fund seeks to track. Benchmarking is the process of comparing a fund’s performance with a comparable index or a group of similar funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation governing the provision of, contribution to and use of financial benchmarks, which funds that track or measure performance against an index must consider.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation governing the provision of, contribution to and use of financial benchmarks, which funds that track or measure performance against an index must consider. Its scope was narrowed from 1 January 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right to enjoy the benefit of property that is legally owned by someone else, such as a trustee or nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right to enjoy the benefit of property that is legally owned by someone else, such as a trustee or nominee. Each unit in a unit trust represents a beneficial interest in the trust’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: In property law, the person entitled to the benefit of an asset held by a legal owner (the person registered as owner or in possession of it), such as a trustee or nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: In property law, the person entitled to the benefit of an asset held by a legal owner (the person registered as owner or in possession of it), such as a trustee or nominee. In AML law, the natural person who ultimately owns or controls an entity, for example through more than 25% of its shares or voting rights, and who must be recorded on a central register.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: In crypto, the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client or wallet. Customer due diligence must look through intermediaries such as trusts, funds and family offices to identify them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The difference between the price at which a market maker or dealer will buy an asset (the bid) and the price at which it will sell it (the offer).
concepts.bodyHtml: The difference between the price at which a market maker or dealer will buy an asset (the bid) and the price at which it will sell it (the offer). It is a cost for investors trading ETF shares and for funds buying and selling assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) for a new type of transaction output that never puts a public key on the blockchain, as protection against future quantum attacks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) for a new type of transaction output that never puts a public key on the blockchain, as protection against future quantum attacks. It is a proposal; using it would require a change to Bitcoin's rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The first blockchain, launched in 2009, and its native coin (BTC).
concepts.bodyHtml: The first blockchain, launched in 2009, and its native coin (BTC). It uses proof of work and has a fixed maximum supply of 21 million coins.

concepts.term: BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund
concepts.sortKey: blackrock usd institutional digital liquidity fund

concepts.shortDefinition: Approving a transaction without being able to see or verify what it actually does.
concepts.bodyHtml: Approving a transaction without being able to see or verify what it actually does. Blind signing was a key factor in the February 2025 Bybit hack.

concepts.shortDefinition: A batch of transactions, linked to the previous block by its hash, that is added to the blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: A batch of transactions, linked to the previous block by its hash, that is added to the blockchain.

concepts.shortDefinition: A website that displays the data on a public blockchain: blocks, transactions, addresses and smart contracts.
concepts.bodyHtml: A website that displays the data on a public blockchain: blocks, transactions, addresses and smart contracts.

concepts.shortDefinition: Whoever creates a given block, whether the winning miner or the chosen validator.
concepts.bodyHtml: Whoever creates a given block, whether the winning miner or the chosen validator. The block producer can choose which transactions to include and in what order.

concepts.shortDefinition: A type of DLT in which transactions are recorded in blocks that are linked cryptographically in a chain, making the record very hard to alter.
concepts.bodyHtml: A type of DLT in which transactions are recorded in blocks that are linked cryptographically in a chain, making the record very hard to alter. It underlies crypto-assets and many tokenised instruments.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A type of distributed ledger in which records are grouped into blocks, each linked to the one before by a cryptographic hash, so that any change to history is detectable.

concepts.shortDefinition: Tools that group addresses into clusters, attribute them to real-world entities, and score and trace transactions to detect illicit activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Tools that group addresses into clusters, attribute them to real-world entities, and score and trace transactions to detect illicit activity.

concepts.notes: token ticker; the Binance-linked BNB Chain token

concepts.shortDefinition: The body that manages and controls a company.
concepts.bodyHtml: The body that manages and controls a company. In a corporate fund it is ultimately responsible for the fund and for acting in investors’ best interests; in an externally managed fund the board of the ManCo is responsible for day-to-day management and the oversight of delegates. Boards typically meet quarterly.

concepts.term: Bona fide purchaser for value without notice
concepts.shortDefinition: A person who acquires property in good faith and for value without knowing, or being reasonably expected to know, that it is subject to a security interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person who acquires property in good faith and for value without knowing, or being reasonably expected to know, that it is subject to a security interest. The law gives such a purchaser priority over the secured creditor, who must look to the seller instead.
concepts.sortKey: bona fide purchaser for value without notice

concepts.shortDefinition: A medium- or long-term debt instrument, with a maturity of more than one year when issued, that usually pays a fixed or floating rate of interest (the coupon) and repays the principal at maturity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A medium- or long-term debt instrument, with a maturity of more than one year when issued, that usually pays a fixed or floating rate of interest (the coupon) and repays the principal at maturity.

concepts.shortDefinition: Taking a loan of cash, for example to buy assets or meet redemptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Taking a loan of cash, for example to buy assets or meet redemptions. It is a source of leverage; a UCITS may borrow only up to 10% of its net assets and only temporarily, and a fund’s prospectus states its borrowing limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: A protocol that moves value or messages between blockchains, typically by locking assets on one chain and minting a representation on the other.
concepts.bodyHtml: A protocol that moves value or messages between blockchains, typically by locking assets on one chain and minting a representation on the other. Bridges have been among the largest targets of hacks.

concepts.shortDefinition: An intermediary that executes trades on behalf of its clients and charges a fee or commission for each transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: An intermediary that executes trades on behalf of its clients and charges a fee or commission for each transaction. A dealer, by contrast, trades on its own account; a firm acting in both capacities is a broker-dealer.

concepts.shortDefinition: To permanently remove tokens from circulation, for example when a stablecoin is redeemed.
concepts.bodyHtml: To permanently remove tokens from circulation, for example when a stablecoin is redeemed.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm's documented assessment of its own money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks, as required by FATF Recommendation 1.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm's documented assessment of its own money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks, as required by FATF Recommendation 1. For a crypto firm it should map risks to each activity, product, customer type and blockchain it supports, using real exposure data.

concepts.shortDefinition: A request by the manager of a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, for investors to pay in part of their capital commitment so that it can make an investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: A request by the manager of a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, for investors to pay in part of their capital commitment so that it can make an investment. Also called a drawdown.

concepts.shortDefinition: The amount an investor agrees to provide to a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, which the manager draws down over time through capital calls (drawdowns) as investments are made.
concepts.bodyHtml: The amount an investor agrees to provide to a closed-ended fund, such as a private equity fund, which the manager draws down over time through capital calls (drawdowns) as investments are made.

concepts.shortDefinition: Government limits on the flow of capital into or out of a country, such as transaction taxes, exchange controls or restrictions on repatriating the proceeds of investments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Government limits on the flow of capital into or out of a country, such as transaction taxes, exchange controls or restrictions on repatriating the proceeds of investments. They can prevent a fund investing in a market or make it expensive.

concepts.shortDefinition: A promise that an investor will get back at least the capital invested.
concepts.bodyHtml: A promise that an investor will get back at least the capital invested. Investment funds generally do not provide one; some structured funds provide capital protection through a derivative or other instrument, at a cost to the fund and indirectly the investor.

concepts.shortDefinition: The share of a private equity fund’s profits paid to the manager, usually only after investors have received a minimum return (the hurdle).
concepts.bodyHtml: The share of a private equity fund’s profits paid to the manager, usually only after investors have received a minimum return (the hurdle).

concepts.shortDefinition: The payment side of a token trade or subscription.
concepts.bodyHtml: The payment side of a token trade or subscription. It may be commercial bank money, tokenised deposits, a regulated stablecoin or wholesale central bank money. Settlement of a tokenised asset is only as safe as its cash leg.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund depositary’s duty to check that investors’ subscription monies are received and that all of a fund’s cash is booked in properly established cash accounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund depositary’s duty to check that investors’ subscription monies are received and that all of a fund’s cash is booked in properly established cash accounts. It was harmonised for AIFs by the AIFMD and for UCITS by UCITS V.

concepts.shortDefinition: Central bank digital currency: a direct claim on a central bank.
concepts.bodyHtml: Central bank digital currency: a direct claim on a central bank. Retail CBDCs are for the public; wholesale CBDCs for settlement between financial institutions.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity that places itself between the buyer and seller of a trade, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so that each party is exposed to the CCP rather than to the other.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity that places itself between the buyer and seller of a trade, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so that each party is exposed to the CCP rather than to the other. EMIR requires many OTC derivatives to be cleared through a CCP.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity that operates a securities settlement system and records securities in book-entry form, usually for a national market.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity that operates a securities settlement system and records securities in book-entry form, usually for a national market. Where a CSD acts as issuer CSD for securities a fund holds, this is not treated as delegation of the fund depositary’s custody functions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A trading platform run by a company that holds customers' assets and matches orders on its own internal ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: A trading platform run by a company that holds customers' assets and matches orders on its own internal ledger.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transferable receipt issued by a bank for a deposit of funds for a fixed term.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transferable receipt issued by a bank for a deposit of funds for a fixed term. The bank pays the principal plus interest to the holder at maturity; CDs are money market instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: Moving funds quickly across several blockchains and tokens, often through bridges or swap services, to break the transaction trail.
concepts.bodyHtml: Moving funds quickly across several blockchains and tokens, often through bridges or swap services, to break the transaction trail. Single-chain analytics can miss it; cross-chain tracing is needed to follow the funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A security interest over an asset, usually created by a company, that gives the creditor a right to be paid out of the asset without transferring ownership.
concepts.bodyHtml: A security interest over an asset, usually created by a company, that gives the creditor a right to be paid out of the asset without transferring ownership. It may be fixed or floating.

concepts.shortDefinition: A court action against property rather than a person, to forfeit assets traced to crime.
concepts.bodyHtml: A court action against property rather than a person, to forfeit assets traced to crime. An example is the June 2025 US Department of Justice complaint seeking forfeiture of more than US$225 million in USDT. A complaint states allegations, not findings.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal system based on a comprehensive written code of rules, much less dependent on precedent, as in Luxembourg and most of continental Europe.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal system based on a comprehensive written code of rules, much less dependent on precedent, as in Luxembourg and most of continental Europe. It generally does not recognise the trust.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share class whose management fee does not include commission payable to distributors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share class whose management fee does not include commission payable to distributors. A bundled share class, by contrast, includes that commission in the management fee. Clean classes are needed where commission is banned.

concepts.shortDefinition: The signing device shows the transaction in readable form (destination, asset, amount), so the signer can verify it independently of a web screen.
concepts.bodyHtml: The signing device shows the transaction in readable form (destination, asset, amount), so the signer can verify it independently of a web screen.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process between trading and settlement in which obligations are confirmed and, where a CCP is used, the CCP becomes the counterparty to both sides.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process between trading and settlement in which obligations are confirmed and, where a CCP is used, the CCP becomes the counterparty to both sides. EMIR requires certain OTC derivatives to be centrally cleared.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account designated as holding money or assets belonging to clients, such as a fund or its investors, rather than the account holder.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account designated as holding money or assets belonging to clients, such as a fund or its investors, rather than the account holder. The bank cannot then set off the balance against the account holder’s own debts.

concepts.shortDefinition: The exclusions applying to EU Climate Transition Benchmarks – broadly, companies involved in controversial weapons or tobacco and companies violating international norms – which a fund using transition, social or governance terms in its name must apply under ESMA’s fund names guidelines).
concepts.bodyHtml: The exclusions applying to EU Climate Transition Benchmarks – broadly, companies involved in controversial weapons or tobacco and companies violating international norms – which a fund using transition, social or governance terms in its name must apply under ESMA’s fund names guidelines).

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that issues units or shares at launch and does not redeem them on demand.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that issues units or shares at launch and does not redeem them on demand. Investors exit by selling to another investor or when the fund is terminated. Many private equity, private credit and real estate funds are closed-ended.

concepts.shortDefinition: A group of addresses believed to be controlled by the same entity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A group of addresses believed to be controlled by the same entity.

concepts.shortDefinition: Grouping addresses likely to be controlled by one entity, using heuristics such as common-input ownership and change detection.
concepts.bodyHtml: Grouping addresses likely to be controlled by one entity, using heuristics such as common-input ownership and change detection. An inference, not proof; CoinJoin is designed to defeat it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A technique in which many users combine their bitcoin transactions into one, making it harder to tell which input paid which output.
concepts.bodyHtml: A technique in which many users combine their bitcoin transactions into one, making it harder to tell which input paid which output.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are generated and kept offline, away from the internet, to protect against remote attack, and used only in controlled, witnessed procedures.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are generated and kept offline, away from the internet, to protect against remote attack, and used only in controlled, witnessed procedures. Custodians typically hold most client assets in cold storage; Hong Kong requires 98% and Japan 95%. Withdrawals are slow by design.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets provided to secure an obligation, for example in derivatives, securities lending and repo transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets provided to secure an obligation, for example in derivatives, securities lending and repo transactions. It may be provided by title transfer, where full ownership passes to the receiver, or by a security interest, where the provider keeps ownership but grants a pledge or charge. Collateral over cash and financial instruments benefits from reduced formalities under the Financial Collateral Directive.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Assets pledged to secure a loan or position, which can be sold (liquidated) if their value falls below a threshold.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short-term unsecured debt instrument issued by companies, normally sold at a discount (like a zero-coupon bond) with a maturity of less than 365 days.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short-term unsecured debt instrument issued by companies, normally sold at a discount (like a zero-coupon bond) with a maturity of less than 365 days. It is a money market instrument.

concepts.shortDefinition: Client assets mixed with a firm's own in the same wallet or account.
concepts.bodyHtml: Client assets mixed with a firm's own in the same wallet or account. Commingling blurs ownership and puts client assets at risk if the firm becomes insolvent.

concepts.term: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier
concepts.sortKey: commission de surveillance du secteur financier

concepts.shortDefinition: A method of measuring the global exposure or leverage of a fund by converting each derivative position into the market value of the equivalent position in the underlying assets, allowing for netting and hedging.
concepts.bodyHtml: A method of measuring the global exposure or leverage of a fund by converting each derivative position into the market value of the equivalent position in the underlying assets, allowing for netting and hedging. A UCITS using it may not have exposure from derivatives exceeding 100% of NAV.

concepts.term: Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures
concepts.sortKey: committee on payments and market infrastructures

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish contractual fund, constituted by a deed of constitution between the ManCo and the fund depositary.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish contractual fund, constituted by a deed of constitution between the ManCo and the fund depositary. It is tax-transparent and its units may not be held by individuals, so it is used for institutional pooling, for example of a multinational group’s pension assets. It may be a UCITS or an AIF.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal system based on practice and precedent, in which earlier court decisions are used to interpret and define the law, as in Ireland, the UK and the US.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal system based on practice and precedent, in which earlier court decisions are used to interpret and define the law, as in Ireland, the UK and the US. It recognises the trust.

concepts.shortDefinition: A product, such as most AIFs or a structured UCITS, whose risks are considered difficult for a retail investor to understand.
concepts.bodyHtml: A product, such as most AIFs or a structured UCITS, whose risks are considered difficult for a retail investor to understand. It cannot be sold on an execution-only basis.

concepts.shortDefinition: The independent function within a ManCo or other regulated firm that monitors and assesses compliance with regulatory obligations and advises management and staff.
concepts.bodyHtml: The independent function within a ManCo or other regulated firm that monitors and assesses compliance with regulatory obligations and advises management and staff. With risk management, it forms the second line of defence.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of breaching regulatory requirements, such as investment restrictions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of breaching regulatory requirements, such as investment restrictions. Breaches may be advertent (caused by the manager’s actions, requiring immediate correction and possibly compensation) or inadvertent (caused by factors such as market movements).

concepts.shortDefinition: The ability of DeFi protocols to connect and build on one another, like building blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ability of DeFi protocols to connect and build on one another, like building blocks. It enables innovation but also transmits failures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The redemption of an investor’s units or shares at the fund’s initiative, for example because the investor is no longer eligible or because the fund is being terminated after its NAV has fallen below a set threshold.
concepts.bodyHtml: The redemption of an investor’s units or shares at the fund’s initiative, for example because the investor is no longer eligible or because the fund is being terminated after its NAV has fallen below a set threshold.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from holding a large exposure to a single issuer, counterparty, sector, market or service provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from holding a large exposure to a single issuer, counterparty, sector, market or service provider. Regulation limits concentration for funds sold to retail investors, and managers diversify to reduce it.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Dependence on one asset, venue, custodian, bank or service provider. In crypto markets many firms rely on the same few providers, so the risk can be shared across a whole sector.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Luxembourg, a person who effectively conducts the business of a ManCo or AIFM and is approved by the CSSF.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Luxembourg, a person who effectively conducts the business of a ManCo or AIFM and is approved by the CSSF. A ManCo must have at least two; together they form the management committee and share responsibility for areas such as investment management, risk management, compliance and valuation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A situation in which the interests of a manager, its staff, its group or a service provider differ from those of the fund or its investors, or the interests of different investors differ.
concepts.bodyHtml: A situation in which the interests of a manager, its staff, its group or a service provider differ from those of the fund or its investors, or the interests of different investors differ. ManCos and AIFMs must identify, prevent or manage and disclose conflicts, for example by separating functions.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: In tokenisation, one firm or group often sits on several sides of the same token, for example keeping the register, valuing the assets and running the trading venue. Separating these roles structurally is stronger than managing them by policy alone.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules by which the nodes of a network agree on one version of the ledger: which transactions are valid and in what order.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules by which the nodes of a network agree on one version of the ledger: which transactions are valid and in what order. Proof of work and proof of stake are the main types. Whoever can influence consensus can influence the record.

concepts.shortDefinition: Where the national law has a consent regime, a firm that has reported suspicion asks the FIU for consent before dealing with the funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: Where the national law has a consent regime, a firm that has reported suspicion asks the FIU for consent before dealing with the funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Something of value given in exchange for a promise.
concepts.bodyHtml: Something of value given in exchange for a promise. Without consideration a promise is generally not enforceable as a contract unless it is made by deed.

concepts.shortDefinition: An MMF that uses amortised cost accounting to keep the value of its shares at a constant level, such as €1.
concepts.bodyHtml: An MMF that uses amortised cost accounting to keep the value of its shares at a constant level, such as €1. Under the MMFR, only public debt CNAV MMFs may do so for all their assets; such funds must invest at least 99.5% in public debt instruments, reverse repos secured on public debt and cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: The document that establishes a fund and sets out its basic rules, such as its instrument of incorporation or memorandum and articles of association, trust deed, deed of constitution, management regulations or partnership agreement.
concepts.bodyHtml: The document that establishes a fund and sets out its basic rules, such as its instrument of incorporation or memorandum and articles of association, trust deed, deed of constitution, management regulations or partnership agreement. Also called the fund rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The spread of losses or loss of confidence from one firm, token or market to others through exposures, shared collateral or shared sentiment.
concepts.bodyHtml: The spread of losses or loss of confidence from one firm, token or market to others through exposures, shared collateral or shared sentiment.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legally binding agreement: an exchange of promises between two or more parties to do, or refrain from doing, certain things.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legally binding agreement: an exchange of promises between two or more parties to do, or refrain from doing, certain things. A valid contract requires offer, acceptance and consideration, an intention to create legal relations, real consent, capacity, a lawful object and, where required, a particular form. Remedies for breach include damages, specific performance and an injunction.

concepts.shortDefinition: A confirmation issued by the TA after an order has been dealt, showing the number of units or shares, the price and the settlement date.
concepts.bodyHtml: A confirmation issued by the TA after an order has been dealt, showing the number of units or shares, the price and the settlement date.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund constituted under contract law, by a deed of constitution (Ireland) or management regulations (Luxembourg), with no legal personality.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund constituted under contract law, by a deed of constitution (Ireland) or management regulations (Luxembourg), with no legal personality. Investors are co-owners of the assets, and the ManCo and depositary contract on the fund’s behalf.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Luxembourg, an entity that oversees the issuance of dematerialised securities, such as fund units issued on DLT, and the reconciliation of the securities in circulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Luxembourg, an entity that oversees the issuance of dematerialised securities, such as fund units issued on DLT, and the reconciliation of the securities in circulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond that gives its holder the option to convert it into other securities, usually shares of the issuer, at a predetermined conversion price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond that gives its holder the option to convert it into other securities, usually shares of the issuer, at a predetermined conversion price.

concepts.shortDefinition: An event initiated by an issuer that affects its securities, such as a dividend, rights issue, stock split, merger or conversion.
concepts.bodyHtml: An event initiated by an issuer that affects its securities, such as a dividend, rights issue, stock split, merger or conversion. It may be mandatory or voluntary for holders.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund established as a company with its own legal personality, managed by a board of directors and issuing shares to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund established as a company with its own legal personality, managed by a board of directors and issuing shares to investors. It may have variable or fixed capital.

concepts.shortDefinition: The system by which a company is directed and controlled, including the role of its board, management, controls and accountability to shareholders.
concepts.bodyHtml: The system by which a company is directed and controlled, including the role of its board, management, controls and accountability to shareholders. It applies both to funds and their ManCos and, through stewardship, to the companies in which funds invest.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ethereum staking, an additional slashing penalty that grows with the number of validators slashed in the same period, punishing common failures.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ethereum staking, an additional slashing penalty that grows with the number of validators slashed in the same period, punishing common failures.

concepts.shortDefinition: Banks exiting or restricting a whole sector or jurisdiction they see as high risk, rather than managing risk client by client.
concepts.bodyHtml: Banks exiting or restricting a whole sector or jurisdiction they see as high risk, rather than managing risk client by client. Often the first visible cost of a financial crime failure.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that the other party to a transaction, such as an OTC derivative, securities lending or repo agreement, or an unsettled trade, defaults before meeting its obligations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that the other party to a transaction, such as an OTC derivative, securities lending or repo agreement, or an unsettled trade, defaults before meeting its obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: Risk-based checks that a crypto service provider carries out on another provider it transacts with or serves, covering its licence or registration, its AML programme and its customer base, as set out in FATF guidance (2021).
concepts.bodyHtml: Risk-based checks that a crypto service provider carries out on another provider it transacts with or serves, covering its licence or registration, its AML programme and its customer base, as set out in FATF guidance (2021).

concepts.shortDefinition: The interest paid periodically on a bond, at a fixed or floating rate, expressed as a percentage of its face value.
concepts.bodyHtml: The interest paid periodically on a bond, at a fixed or floating rate, expressed as a percentage of its face value.

concepts.shortDefinition: The CBI’s Fund Management Companies Guidance and related rules, issued in December 2016 after a consultation of that number and applying to existing FMCs from 1 July 2018.
concepts.bodyHtml: The CBI’s Fund Management Companies Guidance and related rules, issued in December 2016 after a consultation of that number and applying to existing FMCs from 1 July 2018. It covers delegate oversight, managerial functions and designated persons, organisational effectiveness, directors’ time commitments, record retrievability and the location of directors and designated persons.

concepts.shortDefinition: The large block of ETF shares in which an AP creates or redeems directly with the ETF.
concepts.bodyHtml: The large block of ETF shares in which an AP creates or redeems directly with the ETF. Creation and redemption may be in kind, against a basket of securities, or in cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: An assessment by a credit rating agency of an issuer’s or debt instrument’s creditworthiness.
concepts.bodyHtml: An assessment by a credit rating agency of an issuer’s or debt instrument’s creditworthiness. A downgrade can reduce a bond’s price.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that assesses and rates the creditworthiness of issuers and debt instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that assesses and rates the creditworthiness of issuers and debt instruments. In the EU credit rating agencies are supervised directly by ESMA).

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss because an issuer or borrower fails to pay interest or repay capital when due, or because its creditworthiness deteriorates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss because an issuer or borrower fails to pay interest or repay capital when due, or because its creditworthiness deteriorates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Managing and collecting payments on loans, including collecting interest and principal and dealing with borrowers in difficulty.
concepts.bodyHtml: Managing and collecting payments on loans, including collecting interest and principal and dealing with borrowers in difficulty. Since AIFMD II, AIFMs may service loans as an ancillary activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A document supplementing an ISDA master agreement that governs the collateral exchanged between the parties to OTC derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A document supplementing an ISDA master agreement that governs the collateral exchanged between the parties to OTC derivatives. An English law Credit Support Annex works by title transfer; a New York law one by a security interest.

concepts.shortDefinition: The order in which a liquidator applies an insolvent company’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The order in which a liquidator applies an insolvent company’s assets. Broadly, fixed-charge creditors are paid from their security, the costs of the winding-up and preferential debts are paid before floating-charge holders and unsecured creditors, and members rank last.

concepts.shortDefinition: The liquidation of an insolvent company, which is controlled by its creditors or by the court rather than by its shareholders.
concepts.bodyHtml: The liquidation of an insolvent company, which is controlled by its creditors or by the court rather than by its shareholders.

concepts.shortDefinition: An ICT service provider, such as a large cloud provider, designated under DORA as critical to the EU financial sector and overseen directly by the ESAs.
concepts.bodyHtml: An ICT service provider, such as a large cloud provider, designated under DORA as critical to the EU financial sector and overseen directly by the ESAs.

concepts.shortDefinition: The CBDFD and CBDFR, adopted in 2019 and applying in full since 2 August 2021.
concepts.bodyHtml: The CBDFD and CBDFR, adopted in 2019 and applying in full since 2 August 2021. They harmonise pre-marketing, de-notification, facilities for investors and marketing communications and require national regulators to publish their marketing rules and fees.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment by one sub-fund of an umbrella in another sub-fund of the same umbrella, permitted in Ireland and Luxembourg subject to conditions designed to avoid circular holdings and double charging of fees.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment by one sub-fund of an umbrella in another sub-fund of the same umbrella, permitted in Ireland and Luxembourg subject to conditions designed to avoid circular holdings and double charging of fees. In Luxembourg, the voting rights of the target shares are suspended while held.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ability of a system to switch cryptographic algorithms quickly, for example to post-quantum cryptography.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ability of a system to switch cryptographic algorithms quickly, for example to post-quantum cryptography.

concepts.shortDefinition: A digital representation of value or rights that can be transferred and stored electronically using DLT, such as bitcoin.
concepts.bodyHtml: A digital representation of value or rights that can be transferred and stored electronically using DLT, such as bitcoin. Crypto-assets that are not financial instruments are regulated by MiCA. Fund exposure to them is restricted, particularly for UCITS and retail AIFs.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A digital representation of value or rights that can be transferred and stored electronically using DLT. The term used in MiCA.

concepts.shortDefinition: Crypto-asset service provider: the EU's MiCA term for a firm authorised to provide one or more of ten crypto-asset services, with a passport across the EU.
concepts.bodyHtml: Crypto-asset service provider: the EU's MiCA term for a firm authorised to provide one or more of ten crypto-asset services, with a passport across the EU.

concepts.shortDefinition: A coin minted against crypto worth more than the coins issued, with automatic liquidation if cover falls (for example DAI, now USDS under Sky).
concepts.bodyHtml: A coin minted against crypto worth more than the coins issued, with automatic liquidation if cover falls (for example DAI, now USDS under Sky). It fails if collateral crashes faster than liquidations work, as on 12 March 2020.

concepts.shortDefinition: For a floating charge, its conversion into a fixed charge over the assets the company then holds, triggered by an event such as default.
concepts.bodyHtml: For a floating charge, its conversion into a fixed charge over the assets the company then holds, triggered by an event such as default. For a performance fee, the point at which the fee becomes payable to the manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share class denominated in a currency other than the fund’s base currency that seeks to reduce the effect on its investors of exchange-rate movements between the base currency and the class currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share class denominated in a currency other than the fund’s base currency that seeks to reduce the effect on its investors of exchange-rate movements between the base currency and the class currency. For UCITS, ESMA accepts hedging at share class level only for currency risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: Whether a firm holds or controls the keys on the client's behalf (custodial) or the client holds them alone (non-custodial).
concepts.bodyHtml: Whether a firm holds or controls the keys on the client's behalf (custodial) or the client holds them alone (non-custodial). A provider that keeps a recovery share or a signing veto is custodial in substance for that share.

concepts.shortDefinition: Historically, the party appointed to hold the assets of a corporate fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: Historically, the party appointed to hold the assets of a corporate fund. The term has largely been superseded by “depositary” for regulated funds, but is still used for entities, including sub-custodians, that hold assets in custody.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The firm that safekeeps a fund's assets and, in many funds, oversees the administrator. Where the assets are tokens, it holds or oversees the keys.

concepts.shortDefinition: The holding of financial instruments in safekeeping, in accounts opened in the name of the fund and segregated from the custodian’s own assets so that they are protected if it fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: The holding of financial instruments in safekeeping, in accounts opened in the name of the fund and segregated from the custodian’s own assets so that they are protected if it fails. It is part of the fund depositary’s safekeeping duty.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Holding assets, or the means of accessing them, on behalf of others. For virtual assets, the custodian controls the keys.
sectorNotes.defi: In DeFi, users usually keep their own assets in self-hosted wallets and interact with smart contracts directly. Assets deposited into a protocol are controlled by its code and by whoever holds its admin or upgrade keys, rather than by a custodian.

concepts.shortDefinition: The AML process of identifying and verifying an investor and its beneficial owners, understanding the purpose of the relationship and monitoring it on an ongoing basis.
concepts.bodyHtml: The AML process of identifying and verifying an investor and its beneficial owners, understanding the purpose of the relationship and monitoring it on an ongoing basis. For funds it is usually carried out by the TA or distributor.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Identifying and verifying the customer and its beneficial owners and understanding the relationship (FATF Recommendation 10). Enhanced due diligence adds measures for higher risk, such as evidence of source of funds and wealth. The firm remains responsible, including when it relies on third parties.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets of an MMF that mature, or can be turned into cash, within one working day or one week.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets of an MMF that mature, or can be turned into cash, within one working day or one week. The MMFR sets minimum proportions of between 7.5% and 30%, depending on the type of MMF and asset.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money awarded to the injured party for breach of contract, intended to put it in the position it would have been in had the contract been performed.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money awarded to the injured party for breach of contract, intended to put it in the position it would have been in had the contract been performed. Damages may cover loss of profits, but loss that is too remote is not recoverable and contracts often exclude indirect or consequential loss.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent provider of market data, such as asset prices and corporate action information, used by administrators to value assets and reflect corporate actions.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent provider of market data, such as asset prices and corporate action information, used by administrators to value assets and reflect corporate actions. Also called a pricing service or data service provider.

concepts.shortDefinition: The harmonised procedure for ceasing to market a fund in a host Member State.
concepts.bodyHtml: The harmonised procedure for ceasing to market a fund in a host Member State. The manager must offer to repurchase investors’ units free of charges for at least 30 working days, publicise its intention and end arrangements with intermediaries.

concepts.shortDefinition: The deadline by which orders must reach the transfer agent to be dealt on a given dealing day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The deadline by which orders must reach the transfer agent to be dealt on a given dealing day. Later orders are held over to the next dealing day.

concepts.shortDefinition: A day on which an open-ended fund accepts subscriptions and redemptions, as set out in its prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: A day on which an open-ended fund accepts subscriptions and redemptions, as set out in its prospectus. Orders received before the dealing cut-off are dealt at the price calculated at the next valuation point.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond backed only by the general creditworthiness of the issuing company and so unsecured.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond backed only by the general creditworthiness of the issuing company and so unsecured. UK debentures, by contrast, are generally secured on the issuer’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A contractual obligation of an issuer to repay borrowed money, with interest, to the holder on a set schedule.
concepts.bodyHtml: A contractual obligation of an issuer to repay borrowed money, with interest, to the holder on a set schedule. Examples include bonds, debentures, treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit.

concepts.shortDefinition: A group that governs a protocol through token-holder votes executed on-chain.
concepts.bodyHtml: A group that governs a protocol through token-holder votes executed on-chain. Courts have treated some DAOs as associations or partnerships (Ooki, Lido).

concepts.shortDefinition: A trading protocol that runs on smart contracts, letting users trade from their own wallets without a central operator holding the assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A trading protocol that runs on smart contracts, letting users trade from their own wallets without a central operator holding the assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lending, trading, staking and other services built from smart contracts that anyone can use.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lending, trading, staking and other services built from smart contracts that anyone can use. Control is usually spread across several parties rather than absent.

concepts.shortDefinition: A written document executed with special formalities, such as signing and sealing.
concepts.bodyHtml: A written document executed with special formalities, such as signing and sealing. A promise made by deed is enforceable without consideration, and some contracts must be made by deed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The deed, executed under seal between the ManCo and the fund depositary, that constitutes an Irish CCF and sets out the rights of the co-owners and the duties of the parties.
concepts.bodyHtml: The deed, executed under seal between the ManCo and the fund depositary, that constitutes an Irish CCF and sets out the rights of the co-owners and the duties of the parties.

concepts.shortDefinition: AI-generated video, audio or images that impersonate a real person, used to defeat liveness checks or to instruct payments (Arup, 2024).
concepts.bodyHtml: AI-generated video, audio or images that impersonate a real person, used to defeat liveness checks or to instruct payments (Arup, 2024).

concepts.shortDefinition: The website or app through which users reach a decentralised protocol.
concepts.bodyHtml: The website or app through which users reach a decentralised protocol. Under FATF guidance (2021), a person who runs it and keeps control or sufficient influence, for example through admin keys and fees, may be a virtual asset service provider.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entrusting by a ManCo or fund of the performance of a function or task, such as portfolio management or administration, to a third party.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entrusting by a ManCo or fund of the performance of a function or task, such as portfolio management or administration, to a third party. The delegating entity remains responsible, must have an objective reason for the delegation and must oversee the delegate.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Ethereum feature, introduced in May 2025, that lets an ordinary wallet delegate its behaviour to smart contract code by signing an authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Ethereum feature, introduced in May 2025, that lets an ordinary wallet delegate its behaviour to smart contract code by signing an authorisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Settlement in which the transfer of an asset happens if, and only if, payment is made.
concepts.bodyHtml: Settlement in which the transfer of an asset happens if, and only if, payment is made.

concepts.shortDefinition: When a stablecoin's market price departs from its target value.
concepts.bodyHtml: When a stablecoin's market price departs from its target value.

concepts.shortDefinition: The written contract appointing a fund’s depositary, required under the UCITSD and the AIFMD.
concepts.bodyHtml: The written contract appointing a fund’s depositary, required under the UCITSD and the AIFMD. It sets out the fund depositary’s safekeeping and oversight duties, proper instructions, fees, liability, sub-custodians, termination and conflicts of interest; for unit trusts and contractual funds the trust deed or deed of constitution may specify the duties.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund depositary’s liability for loss of assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund depositary’s liability for loss of assets. Under the UCITSD and the AIFMD it must return an identical financial instrument, or the corresponding amount, without undue delay if one held in custody is lost, unless the loss arose from an external event beyond its reasonable control; an AIF depositary may in specific circumstances discharge liability to a sub-custodian.

concepts.shortDefinition: A financial instrument, such as a future, forward, option or swap, whose value is derived from the price of an underlying asset, index, rate or other reference.
concepts.bodyHtml: A financial instrument, such as a future, forward, option or swap, whose value is derived from the price of an underlying asset, index, rate or other reference. Funds use derivatives for hedging, efficient portfolio management or investment, and they can create leverage.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A contract whose value is derived from an underlying asset, such as a future, option or perpetual swap.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, an individual responsible for overseeing one of the six managerial functions of an FMC under CP86.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, an individual responsible for overseeing one of the six managerial functions of an FMC under CP86. A designated person need not be a director but holds a PCF.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets that exist only in electronic form and are recorded on a distributed ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets that exist only in electronic form and are recorded on a distributed ledger. They include tokenised financial instruments and crypto-assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, applying since 17 January 2025 to UCITS ManCos and AIFMs (but not sub-threshold AIFMs).
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, applying since 17 January 2025 to UCITS ManCos and AIFMs (but not sub-threshold AIFMs). It has five pillars: ICT risk management, ICT incident reporting, digital operational resilience testing, ICT third-party risk (including a register of information and mandatory contract terms) and information sharing.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The EU Digital Operational Resilience Act, applying from 17 January 2025, including to MiCA crypto-asset service providers: ICT risk, incident reporting, testing and third parties.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cryptographic proof, created with a private key, that the holder of the key approved a message or transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cryptographic proof, created with a private key, that the holder of the key approved a message or transaction. It proves control of the key, not identity.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token that mirrors an asset recorded elsewhere, such as an administrator's register or a central securities depository.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token that mirrors an asset recorded elsewhere, such as an administrator's register or a central securities depository. The two records must be reconciled, and the legal documents should say which prevails if they differ.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF that invests in crypto-assets, directly or through derivatives or exchange-traded products.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF that invests in crypto-assets, directly or through derivatives or exchange-traded products. The CBI is highly unlikely to approve a UCITS or RIAIF with any crypto-asset exposure, while a QIAIF may have exposure if its AIFM shows how the risks will be managed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The reduction in the value of existing investors’ holdings caused by the dealing costs that a fund incurs when other investors subscribe or redeem.
concepts.bodyHtml: The reduction in the value of existing investors’ holdings caused by the dealing costs that a fund incurs when other investors subscribe or redeem.

concepts.shortDefinition: Direct exposure is when funds come straight from a high-risk source; indirect exposure is when they pass through intermediaries first.
concepts.bodyHtml: Direct exposure is when funds come straight from a high-risk source; indirect exposure is when they pass through intermediaries first. Blockchain analytics measure both, usually by the number of hops, and firms set how far back they look as part of their risk appetite.

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU legislative act that sets out results Member States must achieve and must be transposed into national law, as with the UCITSD, the AIFMD and MiFID II.
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU legislative act that sets out results Member States must achieve and must be transposed into national law, as with the UCITSD, the AIFMD and MiFID II. An EU regulation, by contrast, applies directly.

concepts.term: Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union
concepts.sortKey: directorate-general for financial stability, financial services and capital markets union

concepts.shortDefinition: Managing a client’s portfolio under a mandate that gives the manager discretion to choose investments without consulting the client on each one.
concepts.bodyHtml: Managing a client’s portfolio under a mandate that gives the manager discretion to choose investments without consulting the client on each one. It is a MiFID II investment service and a channel through which funds are bought.

concepts.shortDefinition: Technology that records transactions in a shared ledger replicated across a network of participants, such as a blockchain.
concepts.bodyHtml: Technology that records transactions in a shared ledger replicated across a network of participants, such as a blockchain. It is used for crypto-assets and tokenised instruments, and fund registers may be kept on it.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Technology that keeps a shared, synchronised record across many participants, rather than in one central database.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract between a fund or its ManCo and a distributor setting out how the distributor will sell the fund, the services and information to be exchanged, commissions, AML and financial crime checks, product governance information and order processing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract between a fund or its ManCo and a distributor setting out how the distributor will sell the fund, the services and information to be exchanged, commissions, AML and financial crime checks, product governance information and order processing. Also called an intermediary agreement.

concepts.shortDefinition: The route by which a fund reaches investors: direct, through advisers, through platforms, through insurance and pension products, institutional, or through discretionary managers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The route by which a fund reaches investors: direct, through advisers, through platforms, through insurance and pension products, institutional, or through discretionary managers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund’s policy on whether, when and from what source it pays income to investors, disclosed in the prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund’s policy on whether, when and from what source it pays income to investors, disclosed in the prospectus. Share classes may be distributing or accumulating.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that the channels through which a fund is sold are compromised or closed, cutting off an important source of new investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that the channels through which a fund is sold are compromised or closed, cutting off an important source of new investment.

concepts.shortDefinition: An intermediary that sells a fund’s units or shares to investors, usually under a distribution agreement, and may also carry out marketing and AML checks.
concepts.bodyHtml: An intermediary that sells a fund’s units or shares to investors, usually under a distribution agreement, and may also carry out marketing and AML checks.

concepts.shortDefinition: Spreading a portfolio across assets whose prices do not all move together, so that the fall in value of any one asset has a limited effect on the whole.
concepts.bodyHtml: Spreading a portfolio across assets whose prices do not all move together, so that the fall in value of any one asset has a limited effect on the whole. Funds sold to retail investors are subject to regulatory diversification requirements and concentration limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2022/858, applying since 23 March 2023, which allows market infrastructures to trade and settle tokenised financial instruments, including UCITS units, using DLT under certain exemptions.
