concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2022/858, applying since 23 March 2023, which allows market infrastructures to trade and settle tokenised financial instruments, including UCITS units, using DLT under certain exemptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle that an investment contributing to one sustainability objective must not significantly harm any other.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle that an investment contributing to one sustainability objective must not significantly harm any other. It is a condition both for an SFDR sustainable investment and for Taxonomy alignment).

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk arising from failures in the due diligence documentation investors must provide to access a fund, which can cause legal, regulatory and reputational damage.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk arising from failures in the due diligence documentation investors must provide to access a fund, which can cause legal, regulatory and reputational damage.

concepts.shortDefinition: The jurisdiction in which a fund is established and authorised.
concepts.bodyHtml: The jurisdiction in which a fund is established and authorised. It determines the legal forms available, the fund’s home regulator and the national rules that apply.

concepts.shortDefinition: Spending the same digital money twice.
concepts.bodyHtml: Spending the same digital money twice. Blockchains solve this through consensus on a single history.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fall in value from a peak to a trough.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fall in value from a peak to a trough. Crypto-assets have seen deep drawdowns; bitcoin fell about 77% from its November 2021 peak to its 2022 low.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dealing at a higher subscription (offer) price and a lower redemption (bid) price, reflecting the cost of buying and selling assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dealing at a higher subscription (offer) price and a lower redemption (bid) price, reflecting the cost of buying and selling assets. It is also an anti-dilution LMT.

concepts.shortDefinition: A careful investigation carried out before entering into, and while maintaining, a relationship – for example by a ManCo before appointing and while overseeing a delegate, by an investor before investing, or by a TA or distributor on an investor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A careful investigation carried out before entering into, and while maintaining, a relationship – for example by a ManCo before appointing and while overseeing a delegate, by an investor before investing, or by a TA or distributor on an investor.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiCA, a crypto-asset that aims to keep a stable value by referencing one official currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiCA, a crypto-asset that aims to keep a stable value by referencing one official currency. Must be issued by a credit institution or e-money institution.

concepts.shortDefinition: A yield product in which customers' assets are lent or staked to generate a return.
concepts.bodyHtml: A yield product in which customers' assets are lent or staked to generate a return. The customer becomes a lender to borrowers they may not know (Gemini Earn and Genesis).

concepts.shortDefinition: The part of a FATF-style mutual evaluation that tests whether a country's anti-money-laundering system works in practice, rated across a set of Immediate Outcomes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The part of a FATF-style mutual evaluation that tests whether a country's anti-money-laundering system works in practice, rated across a set of Immediate Outcomes. A country can be placed under increased monitoring for weak effectiveness even when its laws score well on technical compliance.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the UCITS rules, techniques such as securities lending, repo and certain uses of derivatives that are used to reduce risk or cost, or to generate additional income with an appropriate level of risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the UCITS rules, techniques such as securities lending, repo and certain uses of derivatives that are used to reduce risk or cost, or to generate additional income with an appropriate level of risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, a retail client who asks to be treated as a professional client and whom the firm assesses as meeting set criteria of expertise, experience and knowledge.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, a retail client who asks to be treated as a professional client and whom the firm assesses as meeting set criteria of expertise, experience and knowledge. Such a client receives less protection.

concepts.shortDefinition: The categories of asset in which a UCITS may invest: transferable securities, money market instruments, units of other funds, deposits and financial derivative instruments, subject to diversification and concentration limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The categories of asset in which a UCITS may invest: transferable securities, money market instruments, units of other funds, deposits and financial derivative instruments, subject to diversification and concentration limits. UCITS may not invest in real estate or commodities.

concepts.shortDefinition: Commission Directive 2007/16/EC, which clarifies which assets a UCITS may hold.
concepts.bodyHtml: Commission Directive 2007/16/EC, which clarifies which assets a UCITS may hold. The Commission is reviewing it following ESMA technical advice; any change would need new EU legislation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, the category of client, such as banks and investment firms, that receives the least regulatory protection.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, the category of client, such as banks and investment firms, that receives the least regulatory protection.

concepts.shortDefinition: A copy of a wallet's key stored with the app provider in encrypted form, unlocked only on the user's device with their password.
concepts.bodyHtml: A copy of a wallet's key stored with the app provider in encrypted form, unlocked only on the user's device with their password. If the provider can decrypt or reset it, the provider has control.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reserves pledged, lent or used as collateral.
concepts.bodyHtml: Reserves pledged, lent or used as collateral. Encumbered reserves may not be available to holders, so the main regimes limit pledging and reuse.

concepts.shortDefinition: The steps a secured creditor takes to recover a debt from the secured asset, such as retaining it (lien), selling it (mortgage of shares) or appointing a receiver (charge over land or a floating charge).
concepts.bodyHtml: The steps a secured creditor takes to recover a debt from the secured asset, such as retaining it (lien), selling it (mortgage of shares) or appointing a receiver (charge over land or a floating charge).

concepts.shortDefinition: A policy, required of asset managers under SRD II on a comply-or-explain basis, describing how they monitor and engage with investee companies, exercise voting rights and manage related conflicts, with an annual report on how it was applied.
concepts.bodyHtml: A policy, required of asset managers under SRD II on a comply-or-explain basis, describing how they monitor and engage with investee companies, exercise voting rights and manage related conflicts, with an annual report on how it was applied.

concepts.shortDefinition: Additional checks applied to higher-risk customers or transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Additional checks applied to higher-risk customers or transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The amount of true randomness behind a cryptographic key, measured in bits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The amount of true randomness behind a cryptographic key, measured in bits. A key with 128 bits of entropy is beyond any brute-force search; weak random number generation has led to stolen funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A one-off charge paid by an investor on subscribing to a fund, often waived or discounted by distributors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A one-off charge paid by an investor on subscribing to a fund, often waived or discounted by distributors. Also called an initial or subscription charge.

concepts.shortDefinition: The three groups of non-financial factors, such as climate impact, labour practices and board quality, that investors consider in assessing companies and that sustainable funds take into account.
concepts.bodyHtml: The three groups of non-financial factors, such as climate impact, labour practices and board quality, that investors consider in assessing companies and that sustainable funds take into account.

concepts.shortDefinition: A mortgage under which the borrower remains the legal owner of the asset, such as shares, while the lender takes the beneficial interest, often holding signed but undated transfer forms so that it can take legal title on enforcement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A mortgage under which the borrower remains the legal owner of the asset, such as shares, while the lender takes the beneficial interest, often holding signed but undated transfer forms so that it can take legal title on enforcement.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share representing part-ownership of a company and entitling the holder to share in its profits, usually through dividends, and often to vote at general meetings.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share representing part-ownership of a company and entitling the holder to share in its profits, usually through dividends, and often to vote at general meetings. Ordinary shares and preferred stock are the most common types.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests mainly in shares (equities).
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests mainly in shares (equities).

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a debtor who has given a mortgage to recover the asset free of the security by repaying the debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a debtor who has given a mortgage to recover the asset free of the security by repaying the debt.

concepts.shortDefinition: The basic Ethereum fungible-token standard; anyone can send to anyone.
concepts.bodyHtml: The basic Ethereum fungible-token standard; anyone can send to anyone. Unsuitable on its own for a regulated security.

concepts.shortDefinition: A permissioned token standard linking holders to an on-chain identity registry.
concepts.bodyHtml: A permissioned token standard linking holders to an on-chain identity registry. An agent can freeze, force transfers, recover wallets, pause, mint and burn.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that integrates environmental, social and governance factors into its investment decisions, typically one that promotes environmental or social characteristics (Article 8) or has a sustainable investment objective (Article 9).
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that integrates environmental, social and governance factors into its investment decisions, typically one that promotes environmental or social characteristics (Article 8) or has a sustainable investment objective (Article 9). Its name is subject to ESMA’s fund names guidelines.

concepts.shortDefinition: The native coin of the Ethereum network, used to pay fees and to stake.
concepts.bodyHtml: The native coin of the Ethereum network, used to pay fees and to stake.
concepts.notes: the unit of the Ethereum network

concepts.shortDefinition: A programmable blockchain launched in 2015 that runs smart contracts.
concepts.bodyHtml: A programmable blockchain launched in 2015 that runs smart contracts. It moved from proof of work to proof of stake in September 2022.

concepts.notes: a token standard, such as ERC-20

concepts.shortDefinition: The wallet each EU Member State must offer under eIDAS 2.
concepts.bodyHtml: The wallet each EU Member State must offer under eIDAS 2. EU clients will present it; firms outside the EU must assess any reliance on it like any third-party reliance.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European Commission's list of third countries with strategic deficiencies in their anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing regimes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The European Commission's list of third countries with strategic deficiencies in their anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing regimes. EU firms must apply enhanced due diligence to business relationships and transactions involving these countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF authorised under one of the EU fund regulations – ELTIF, EuVECA or EuSEF – with requirements tailored to its strategy and the right to be marketed across the EEA under a passport.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF authorised under one of the EU fund regulations – ELTIF, EuVECA or EuSEF – with requirements tailored to its strategy and the right to be marketed across the EEA under a passport. Also called a designated AIF.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU classification, under the Taxonomy Regulation, of economic activities that are environmentally sustainable: those that contribute substantially to at least one of six environmental objectives, do no significant harm (DNSH) to the others and meet minimum social safeguards.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU classification, under the Taxonomy Regulation, of economic activities that are environmentally sustainable: those that contribute substantially to at least one of six environmental objectives, do no significant harm (DNSH) to the others and meet minimum social safeguards. Article 8 and 9 funds disclose their Taxonomy alignment.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond issued in a currency other than that of the country or market in which it is issued, usually sold to investors in several countries at once.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond issued in a currency other than that of the country or market in which it is issued, usually sold to investors in several countries at once.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standard data template through which fund managers give distributors the sustainability information they need for product governance, suitability and their own disclosures).
concepts.bodyHtml: A standard data template through which fund managers give distributors the sustainability information they need for product governance, suitability and their own disclosures).

concepts.term: European Fund and Asset Management Association
concepts.sortKey: european fund and asset management association

concepts.term: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
concepts.sortKey: european insurance and occupational pensions authority

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU labelled AIF, managed by an authorised EEA AIFM, that invests at least 55% of its capital in long-term assets such as infrastructure, unlisted companies and real assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU labelled AIF, managed by an authorised EEA AIFM, that invests at least 55% of its capital in long-term assets such as infrastructure, unlisted companies and real assets. Since ELTIF 2.0 it can be marketed more easily to retail investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, the EU response to the G20 commitment on OTC derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, the EU response to the G20 commitment on OTC derivatives. It requires central clearing of certain OTC derivatives, risk mitigation (including margin) for non-cleared ones, reporting to trade repositories and requirements for CCPs; it has been amended by EMIR Refit, EMIR 2.2 and EMIR 3.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standard data template through which fund managers give distributors the information they need under MiFID II, including the target market and costs and charges.
concepts.bodyHtml: A standard data template through which fund managers give distributors the information they need under MiFID II, including the target market and costs and charges.

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU labelled AIF that invests at least 70% of its capital in social undertakings achieving measurable, positive social impacts.
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU labelled AIF that invests at least 70% of its capital in social undertakings achieving measurable, positive social impacts.

concepts.shortDefinition: The three EU supervisory authorities – ESMA, the European Banking Authority and the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority – which work together through a Joint Committee on cross-sector matters such as the PRIIPs KID, SFDR and DORA).
concepts.bodyHtml: The three EU supervisory authorities – ESMA, the European Banking Authority and the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority – which work together through a Joint Committee on cross-sector matters such as the PRIIPs KID, SFDR and DORA).

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU labelled AIF that invests at least 70% of its capital in qualifying portfolio undertakings, mainly unlisted start-ups and small and medium-sized companies.
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU labelled AIF that invests at least 70% of its capital in qualifying portfolio undertakings, mainly unlisted start-ups and small and medium-sized companies.

concepts.shortDefinition: A private equity-type fund that accepts subscriptions over time rather than raising all its capital at launch.
concepts.bodyHtml: A private equity-type fund that accepts subscriptions over time rather than raising all its capital at launch.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish court process under Part 10 of the Companies Act 2014 that protects an insolvent company with a reasonable prospect of survival from its creditors while an examiner prepares a scheme of arrangement.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish court process under Part 10 of the Companies Act 2014 that protects an insolvent company with a reasonable prospect of survival from its creditors while an examiner prepares a scheme of arrangement.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token issued by a trading platform, giving fee discounts or other benefits (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token issued by a trading platform, giving fee discounts or other benefits (e.g. BNB, OKB). Conflicts are built in: the issuer lists, prices and may lend against it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange or other trading venue throughout the day at a market price.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange or other trading venue throughout the day at a market price. Arbitrage by authorised participants keeps its market price close to the value of its assets. Nearly all EEA ETFs are UCITS and must include “UCITS ETF” in their name.

concepts.shortDefinition: A debt security traded on an exchange whose return is linked to an index or other reference asset.
concepts.bodyHtml: A debt security traded on an exchange whose return is linked to an index or other reference asset. ESMA has advised a look-through test so that a UCITS cannot use such instruments to gain significant exposure to assets it could not hold directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: A listed security, such as an exchange-traded fund, that gives exposure to an asset such as bitcoin without the investor holding it directly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A listed security, such as an exchange-traded fund, that gives exposure to an asset such as bitcoin without the investor holding it directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: Binding restrictions that prevent a fund investing in certain sectors, companies or activities, such as controversial weapons or fossil fuels.
concepts.bodyHtml: Binding restrictions that prevent a fund investing in certain sectors, companies or activities, such as controversial weapons or fossil fuels. Funds with ESG terms in their names must apply set exclusions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A sale of a fund made at the client’s initiative without investment advice.
concepts.bodyHtml: A sale of a fund made at the client’s initiative without investment advice. Under MiFID II only non-complex products, such as most UCITS, may be sold this way without assessing the client.

concepts.shortDefinition: A one-off charge paid by an investor on redeeming from a fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A one-off charge paid by an investor on redeeming from a fund. Also called a redemption charge; it differs from a redemption fee LMT, which is paid into the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A documented plan for ending an outsourcing or ICT arrangement and moving the service to another provider or in-house without disruption.
concepts.bodyHtml: A documented plan for ending an outsourcing or ICT arrangement and moving the service to another provider or in-house without disruption. Regulators expect workable exit plans and DORA requires exit strategies for critical or important functions.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ethereum staking, the queue validators join to stop validating and withdraw.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ethereum staking, the queue validators join to stop validating and withdraw. It can take days or weeks when many leave at once.

concepts.shortDefinition: A quantitative LMT that requires investors to give longer notice before redeeming than normally applies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A quantitative LMT that requires investors to give longer notice before redeeming than normally applies.

concepts.shortDefinition: The independent accountant appointed to give an opinion to investors on whether a fund’s financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with the applicable accounting standards and law.
concepts.bodyHtml: The independent accountant appointed to give an opinion to investors on whether a fund’s financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with the applicable accounting standards and law.

concepts.shortDefinition: Support from a sponsor or other third party to guarantee an MMF’s liquidity or stabilise its NAV, such as buying its assets at above market value.
concepts.bodyHtml: Support from a sponsor or other third party to guarantee an MMF’s liquidity or stabilise its NAV, such as buying its assets at above market value. The MMFR prohibits it.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent party appointed to value assets for which a reliable market price is not readily available, such as real estate or unlisted holdings, as an input to the NAV.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent party appointed to value assets for which a reliable market price is not readily available, such as real estate or unlisted holdings, as an input to the NAV. The AIFMD sets requirements on its independence, registration and liability.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that has appointed a separate ManCo (a UCITS ManCo or an AIFM).
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that has appointed a separate ManCo (a UCITS ManCo or an AIFM). Unit trusts and contractual funds must always be externally managed.

concepts.shortDefinition: A party that provides facilities to investors in a host Member State, for example to process orders and provide information.
concepts.bodyHtml: A party that provides facilities to investors in a host Member State, for example to process orders and provide information. Since the CBDF package these facilities may be provided electronically, without a physical presence.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short, regularly updated marketing document summarising a fund’s objective, performance, main holdings and charges.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short, regularly updated marketing document summarising a fund’s objective, performance, main holdings and charges. It is a marketing communication.

concepts.shortDefinition: Many senders funding one account, or one account sending to many wallets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Many senders funding one account, or one account sending to many wallets. Typical of money mules and layering.

concepts.shortDefinition: The five activities that make a person a VASP when done as a business for or on behalf of another: exchange VA–fiat, exchange VA–VA, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services for an issuer's offer or sale.
concepts.bodyHtml: The five activities that make a person a VASP when done as a business for or on behalf of another: exchange VA–fiat, exchange VA–VA, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services for an issuer's offer or sale.

concepts.shortDefinition: The FATF's list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring, often called the "grey list".
concepts.bodyHtml: The FATF's list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring, often called the "grey list". It covers jurisdictions that have committed to fix strategic deficiencies in their anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist financing regimes within agreed timeframes, under an action plan.

concepts.shortDefinition: The FATF standard on new technologies, extended to virtual assets in 2018–19: VASPs must be licensed or registered, supervised and apply the full AML/CFT preventive measures (Interpretive Note, June 2019).
concepts.bodyHtml: The FATF standard on new technologies, extended to virtual assets in 2018–19: VASPs must be licensed or registered, supervised and apply the full AML/CFT preventive measures (Interpretive Note, June 2019).

concepts.shortDefinition: FATF's September 2020 list of warning signs for virtual assets, grouped by transaction size and patterns, anonymity, senders and recipients, source of funds and geography.
concepts.bodyHtml: FATF's September 2020 list of warning signs for virtual assets, grouped by transaction size and patterns, anonymity, senders and recipients, source of funds and geography.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Luxembourg contractual fund: an undivided co-ownership of assets managed by a ManCo or AIFM under management regulations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Luxembourg contractual fund: an undivided co-ownership of assets managed by a ManCo or AIFM under management regulations. It has no legal personality, so it cannot be self-managed. It can be a UCITS, a Part II fund, a SIF or a RAIF.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests at least 85% of its assets in a master fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests at least 85% of its assets in a master fund. A feeder UCITS must invest in a master UCITS; a feeder AIF invests in one master AIF, or several with identical strategies.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund of funds that invests only in funds managed by its own manager or group.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund of funds that invests only in funds managed by its own manager or group. An unfettered fund of funds may also, or only, invest in third-party funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A coin backed by cash, deposits and short-dated government debt, which the issuer promises to redeem at par (for example USDT, USDC, EURC).
concepts.bodyHtml: A coin backed by cash, deposits and short-dated government debt, which the issuer promises to redeem at par (for example USDT, USDC, EURC). The great majority of the market.

concepts.shortDefinition: The holding of property for the benefit of others, as a trustee, depositary or nominee does.
concepts.bodyHtml: The holding of property for the benefit of others, as a trustee, depositary or nominee does. A liquidator cannot use property held in a fiduciary capacity to pay the holder’s own creditors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Luxembourg fiduciary arrangement, under the Law of 27 July 2003, under which a fiduciary holds assets as a separate estate for the benefit of another.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Luxembourg fiduciary arrangement, under the Law of 27 July 2003, under which a fiduciary holds assets as a separate estate for the benefit of another. It performs a similar role to a trust in a civil law system.

concepts.shortDefinition: The duty of a person acting for others, such as a ManCo or investment manager, to act in their best interests, with loyalty and care.
concepts.bodyHtml: The duty of a person acting for others, such as a ManCo or investment manager, to act in their best interests, with loyalty and care.

concepts.shortDefinition: The point after which a blockchain transaction cannot realistically be reversed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The point after which a blockchain transaction cannot realistically be reversed. Bitcoin's finality is probabilistic; Ethereum finalises checkpoints after about two epochs (roughly 13 minutes). Technical finality is not the same as legal settlement finality.

concepts.shortDefinition: An intermediary that gives investors advice or recommendations on investments, including which funds to buy.
concepts.bodyHtml: An intermediary that gives investors advice or recommendations on investments, including which funds to buy. Under MiFID II it must assess suitability and comply with the inducement rules.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive that reduces the formalities for creating and enforcing collateral arrangements over cash and financial instruments, implemented in Ireland by S.I.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive that reduces the formalities for creating and enforcing collateral arrangements over cash and financial instruments, implemented in Ireland by S.I. No. 1 of 2004 and in Luxembourg by the Law of 5 August 2005.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, an instrument such as a transferable security, money market instrument, unit in a collective investment undertaking, derivative or emission allowance.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, an instrument such as a transferable security, money market instrument, unit in a collective investment undertaking, derivative or emission allowance. The definition is technology-neutral and includes instruments issued using DLT.

concepts.shortDefinition: The national agency that receives and analyses suspicious activity reports and passes intelligence to law enforcement.
concepts.bodyHtml: The national agency that receives and analyses suspicious activity reports and passes intelligence to law enforcement. Firms that know or suspect money laundering or terrorist financing must report promptly and must not tip off the customer.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under SFDR, a firm subject to its disclosure rules, including UCITS ManCos and AIFMs (see Annex (vii)).
concepts.bodyHtml: Under SFDR, a firm subject to its disclosure rules, including UCITS ManCos and AIFMs (see Annex (vii)).

concepts.shortDefinition: Financial Stability Board.
concepts.bodyHtml: Financial Stability Board. Its July 2023 framework covers crypto-asset activities and global stablecoin arrangements; its October 2025 peer review found implementation uneven, creating room for regulatory arbitrage.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund’s accounts, comprising the annual statements, which must be audited, and half-yearly statements.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund’s accounts, comprising the annual statements, which must be audited, and half-yearly statements. They are the responsibility of the board or ManCo and are usually prepared by the fund administrator.

concepts.shortDefinition: The first NIST post-quantum standards (August 2024): ML-KEM for key exchange; ML-DSA and SLH-DSA for signatures.
concepts.bodyHtml: The first NIST post-quantum standards (August 2024): ML-KEM for key exchange; ML-DSA and SLH-DSA for signatures.

concepts.shortDefinition: Software built into a hardware device, such as a hardware wallet.
concepts.bodyHtml: Software built into a hardware device, such as a hardware wallet. Every firmware update can change the device's security, so updates need verification before use.

concepts.shortDefinition: The test that controllers, directors and key persons have integrity, competence and financial standing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The test that controllers, directors and key persons have integrity, competence and financial standing. In a VASP it is also a financial crime control.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standards that individuals in senior roles at regulated firms and funds must meet: competence and capability, honesty, ethics and integrity, and financial soundness.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standards that individuals in senior roles at regulated firms and funds must meet: competence and capability, honesty, ethics and integrity, and financial soundness. In Ireland, holders of PCFs need prior CBI approval; in Luxembourg, the CSSF approves directors and conducting officers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund with a fixed share capital, whose shares are bought and sold between investors after launch and may trade at a premium or discount to NAV.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund with a fixed share capital, whose shares are bought and sold between investors after launch and may trade at a premium or discount to NAV. The Luxembourg SICAF is an example. A SICAF can legally be a UCITS, although in practice the CSSF has not authorised any.

concepts.shortDefinition: A charge over specific identified assets, which the debtor cannot sell without the creditor’s consent.
concepts.bodyHtml: A charge over specific identified assets, which the debtor cannot sell without the creditor’s consent.

concepts.shortDefinition: The asset class of debt instruments, such as deposits, bonds and money market instruments, that pay a set or determinable income.
concepts.bodyHtml: The asset class of debt instruments, such as deposits, bonds and money market instruments, that pay a set or determinable income. A fixed income (bond) fund invests mainly in them.

concepts.shortDefinition: An uncollateralised loan that is borrowed and repaid within a single transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: An uncollateralised loan that is borrowed and repaid within a single transaction. Often used in DeFi exploits to manipulate prices.

concepts.shortDefinition: A charge over a changing class of a company’s assets, such as stock, which the company may deal with in the ordinary course of business until an event causes the charge to crystallise into a fixed charge over the assets then held.
concepts.bodyHtml: A charge over a changing class of a company’s assets, such as stock, which the company may deal with in the ordinary course of business until an event causes the charge to crystallise into a fixed charge over the assets then held.

concepts.term: For or on behalf of another
concepts.shortDefinition: FATF's qualifier: only services provided to other people are VASP activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: FATF's qualifier: only services provided to other people are VASP activity. Own-account trading or validation is generally outside, though other regimes may still apply.
concepts.sortKey: for or on behalf of another

concepts.shortDefinition: Moving tokens without the holder's signature, for example after a court order, death, insolvency or theft.
concepts.bodyHtml: Moving tokens without the holder's signature, for example after a court order, death, insolvency or theft. It needs a legal basis in the documents, approval and a log.

concepts.shortDefinition: Government limits on foreign investors buying the securities of domestic companies, such as caps on the proportion of a company’s equity that overseas investors may hold.
concepts.bodyHtml: Government limits on foreign investors buying the securities of domestic companies, such as caps on the proportion of a company’s equity that overseas investors may hold.

concepts.shortDefinition: A change to a blockchain's rules.
concepts.bodyHtml: A change to a blockchain's rules. A soft fork is backward-compatible; a hard fork is not and can split the chain into two.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bilateral OTC contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, tailored to the needs of the parties.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bilateral OTC contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, tailored to the needs of the parties. Funds commonly use currency forwards for hedging.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dealing at the price calculated at the next valuation point after an order is received, so that the price is not known when the order is placed.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dealing at the price calculated at the next valuation point after an order is received, so that the price is not known when the order is placed. It prevents investors trading on out-of-date prices.

concepts.shortDefinition: Stopping a wallet, or the whole token, from transacting: a sanctions and court-order tool.
concepts.bodyHtml: Stopping a wallet, or the whole token, from transacting: a sanctions and court-order tool. Only useful if the right person can use it quickly and lawfully.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract function that lets the issuer stop an address from moving tokens.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract function that lets the issuer stop an address from moving tokens. It is both a financial crime control and a custody risk, so issuers and custodians need a written policy on when and how it is used.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ending of a contract because, without the fault of either party, it has become impossible to perform, for example because its subject matter has been destroyed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ending of a contract because, without the fault of either party, it has become impossible to perform, for example because its subject matter has been destroyed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK's regime bringing cryptoasset activities within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK's regime bringing cryptoasset activities within the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026. It creates new regulated activities, such as operating a cryptoasset trading platform, dealing, arranging, safeguarding, staking and issuing qualifying stablecoins, which require FCA authorisation. The regime fully commences on 25 October 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: A node that checks every block and transaction against the network's rules itself.
concepts.bodyHtml: A node that checks every block and transaction against the network's rules itself. Running a full node is the strongest way for a firm to verify its own deposits and balances.

concepts.shortDefinition: A regulated activity that a ManCo must perform for the funds it manages: investment management (portfolio and risk management), administration and marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: A regulated activity that a ManCo must perform for the funds it manages: investment management (portfolio and risk management), administration and marketing. The tasks making up a function may be delegated, but the ManCo remains responsible.

concepts.shortDefinition: Maintaining a fund’s books and records, including its list of investments, cash, income, fees and expense accruals, so that the NAV can be calculated and financial statements prepared.
concepts.bodyHtml: Maintaining a fund’s books and records, including its list of investments, cash, income, fees and expense accruals, so that the NAV can be calculated and financial statements prepared. It is a core fund administration activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The activities that support the ongoing operation of a fund, including fund accounting, valuation and pricing, maintaining the investor register, processing issues and redemptions, distributing income, compliance monitoring and record keeping.
concepts.bodyHtml: The activities that support the ongoing operation of a fund, including fund accounting, valuation and pricing, maintaining the investor register, processing issues and redemptions, distributing income, compliance monitoring and record keeping.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract appointing a fund administrator, describing its services, such as NAV calculation, fee calculation, financial statements, assistance with the audit, regulatory filings and, often, TA services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract appointing a fund administrator, describing its services, such as NAV calculation, fee calculation, financial statements, assistance with the audit, regulatory filings and, often, TA services.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity, usually appointed by the ManCo, that performs fund administration, in particular calculating the NAV, keeping the fund’s accounts and often acting as transfer agent.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity, usually appointed by the ManCo, that performs fund administration, in particular calculating the NAV, keeping the fund’s accounts and often acting as transfer agent. In Ireland administrators are authorised by the CBI under the IIA; in Luxembourg their activities are governed by CSSF Circular 22/811.

concepts.shortDefinition: The independent entity, usually a bank or specialist trust company, appointed to safekeep a fund’s assets and to oversee the fund’s operation, including subscriptions and redemptions, NAV calculation, cash flows and compliance with investment limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The independent entity, usually a bank or specialist trust company, appointed to safekeep a fund’s assets and to oversee the fund’s operation, including subscriptions and redemptions, NAV calculation, cash flows and compliance with investment limits. Every UCITS, and every AIF managed by an authorised AIFM, must appoint one. The term has largely superseded “custodian” and “trustee”.

concepts.shortDefinition: A unit or share in a regulated fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A unit or share in a regulated fund. A token that simply represents one is regulated as a fund interest under fund rules, not as a virtual asset.

concepts.shortDefinition: The stages of a fund’s life: its design and establishment, its distribution to investors, its management, investment and administration, and its termination and winding up.
concepts.bodyHtml: The stages of a fund’s life: its design and establishment, its distribution to investors, its management, investment and administration, and its termination and winding up.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, the collective term for UCITS ManCos, AIFMs and self-managed investment companies to which the CBI’s CP86 framework applies.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, the collective term for UCITS ManCos, AIFMs and self-managed investment companies to which the CBI’s CP86 framework applies.

concepts.shortDefinition: The combination of two or more funds, in which the assets of one or more merging funds are transferred to a receiving fund and investors receive units in it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The combination of two or more funds, in which the assets of one or more merging funds are transferred to a receiving fund and investors receive units in it. UCITS mergers require prior authorisation and at least 30 days’ information to investors; AIF mergers are governed by national law.

concepts.shortDefinition: ESMA’s Guidelines on funds’ names using ESG or sustainability-related terms, which apply from 21 November 2024 for new funds and 21 May 2025 for existing funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: ESMA’s Guidelines on funds’ names using ESG or sustainability-related terms, which apply from 21 November 2024 for new funds and 21 May 2025 for existing funds. A fund using such terms must invest at least 80% of its assets in line with its characteristics or objectives and apply PAB or CTB exclusions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests principally in other funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests principally in other funds. It may be “fettered” (investing only in funds of its own manager or group) or “unfettered” (investing also or only in third-party funds). Investors may bear fees at both levels.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm, usually an asset management group, that initiates a fund, designs its strategy and markets it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm, usually an asset management group, that initiates a fund, designs its strategy and markets it. It typically sets up or appoints the ManCo and acts as, or appoints, the investment manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: The periodic payment between long and short positions on perpetual futures.
concepts.bodyHtml: The periodic payment between long and short positions on perpetual futures. It provides a synthetic dollar's yield — and becomes a cost when it turns negative.

concepts.shortDefinition: Interchangeable, unit for unit, like coins or shares of the same class.
concepts.bodyHtml: Interchangeable, unit for unit, like coins or shares of the same class. NFTs are non-fungible.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standardised, exchange-traded contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, with margin exchanged through a CCP.
concepts.bodyHtml: A standardised, exchange-traded contract to buy or sell an asset at an agreed price on a future date, with margin exchanged through a CCP.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fee paid to process a transaction or run a smart contract on Ethereum and similar networks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fee paid to process a transaction or run a smart contract on Ethereum and similar networks.

concepts.shortDefinition: The partner that manages a limited partnership and has unlimited liability for its debts.
concepts.bodyHtml: The partner that manages a limited partnership and has unlimited liability for its debts. In a fund LP it usually appoints an external AIFM.

concepts.shortDefinition: The exposure of a UCITS arising from its use of derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: The exposure of a UCITS arising from its use of derivatives. Under the commitment approach, which converts derivative positions into the equivalent position in the underlying assets, it may not exceed 100% of NAV; alternatively it is measured using a value-at-risk approach.

concepts.shortDefinition: The addition by a Member State of national requirements on top of those in EU legislation, for example on fund marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The addition by a Member State of national requirements on top of those in EU legislation, for example on fund marketing. The Commission’s Market Integration and Supervision proposals would stop host Member States doing so.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token that gives its holders votes on changes to a protocol.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token that gives its holders votes on changes to a protocol. Concentrated holdings can let a few holders control it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond issued by a national government, such as an Irish government bond.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bond issued by a national government, such as an Irish government bond. Governments also issue short-term bills. Also called a sovereign bond.

concepts.shortDefinition: The practice of deliberately understating or ceasing to disclose the sustainability features of products – for example, reclassifying Article 9 funds as Article 8 or removing ESG terms from fund names – to reduce regulatory, legal or reputational risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: The practice of deliberately understating or ceasing to disclose the sustainability features of products – for example, reclassifying Article 9 funds as Article 8 or removing ESG terms from fund names – to reduce regulatory, legal or reputational risk. It deprives investors of information and is the opposite risk to greenwashing. Also called greenhushing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Sustainability-related statements, declarations, actions or communications that do not clearly and fairly reflect the underlying sustainability profile of an entity or product, and that may mislead investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: Sustainability-related statements, declarations, actions or communications that do not clearly and fairly reflect the underlying sustainability profile of an entity or product, and that may mislead investors. It is a supervisory priority for the CBI, the CSSF and ESMA).

concepts.shortDefinition: A method of calculating an AIF’s leverage that adds together the absolute values of all its positions, without netting or hedging.
concepts.bodyHtml: A method of calculating an AIF’s leverage that adds together the absolute values of all its positions, without netting or hedging. AIFMs must calculate leverage under both the gross and the commitment methods.

concepts.shortDefinition: A quantum algorithm that speeds up brute-force search.
concepts.bodyHtml: A quantum algorithm that speeds up brute-force search. It weakens hashes and symmetric keys, but 256-bit versions remain strong.

concepts.term: Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act 2025
concepts.shortDefinition: The US federal stablecoin law, signed 18 July 2025 and effective by 18 January 2027 at the latest.
concepts.bodyHtml: The US federal stablecoin law, signed 18 July 2025 and effective by 18 January 2027 at the latest. It requires 1:1 reserves, monthly reserve examination and bans issuer interest; issuers are Bank Secrecy Act financial institutions.
concepts.sortKey: guiding and establishing national innovation for us stablecoins act 2025

concepts.shortDefinition: The discount applied to an asset's market value when it is used as collateral or counted towards capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: The discount applied to an asset's market value when it is used as collateral or counted towards capital. Haircuts can be set by models or from historical price falls.

concepts.shortDefinition: The scheduled halving of the new bitcoin issued to miners, about every four years (most recently April 2024).
concepts.bodyHtml: The scheduled halving of the new bitcoin issued to miners, about every four years (most recently April 2024). Supply is capped at 21 million.

concepts.shortDefinition: Certified tamper-resistant hardware, usually in a data centre, that stores keys and signs.
concepts.bodyHtml: Certified tamper-resistant hardware, usually in a data centre, that stores keys and signs. The control point becomes whoever administers the HSM.

concepts.shortDefinition: A small physical device that stores private keys offline and signs transactions on the device.
concepts.bodyHtml: A small physical device that stores private keys offline and signs transactions on the device.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recording encrypted data today in order to decrypt it once a quantum computer exists.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recording encrypted data today in order to decrypt it once a quantum computer exists. A live risk now for long-lived confidential data, such as Travel Rule messages.

concepts.shortDefinition: A function that turns any input into a short, fixed-length fingerprint.
concepts.bodyHtml: A function that turns any input into a short, fixed-length fingerprint. Any change to the input changes the output completely, and the input cannot be worked out from the output. Hashing makes tampering with a record visible, not impossible.

concepts.shortDefinition: In DeFi lending, a measure of how safe a loan is.
concepts.bodyHtml: In DeFi lending, a measure of how safe a loan is. Below 1, the collateral can be liquidated.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment fund, usually an AIF, that uses flexible strategies and techniques such as short selling, leverage and derivatives to seek returns in different market conditions.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment fund, usually an AIF, that uses flexible strategies and techniques such as short selling, leverage and derivatives to seek returns in different market conditions. It has no definition in EU law.

concepts.shortDefinition: Using a derivative or other position to offset the risk of an adverse price movement in an asset or currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: Using a derivative or other position to offset the risk of an adverse price movement in an asset or currency.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wealthy individual investor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wealthy individual investor. Depending on the rules, such an individual may elect to be treated as a professional client, or qualify as a qualifying investor or well-informed investor.

concepts.shortDefinition: The highest NAV per share previously reached by a fund, used as a reference point so that a performance fee is paid only on new gains above it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The highest NAV per share previously reached by a fund, used as a reference point so that a performance fee is paid only on new gains above it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised and whose regulator supervises it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised and whose regulator supervises it. Its product and licensing rules apply wherever the fund is marketed.

concepts.shortDefinition: One transfer between addresses.
concepts.bodyHtml: One transfer between addresses. Analytics counts the hops between a deposit and a risky source; confidence usually falls with each hop, but the risk does not disappear.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Member State, other than the home Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised, in which the fund is marketed or the manager operates under a passport, and whose local marketing rules apply.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Member State, other than the home Member State in which a fund or manager is authorised, in which the fund is marketed or the manager operates under a passport, and whose local marketing rules apply.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are held by a service provider on the customer's behalf.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are held by a service provider on the customer's behalf. Also called a custodial wallet.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are online, so that it can pay withdrawals quickly.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are online, so that it can pay withdrawals quickly. It is the most exposed to attack.

concepts.shortDefinition: High-quality liquid assets: cash and assets such as short-dated government debt that can be sold quickly near full value.
concepts.bodyHtml: High-quality liquid assets: cash and assets such as short-dated government debt that can be sold quickly near full value. Central to stablecoin reserves where there is no central bank to hold deposits.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum return that investors must receive before the manager earns a performance fee or carried interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum return that investors must receive before the manager earns a performance fee or carried interest. Also called the hurdle.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from the failure, compromise or misuse of information and communication technology systems and data, including cyber attacks, at the manager or its service providers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from the failure, compromise or misuse of information and communication technology systems and data, including cyber attacks, at the manager or its service providers. Under DORA, managers must have an ICT risk management framework.

concepts.shortDefinition: A contract with an ICT third-party service provider which, under Article 30 of DORA, must include mandatory terms such as a description of the services, data locations, service levels, incident assistance, cooperation with regulators and termination rights and, for critical or important functions, audit rights and exit strategies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A contract with an ICT third-party service provider which, under Article 30 of DORA, must include mandatory terms such as a description of the services, data locations, service levels, incident assistance, cooperation with regulators and termination rights and, for critical or important functions, audit rights and exit strategies.

concepts.shortDefinition: In practice, "very costly to change" rather than "impossible to change".
concepts.bodyHtml: In practice, "very costly to change" rather than "impossible to change". How immutable a blockchain is depends on how widely its network is spread; majority control can rewrite recent history.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investing with the intention of generating, and measuring, positive environmental or social effects alongside a financial return.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investing with the intention of generating, and measuring, positive environmental or social effects alongside a financial return.

concepts.shortDefinition: The maximum disruption to an important business service that a firm can tolerate before harm becomes intolerable.
concepts.bodyHtml: The maximum disruption to an important business service that a firm can tolerate before harm becomes intolerable. A concept from the UK operational resilience rules, now widely used elsewhere.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ethereum proof of stake, the gradual draining of offline validators' stake when the chain cannot finalise.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ethereum proof of stake, the gradual draining of offline validators' stake when the chain cannot finalise.

concepts.shortDefinition: A breach of an investment restriction caused by factors outside the manager’s control, such as market movements or subscriptions and redemptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A breach of an investment restriction caused by factors outside the manager’s control, such as market movements or subscriptions and redemptions. It must be remedied as a priority, taking due account of investors’ interests, but compensation is generally not payable.

concepts.shortDefinition: Costs that arise only in certain conditions, such as performance fees and carried interest, shown separately in the PRIIPs KID.
concepts.bodyHtml: Costs that arise only in certain conditions, such as performance fees and carried interest, shown separately in the PRIIPs KID.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment advice that, under MiFID II, is based on a sufficiently wide range of products.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment advice that, under MiFID II, is based on a sufficiently wide range of products. A firm giving it may not keep inducements from fund managers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A director who has no relationship with the promoter, manager or service providers that could affect his or her judgement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A director who has no relationship with the promoter, manager or service providers that could affect his or her judgement. The Irish Funds Corporate Governance Code provides for at least one, and the ALFI Code of Conduct recommends at least one; under CP86 an independent director takes the organisational effectiveness role.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement under Article 19 of the AIFMD that an AIF’s assets be valued properly and independently, either by an external valuer or by the AIFM itself if the valuation task is functionally independent from portfolio management.
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement under Article 19 of the AIFMD that an AIF’s assets be valued properly and independently, either by an external valuer or by the AIFM itself if the valuation task is functionally independent from portfolio management.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that seeks to replicate the performance of a market index by holding all, or a representative sample, of its constituents or by using derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that seeks to replicate the performance of a market index by holding all, or a representative sample, of its constituents or by using derivatives. Also called a tracker fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: An estimate of an ETF’s NAV per share calculated and published at frequent intervals during the trading day, to help investors judge whether the market price is fair.
concepts.bodyHtml: An estimate of an ETF’s NAV per share calculated and published at frequent intervals during the trading day, to help investors judge whether the market price is fair.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish framework introduced by the Central Bank (Individual Accountability Framework) Act 2023.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish framework introduced by the Central Bank (Individual Accountability Framework) Act 2023. Its conduct standards and enhanced fitness and probity rules have applied since 29 December 2023, including to FMCs and funds; its SEAR element does not apply to FMCs.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fee, commission or non-monetary benefit paid to or received by an intermediary from a third party, such as a fund manager, in connection with a service to a client.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fee, commission or non-monetary benefit paid to or received by an intermediary from a third party, such as a fund manager, in connection with a service to a client. MiFID II restricts inducements and bans them for independent advice and portfolio management.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund, usually closed-ended and structured like a private equity fund, that invests in long-life assets such as transport, energy, utilities and digital infrastructure, typically through equity or debt in project companies.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund, usually closed-ended and structured like a private equity fund, that invests in long-life assets such as transport, energy, utilities and digital infrastructure, typically through equity or debt in project companies.

concepts.shortDefinition: Risk before controls are taken into account, usually rated by impact and likelihood.
concepts.bodyHtml: Risk before controls are taken into account, usually rated by impact and likelihood. A crypto custodian's inherent risk of theft is high by definition.

concepts.shortDefinition: A sale of newly created tokens to the public to raise funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: A sale of newly created tokens to the public to raise funds. Variants include the initial exchange offering (IEO), run by an exchange for its users, and the initial DEX offering (IDO), run through a decentralised exchange or launchpad.

concepts.shortDefinition: The period at a fund’s launch during which units or shares are offered at a fixed initial offer price.
concepts.bodyHtml: The period at a fund’s launch during which units or shares are offered at a fixed initial offer price. Afterwards, they are issued at the NAV per share on each dealing day.

concepts.shortDefinition: A court order requiring a party to do, or more commonly to refrain from doing, something, for example to stop a breach of a contractual promise.
concepts.bodyHtml: A court order requiring a party to do, or more commonly to refrain from doing, something, for example to stop a breach of a contractual promise.

concepts.shortDefinition: The inability of a company to pay its debts as they fall due.
concepts.bodyHtml: The inability of a company to pay its debts as they fall due. A company can be insolvent even if its assets exceed its liabilities.

concepts.shortDefinition: An organisation, such as a pension scheme, insurer, bank, company or another fund, that invests on its own account or on behalf of others, usually in large amounts.
concepts.bodyHtml: An organisation, such as a pension scheme, insurer, bank, company or another fund, that invests on its own account or on behalf of others, usually in large amounts. Institutional investors are generally professional investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The constitutional document of an ICAV, equivalent to a company’s memorandum and articles of association.
concepts.bodyHtml: The constitutional document of an ICAV, equivalent to a company’s memorandum and articles of association.

concepts.shortDefinition: A benchmark interest rate at which banks are assumed to lend to each other, such as EURIBOR.
concepts.bodyHtml: A benchmark interest rate at which banks are assumed to lend to each other, such as EURIBOR. The London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) has ceased and been replaced by risk-free rates.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that stands between an investor and a fund or issuer, such as a financial adviser, bank, broker, platform or wealth manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that stands between an investor and a fund or issuer, such as a financial adviser, bank, broker, platform or wealth manager. In financial markets the main intermediaries are investment banks and broker-dealers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The function that provides independent assurance to management and the board on the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance.
concepts.bodyHtml: The function that provides independent assurance to management and the board on the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance. Company law does not require it, but UCITS and AIFM rules do in certain cases; it is the third line of defence.

concepts.shortDefinition: A centralised platform's own record of customer balances.
concepts.bodyHtml: A centralised platform's own record of customer balances. Customers hold a claim on the platform, not coins recorded in their own name on the blockchain.

concepts.shortDefinition: A CSD that settles internationally traded securities, such as eurobonds, across many markets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A CSD that settles internationally traded securities, such as eurobonds, across many markets. Many Irish ETFs settle through an ICSD, which allows a share class to be cross-listed on several exchanges and settled in a single pool.

concepts.shortDefinition: International Organization of Securities Commissions: 18 crypto and digital-asset recommendations (November 2023) and nine on DeFi (December 2023) — conflicts, market abuse, custody, retail distribution, cooperation.
concepts.bodyHtml: International Organization of Securities Commissions: 18 crypto and digital-asset recommendations (November 2023) and nine on DeFi (December 2023) — conflicts, market abuse, custody, retail distribution, cooperation.

concepts.shortDefinition: The common data standard for Travel Rule messages, so that different networks (TRP, TRUST, Sygna Bridge, Notabene) describe originators and beneficiaries the same way.
concepts.bodyHtml: The common data standard for Travel Rule messages, so that different networks (TRP, TRUST, Sygna Bridge, Notabene) describe originators and beneficiaries the same way.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, the provision of a personal recommendation to a client in respect of transactions in financial instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, the provision of a personal recommendation to a client in respect of transactions in financial instruments. A firm giving advice must assess suitability.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish public limited company established as a fund under Part 24 of the Companies Act 2014, usually with variable capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish public limited company established as a fund under Part 24 of the Companies Act 2014, usually with variable capital. It may be a UCITS or an AIF and may be an umbrella with segregated liability.

concepts.shortDefinition: A vehicle that pools the money of multiple investors and invests it collectively in assets, such as shares and bonds, for their mutual benefit, under a defined investment policy.
concepts.bodyHtml: A vehicle that pools the money of multiple investors and invests it collectively in assets, such as shares and bonds, for their mutual benefit, under a defined investment policy. Also called a mutual fund, collective investment undertaking, collective investment scheme or pooled investment vehicle.

concepts.shortDefinition: Instructions from a fund’s manager or directors to the investment manager about the nature or mode of acquisition of investments, in addition to the objective, policies and restrictions in the prospectus – for example, limiting the proportion of non-base currency assets that may be hedged.
concepts.bodyHtml: Instructions from a fund’s manager or directors to the investment manager about the nature or mode of acquisition of investments, in addition to the objective, policies and restrictions in the prospectus – for example, limiting the proportion of non-base currency assets that may be hedged.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Irish limited partnership fund vehicle.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Irish limited partnership fund vehicle. It can only be an AIF (a RIAIF or QIAIF) and is mostly used for closed-ended private equity, infrastructure and similar funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The combination of portfolio management and risk management, which is the core function of a ManCo or AIFM and is often delegated in part to an investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: The combination of portfolio management and risk management, which is the core function of a ManCo or AIFM and is often delegated in part to an investment manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract appointing an investment manager, setting out how the fund’s portfolio is to be managed and invested and the operational terms of the service, such as dealing, delegation, fees and reporting.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract appointing an investment manager, setting out how the fund’s portfolio is to be managed and invested and the operational terms of the service, such as dealing, delegation, fees and reporting. Also called the investment mandate.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm that manages the fund’s portfolio and takes investment decisions on which assets to buy and sell, within the fund’s investment objective, policies and restrictions, usually under a delegation from the ManCo or AIFM.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm that manages the fund’s portfolio and takes investment decisions on which assets to buy and sell, within the fund’s investment objective, policies and restrictions, usually under a delegation from the ManCo or AIFM.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fundamental aim of a fund, set out in its prospectus, for example long-term capital growth or a high level of income, usually indicating the main types of asset and markets in which it will invest.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fundamental aim of a fund, set out in its prospectus, for example long-term capital growth or a high level of income, usually indicating the main types of asset and markets in which it will invest.

concepts.shortDefinition: The period, usually several years, during which a closed-ended fund such as a private equity fund makes new investments and draws down commitments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The period, usually several years, during which a closed-ended fund such as a private equity fund makes new investments and draws down commitments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The detailed description in a fund’s prospectus of how the investment manager will try to achieve the investment objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: The detailed description in a fund’s prospectus of how the investment manager will try to achieve the investment objective.

concepts.shortDefinition: The way in which a portfolio manager executes a fund’s investment strategy, made up of asset allocation, security selection, portfolio construction and risk control.
concepts.bodyHtml: The way in which a portfolio manager executes a fund’s investment strategy, made up of asset allocation, security selection, portfolio construction and risk control.

concepts.shortDefinition: Limits on a fund’s powers of investment, such as the maximum exposure to one issuer or the maximum leverage, imposed by regulation, the fund documents, a stock exchange or the fund’s directors, to limit its exposure to risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: Limits on a fund’s powers of investment, such as the maximum exposure to one issuer or the maximum leverage, imposed by regulation, the fund documents, a stock exchange or the fund’s directors, to limit its exposure to risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The gain or loss on an investment over a period, from income and capital growth, expressed as a percentage of the amount invested.
concepts.bodyHtml: The gain or loss on an investment over a period, from income and capital growth, expressed as a percentage of the amount invested.

concepts.shortDefinition: The services regulated by MiFID II, including reception and transmission of orders, execution of orders, dealing on own account, portfolio management, investment advice and placing of financial instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: The services regulated by MiFID II, including reception and transmission of orders, execution of orders, dealing on own account, portfolio management, investment advice and placing of financial instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: The approach a fund’s manager takes to achieve its investment objective, such as active or passive management, income or growth, or a particular asset class, region or theme.
concepts.bodyHtml: The approach a fund’s manager takes to achieve its investment objective, such as active or passive management, income or growth, or a particular asset class, region or theme.

concepts.shortDefinition: A UK closed-ended investment company whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange, so that investors can exit by selling to other investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A UK closed-ended investment company whose shares are listed and traded on a stock exchange, so that investors can exit by selling to other investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: A scheme that compensates clients of a failed investment firm that cannot return their money or assets, up to a limit.
concepts.bodyHtml: A scheme that compensates clients of a failed investment firm that cannot return their money or assets, up to a limit. It does not cover falls in market value. Ireland’s scheme pays 90% of a net loss up to €20,000.

concepts.shortDefinition: The information an AIFM must make available to investors before they invest in an AIF under Article 23 of the AIFMD, such as its strategy, risks, leverage, parties, valuation, liquidity management, LMTs, fees and performance, together with material changes and periodic disclosures.
concepts.bodyHtml: The information an AIFM must make available to investors before they invest in an AIF under Article 23 of the AIFMD, such as its strategy, risks, leverage, parties, valuation, liquidity management, LMTs, fees and performance, together with material changes and periodic disclosures.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules that protect investors, such as product restrictions, disclosure, conduct rules and independent safekeeping of assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules that protect investors, such as product restrictions, disclosure, conduct rules and independent safekeeping of assets. Its level depends on the category of investor, with retail investors receiving the most.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish corporate fund vehicle with variable capital, established under the ICAV Act 2015 specifically for investment funds and registered and supervised by the CBI.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish corporate fund vehicle with variable capital, established under the ICAV Act 2015 specifically for investment funds and registered and supervised by the CBI. It may be a UCITS or an AIF, can be an umbrella with segregated liability, may dispense with its AGM and can elect to be treated as transparent for US tax purposes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard contract published by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association under which most OTC derivatives are documented.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard contract published by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association under which most OTC derivatives are documented. Its annexes, such as a Credit Support Annex, set out the collateral or security a fund provides.

concepts.shortDefinition: The typical return pattern of a private equity fund: negative in the early years, as fees are paid before investments mature, and rising later as investments are realised.
concepts.bodyHtml: The typical return pattern of a private equity fund: negative in the early years, as fees are paid before investments mature, and rising later as investments are realised.

concepts.shortDefinition: A scripted, witnessed and recorded procedure to generate, use, rotate or recover cryptographic keys.
concepts.bodyHtml: A scripted, witnessed and recorded procedure to generate, use, rotate or recover cryptographic keys. Good practice keeps the script, attendance record, video and signed minutes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standardised pre-contractual document of no more than three sides of A4 that must be given to retail investors in good time before they invest in a packaged retail and insurance-based investment product (PRIIP), including a UCITS or an AIF sold to retail investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standardised pre-contractual document of no more than three sides of A4 that must be given to retail investors in good time before they invest in a packaged retail and insurance-based investment product (PRIIP), including a UCITS or an AIF sold to retail investors. It explains the product, its risks (including the SRI), four performance scenarios (stress, unfavourable, moderate and favourable) and costs.

concepts.shortDefinition: The short UCITS disclosure document introduced by UCITS IV.
concepts.bodyHtml: The short UCITS disclosure document introduced by UCITS IV. Since 1 January 2023 it has been replaced by the PRIIPs KID for UCITS sold to retail investors and survives only where no KID is produced.

concepts.shortDefinition: A metric that signals a change in risk and can trigger an alert when it crosses a threshold, such as hot-wallet balances, failed withdrawals or reconciliation breaks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A metric that signals a change in risk and can trigger an alert when it crosses a threshold, such as hot-wallet balances, failed withdrawals or reconciliation breaks.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dependence on one individual for decisions or know-how — a founder no one can challenge, or one engineer who knows key recovery.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dependence on one individual for decisions or know-how — a founder no one can challenge, or one engineer who knows key recovery.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent rating of rollups.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent rating of rollups. Stage 0: the operator can override. Stage 1: proofs are live but a security council can intervene. Stage 2: no override.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that runs token sales for issuers, usually for a fee plus a share of the tokens.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that runs token sales for issuers, usually for a fee plus a share of the tokens. Providing services for an issuer's offer or sale is one of the FATF virtual asset activities; issuing tokens alone generally is not.

concepts.shortDefinition: Layer 0 connects chains; layer 1 is the base chain and final record; layer 2 executes transactions and settles to layer 1; layer 3 settles to a layer 2.
concepts.bodyHtml: Layer 0 connects chains; layer 1 is the base chain and final record; layer 2 executes transactions and settles to layer 1; layer 3 settles to a layer 2.

concepts.shortDefinition: A base blockchain, such as Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana, that settles transactions itself.
concepts.bodyHtml: A base blockchain, such as Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana, that settles transactions itself.

concepts.shortDefinition: A network built on top of a layer 1 that processes transactions more cheaply and posts the results, or proofs of them, back to the layer 1.
concepts.bodyHtml: A network built on top of a layer 1 that processes transactions more cheaply and posts the results, or proofs of them, back to the layer 1. Rollups are the main type.

concepts.shortDefinition: A network built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.
concepts.bodyHtml: A network built on top of a layer 2, often for a single application.

concepts.shortDefinition: The second stage of money laundering, in which funds are moved through many transactions to obscure their origin.
concepts.bodyHtml: The second stage of money laundering, in which funds are moved through many transactions to obscure their origin.

concepts.shortDefinition: North Korean state-linked hacking group; the FBI attributed the Bybit theft to North Korea ("TraderTraitor").
concepts.bodyHtml: North Korean state-linked hacking group; the FBI attributed the Bybit theft to North Korea ("TraderTraitor"). Its proceeds raise sanctions and proliferation-financing issues.

concepts.shortDefinition: A record of who owns what and who has paid whom.
concepts.bodyHtml: A record of who owns what and who has paid whom. A blockchain is a ledger shared and maintained by many participants rather than kept by one record-keeper.

concepts.shortDefinition: The law firm, sometimes called outside legal counsel, appointed to advise a fund.
