concepts.bodyHtml: The law firm, sometimes called outside legal counsel, appointed to advise a fund. It prepares applications to the regulator, drafts the constitutional documents and prospectus, negotiates service agreements, coordinates the launch and updates documents for later changes in law.

concepts.shortDefinition: The legal structure in which a fund is constituted: corporate, unit trust, contractual or limited partnership.
concepts.bodyHtml: The legal structure in which a fund is constituted: corporate, unit trust, contractual or limited partnership. It is distinct from the fund’s regulatory type (UCITS or AIF).

concepts.shortDefinition: The person registered as the owner of an asset or in possession of it, who may hold it for the benefit of a different beneficial owner, such as a trustee or nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person registered as the owner of an asset or in possession of it, who may hold it for the benefit of a different beneficial owner, such as a trustee or nominee.

concepts.shortDefinition: The legal capacity of an entity to own assets, enter into contracts and sue or be sued in its own name.
concepts.bodyHtml: The legal capacity of an entity to own assets, enter into contracts and sue or be sued in its own name. Corporate funds have it; unit trusts, contractual funds and most limited partnerships do not, so their ManCo, trustee or GP acts for them.

concepts.shortDefinition: A central bank's power to lend to solvent but illiquid institutions in a crisis.
concepts.bodyHtml: A central bank's power to lend to solvent but illiquid institutions in a crisis. Stablecoin issuers have no lender of last resort, so their reserves must be safe and liquid by design, as the USDC depeg during the Silicon Valley Bank failure (March 2023) showed.

concepts.shortDefinition: A ManCo or AIFM that has delegated so much, or retains so little expertise, resources or decision-making power, that it can no longer be considered the manager of the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A ManCo or AIFM that has delegated so much, or retains so little expertise, resources or decision-making power, that it can no longer be considered the manager of the fund. Regulation prohibits a manager from becoming one.

concepts.shortDefinition: Any method by which a fund increases its exposure beyond its NAV, whether through borrowing cash or securities, or leverage embedded in derivative positions or by any other means.
concepts.bodyHtml: Any method by which a fund increases its exposure beyond its NAV, whether through borrowing cash or securities, or leverage embedded in derivative positions or by any other means. It magnifies both gains and losses. Also called gearing.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a creditor in possession of a debtor’s asset to retain it until the debt is paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a creditor in possession of a debtor’s asset to retain it until the debt is paid. The holder generally cannot sell the asset and loses the lien if it parts with possession. Depositary agreements often give the fund depositary a lien.

concepts.shortDefinition: Bitcoin's payment-channel network: two on-chain transactions to open and close, many off-chain payments in between.
concepts.bodyHtml: Bitcoin's payment-channel network: two on-chain transactions to open and close, many off-chain payments in between.

concepts.shortDefinition: An open-ended fund that offers redemptions less frequently than normally required.
concepts.bodyHtml: An open-ended fund that offers redemptions less frequently than normally required. In Ireland, a RIAIF offering less than monthly, or a QIAIF less than quarterly, redemptions.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investor in a limited partnership, whose liability for its debts is generally limited to its capital contribution or commitment and who does not take part in managing it.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investor in a limited partnership, whose liability for its debts is generally limited to its capital contribution or commitment and who does not take part in managing it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A partnership with at least one general partner, which manages it and has unlimited liability, and limited partners, whose liability is limited to their capital contribution.
concepts.bodyHtml: A partnership with at least one general partner, which manages it and has unlimited liability, and limited partners, whose liability is limited to their capital contribution. Fund LPs can only be AIFs, are mostly closed-ended and are used for professional investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: A licence granted for a set period, or with limits on volumes, activities or client types, before a full licence is given (for example Bermuda's Class M licence).
concepts.bodyHtml: A licence granted for a set period, or with limits on volumes, activities or client types, before a full licence is given (for example Bermuda's Class M licence). The conditions act as the main controls while the firm builds a track record.

concepts.shortDefinition: Staking through a pool that issues a tradable receipt token (a liquid staking token) representing the staked asset and its rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: Staking through a pool that issues a tradable receipt token (a liquid staking token) representing the staked asset and its rewards.

concepts.shortDefinition: A tradable receipt for staked tokens, such as stETH or cbETH, representing the staked asset and its rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: A tradable receipt for staked tokens, such as stETH or cbETH, representing the staked asset and its rewards. It can trade below the value of the tokens behind it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process of winding up a company’s affairs, in which a liquidator realises its assets and distributes the proceeds to creditors and then members in a prescribed order.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process of winding up a company’s affairs, in which a liquidator realises its assets and distributes the proceeds to creditors and then members in a prescribed order. A liquidator cannot use property the company holds on trust or in a fiduciary capacity to pay its creditors. Also called winding up.

concepts.shortDefinition: The forced sale of a borrower's or trader's collateral when a loan or leveraged position falls below the required margin.
concepts.bodyHtml: The forced sale of a borrower's or trader's collateral when a loan or leveraged position falls below the required margin. In DeFi lending, the protocol does this automatically when a loan's health factor falls below 1, and liquidators are paid a bonus for doing so.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person appointed to wind up a company: to gather in and sell its assets, pay its creditors in a prescribed order and distribute any surplus to its members.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person appointed to wind up a company: to gather in and sell its assets, pay its creditors in a prescribed order and distribute any surplus to its members. A liquidator cannot use assets held on trust or in a fiduciary capacity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The ease with which an asset can be turned into cash quickly without a significant loss of value.
concepts.bodyHtml: The ease with which an asset can be turned into cash quickly without a significant loss of value. Cash is the most liquid asset; real estate and loans are illiquid.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: How easily an asset can be bought or sold quickly without moving its price.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cash and liquid assets held by a fund to meet redemptions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cash and liquid assets held by a fund to meet redemptions. Holding too much lowers returns, so it must be balanced against the fund’s dealing terms.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fee charged on redemptions to reflect the cost to the fund of providing liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fee charged on redemptions to reflect the cost to the fund of providing liquidity. Under the MMFR, a public debt CNAV or LVNAV MMF must consider or apply liquidity fees when its weekly maturing assets fall below set levels.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum share of reserves that must be available as cash within a set time — same day, five days, 30 days — sized to the worst observed outflow.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum share of reserves that must be available as cash within a set time — same day, five days, 30 days — sized to the worst observed outflow. The fix for a coin that is solvent but illiquid.

concepts.shortDefinition: A tool used to manage redemptions in an open-ended fund, such as suspension, redemption gates, extended notice periods, redemption in kind, redemption fees, swing pricing, dual pricing, anti-dilution levies and side pockets.
concepts.bodyHtml: A tool used to manage redemptions in an open-ended fund, such as suspension, redemption gates, extended notice periods, redemption in kind, redemption fees, swing pricing, dual pricing, anti-dilution levies and side pockets. Since 16 April 2026 UCITS and open-ended AIFs must select at least two from the harmonised lists, other than suspension and side pockets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A difference between how often investors can redeem from a fund and how quickly its assets can be sold without loss.
concepts.bodyHtml: A difference between how often investors can redeem from a fund and how quickly its assets can be sold without loss.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Tokens that move 24/7 over assets that take days or months to sell. The FSB's first tokenisation vulnerability: run risk where the token looks more liquid than the asset.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person or firm that deposits tokens into an AMM pool, or quotes prices, so that others can trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person or firm that deposits tokens into an AMM pool, or quotes prices, so that others can trade.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that a fund cannot sell assets quickly enough, or at a fair price, to meet redemptions or other obligations.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that a fund cannot sell assets quickly enough, or at a fair price, to meet redemptions or other obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which a manager keeps a fund’s liquidity consistent with its redemption terms, including setting dealing terms, holding liquid assets, monitoring the investor base and liquidity stress testing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which a manager keeps a fund’s liquidity consistent with its redemption terms, including setting dealing terms, holding liquid assets, monitoring the investor base and liquidity stress testing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Testing how a fund’s liquidity would cope with severe but plausible conditions, such as large redemptions or falling market liquidity, in line with ESMA guidelines.
concepts.bodyHtml: Testing how a fund’s liquidity would cope with severe but plausible conditions, such as large redemptions or falling market liquidity, in line with ESMA guidelines.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that arranges the admission of a fund’s shares, such as ETF shares, to trading on a stock exchange.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that arranges the admission of a fund’s shares, such as ETF shares, to trading on a stock exchange.

concepts.shortDefinition: Granting a loan directly as original lender, or indirectly through a third party or special purpose vehicle.
concepts.bodyHtml: Granting a loan directly as original lender, or indirectly through a third party or special purpose vehicle. UCITS may not grant loans.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF whose strategy is mainly to originate loans, or whose originated loans have a notional value of at least 50% of its NAV.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF whose strategy is mainly to originate loans, or whose originated loans have a notional value of at least 50% of its NAV. Under AIFMD II it must retain 5% of the notional value of loans it sells, its leverage is capped at 175% (open-ended) or 300% (closed-ended), and it must be closed-ended unless its manager can show that its liquidity management is compatible with open-ended redemption.

concepts.shortDefinition: A former category of Irish QIAIF permitted to originate loans.
concepts.bodyHtml: A former category of Irish QIAIF permitted to originate loans. The revised AIF Rulebook removed it on 5 May 2026, and Irish AIFs that originate loans now follow the AIFMD II rules.
concepts.notes: Ireland; replaced by the AIFMD II loan origination rules

concepts.shortDefinition: A period after investing during which an investor may not redeem from a fund, common in hedge funds and in closed-ended or limited liquidity AIFs.
concepts.bodyHtml: A period after investing during which an investor may not redeem from a fund, common in hedge funds and in closed-ended or limited liquidity AIFs.

concepts.shortDefinition: Quantum attacks on public keys already visible on-chain (long), or on a key revealed while a transaction waits to be confirmed (short).
concepts.bodyHtml: Quantum attacks on public keys already visible on-chain (long), or on a key revealed while a transaction waits to be confirmed (short).

concepts.shortDefinition: Considering the underlying exposure of an instrument rather than only its legal form.
concepts.bodyHtml: Considering the underlying exposure of an instrument rather than only its legal form. ESMA has advised a stricter look-through test so that a UCITS cannot use instruments such as exchange-traded notes to gain significant exposure to assets it could not hold directly.

concepts.term: Low volatility net asset value MMF
concepts.shortDefinition: An MMF permitted to deal at a constant NAV, using amortised cost for assets maturing within 75 days, while that NAV stays within 20 basis points of its mark-to-market NAV.
concepts.bodyHtml: An MMF permitted to deal at a constant NAV, using amortised cost for assets maturing within 75 days, while that NAV stays within 20 basis points of its mark-to-market NAV.
concepts.sortKey: low volatility net asset value mmf

concepts.shortDefinition: The acquisition of a company by an external management team, which replaces the incumbent management, often financed by a private equity fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The acquisition of a company by an external management team, which replaces the incumbent management, often financed by a private equity fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The acquisition of a company by its existing management team, often financed by a private equity fund and debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: The acquisition of a company by its existing management team, often financed by a private equity fund and debt.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity responsible for the management of an externally managed fund, including investment management, administration and marketing.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity responsible for the management of an externally managed fund, including investment management, administration and marketing. In the EEA it is either a UCITS ManCo or an AIFM, and it retains regulatory responsibility for any tasks it delegates.

concepts.shortDefinition: The periodic fee, usually a percentage of NAV, paid from a fund’s assets to its manager for managing it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The periodic fee, usually a percentage of NAV, paid from a fund’s assets to its manager for managing it. It is the main part of a fund’s ongoing charges.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a UCITS ManCo or EEA AIFM authorised in its home Member State to manage funds domiciled in another Member State, either directly or through a branch, after notifying its home regulator, without being authorised again.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a UCITS ManCo or EEA AIFM authorised in its home Member State to manage funds domiciled in another Member State, either directly or through a branch, after notifying its home regulator, without being authorised again.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules, drawn up by the ManCo, that constitute a Luxembourg FCP and set out unitholders’ rights.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules, drawn up by the ManCo, that constitute a Luxembourg FCP and set out unitholders’ rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under CP86, the six functions of an Irish FMC that must each be overseen by a designated person: investment management, fund risk management, operational risk management, regulatory compliance, distribution, and capital and financial management.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under CP86, the six functions of an Irish FMC that must each be overseen by a designated person: investment management, fund risk management, operational risk management, regulatory compliance, distribution, and capital and financial management.

concepts.shortDefinition: The firm that creates a financial product.
concepts.bodyHtml: The firm that creates a financial product. Under MiFID II a manufacturer defines a target market; under the PRIIPs Regulation the manufacturer of a fund, usually its ManCo, produces the KID.

concepts.shortDefinition: Collateral exchanged to cover exposure on derivatives, such as futures and OTC derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: Collateral exchanged to cover exposure on derivatives, such as futures and OTC derivatives. EMIR requires margin to be exchanged on many non-cleared OTC derivatives.

concepts.shortDefinition: Valuing an asset at readily available closing prices from independent sources.
concepts.bodyHtml: Valuing an asset at readily available closing prices from independent sources. Where this is not possible, the asset is valued conservatively using a model based on market inputs (mark-to-model).

concepts.shortDefinition: Valuing an asset using a model based on market inputs where a readily available market price does not exist.
concepts.bodyHtml: Valuing an asset using a model based on market inputs where a readily available market price does not exist. The MMFR requires it to be done conservatively.

concepts.shortDefinition: European Commission proposals of 4 December 2025, not yet law, which for funds would allow notification of cross-border marketing at authorisation, stop gold-plating, change the pre-marketing rules, delete the UCITS KIID obligation and give ESMA a role in the supervision of large cross-border asset management groups.
concepts.bodyHtml: European Commission proposals of 4 December 2025, not yet law, which for funds would allow notification of cross-border marketing at authorisation, stop gold-plating, change the pre-marketing rules, delete the UCITS KIID obligation and give ESMA a role in the supervision of large cross-border asset management groups.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that undertakes to quote prices at which it will buy and sell a security continuously, providing liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that undertakes to quote prices at which it will buy and sell a security continuously, providing liquidity. ETF market makers quote two-way prices on exchange within a maximum spread.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A firm that continuously quotes buy and sell prices to provide liquidity, earning the spread.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that quotes buy and sell prices for a token, often paid by the issuer in borrowed tokens with call options.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that quotes buy and sell prices for a token, often paid by the issuer in borrowed tokens with call options. A legitimate service, but open to abuse through wash trading, as the US Operation Token Mirrors (2024) showed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from movements in market prices, such as interest rates, equity prices, commodity prices and exchange rates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from movements in market prices, such as interest rates, equity prices, commodity prices and exchange rates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the AIFMD, a direct or indirect offering or placement, at the initiative of the AIFM or on its behalf, of units or shares of an AIF it manages to or with investors domiciled or with a registered office in the EEA.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the AIFMD, a direct or indirect offering or placement, at the initiative of the AIFM or on its behalf, of units or shares of an AIF it manages to or with investors domiciled or with a registered office in the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: Any message about a fund that promotes it, such as a fact sheet, advertisement, website or social media post.
concepts.bodyHtml: Any message about a fund that promotes it, such as a fact sheet, advertisement, website or social media post. Under the CBDFR and ESMA guidelines it must be identifiable as such, describe risks and rewards equally prominently, be fair, clear and not misleading, and be consistent with the prospectus and KID.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a UCITS to be marketed to retail and professional investors, and of an EEA AIF managed by an authorised EEA AIFM to be marketed to professional investors, in other Member States after a notification procedure.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a UCITS to be marketed to retail and professional investors, and of an EEA AIF managed by an authorised EEA AIFM to be marketed to professional investors, in other Member States after a notification procedure.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, which has applied in full since 30 December 2024 and regulates issuers of, and service providers in, crypto-assets that are not financial instruments.
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, which has applied in full since 30 December 2024 and regulates issuers of, and service providers in, crypto-assets that are not financial instruments. It does not regulate investment funds, and tokenised fund units fall outside it.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The EU Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114). Its stablecoin rules applied from 30 June 2024 and its rules for crypto-asset service providers from 30 December 2024. The transitional period for firms operating under earlier national regimes ended on 1 July 2026.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU framework for investment services and activities, made up of Directive 2014/65/EU and the directly applicable MiFIR, which has applied since 3 January 2018.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU framework for investment services and activities, made up of Directive 2014/65/EU and the directly applicable MiFIR, which has applied since 3 January 2018. It covers portfolio management, advice and distribution of funds, including product governance, suitability, appropriateness and inducements.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund in a master-feeder structure into which one or more feeder funds invest and where the trading takes place.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund in a master-feeder structure into which one or more feeder funds invest and where the trading takes place. A master UCITS must have at least one feeder, cannot itself be a feeder and may not charge the feeder subscription or redemption fees.

concepts.shortDefinition: A structure in which one or more feeder funds, often domiciled in different jurisdictions, invest all or most of their assets in a single master fund, where the trading takes place.
concepts.bodyHtml: A structure in which one or more feeder funds, often domiciled in different jurisdictions, invest all or most of their assets in a single master fund, where the trading takes place.

concepts.shortDefinition: The level of NAV error, expressed as a percentage of NAV, above which an error must be corrected, investors and the fund compensated and the regulator informed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The level of NAV error, expressed as a percentage of NAV, above which an error must be corrected, investors and the fund compensated and the regulator informed. Also called the tolerance threshold; in Luxembourg CSSF Circular 24/856 sets 0.20% for MMFs, 0.50% for bond and mixed funds and 1.00% for equity and other funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The profit that can be made by including, excluding or reordering transactions in a block, for example by front-running a trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: The profit that can be made by including, excluding or reordering transactions in a block, for example by front-running a trade.

concepts.shortDefinition: The liquidation of a solvent company at the choice of its directors and shareholders, who control the process.
concepts.bodyHtml: The liquidation of a solvent company at the choice of its directors and shareholders, who control the process. It is the usual way to wind up a corporate fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token driven by internet culture and speculation, typically with no rights or underlying business.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token driven by internet culture and speculation, typically with no rights or underlying business.

concepts.shortDefinition: The pool of transactions that have been broadcast but not yet included in a block.
concepts.bodyHtml: The pool of transactions that have been broadcast but not yet included in a block.

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of work, a participant who uses specialised hardware and electricity to compete for the right to add the next block and earn the reward.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of work, a participant who uses specialised hardware and electricity to compete for the right to add the next block and earn the reward.

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of work, the process of competing to add blocks by solving computational puzzles, in return for newly issued coins and fees.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of work, the process of competing to add blocks by solving computational puzzles, in return for newly issued coins and fees. In proof of stake, validators perform the equivalent role by locking up a stake (32 ETH per validator on Ethereum). Mining or validating on one's own account is generally not a regulated service.

concepts.shortDefinition: Miners combining computing power and sharing rewards; the pool operator chooses the transactions and builds the block.
concepts.bodyHtml: Miners combining computing power and sharing rewards; the pool operator chooses the transactions and builds the block. Bitcoin mining is concentrated in a small number of large pools.

concepts.shortDefinition: To create new tokens.
concepts.bodyHtml: To create new tokens.

concepts.shortDefinition: Creating new tokens and removing them from supply.
concepts.bodyHtml: Creating new tokens and removing them from supply. For a stablecoin, tokens are minted against money received and burned on redemption, so every mint should match money in and every burn a payment out, reconciled daily.

concepts.shortDefinition: Selling a product to an investor for whom it is unsuitable, or on the basis of misleading information.
concepts.bodyHtml: Selling a product to an investor for whom it is unsuitable, or on the basis of misleading information. Marketing and mis-selling risk arises from misleading or out-of-date offering and sales documents.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that pools and redistributes funds from many users to break the link between the source and the destination.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that pools and redistributes funds from many users to break the link between the source and the destination. Tornado Cash is a smart contract mixer.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person in a firm responsible for receiving internal suspicion reports and deciding whether to report to the Financial Intelligence Unit.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person in a firm responsible for receiving internal suspicion reports and deciding whether to report to the Financial Intelligence Unit. The role needs access to data, authority and a direct line to the board.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests in short-term money market instruments, deposits and reverse repos, aiming to preserve capital and provide daily liquidity with a return in line with short-term interest rates.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests in short-term money market instruments, deposits and reverse repos, aiming to preserve capital and provide daily liquidity with a return in line with short-term interest rates. MMFs, whether UCITS or AIFs, are regulated by the MMFR, which limits the WAM and WAL of a short-term MMF to 60 and 120 days and of a standard MMF to 6 and 12 months.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2017/1131, which has applied to all MMFs, whether UCITS or AIFs, since 21 January 2019.
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2017/1131, which has applied to all MMFs, whether UCITS or AIFs, since 21 January 2019. It defines public debt CNAV, LVNAV and VNAV MMFs and sets rules on eligible assets, diversification, credit quality, liquidity, valuation, stress testing and transparency.

concepts.shortDefinition: Short-term debt instruments normally dealt in on the money market, such as treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit, that are liquid and can be accurately valued at any time.
concepts.bodyHtml: Short-term debt instruments normally dealt in on the money market, such as treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit, that are liquid and can be accurately valued at any time.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person who moves illicit funds through their own accounts or wallets on behalf of criminals, knowingly or not.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person who moves illicit funds through their own accounts or wallets on behalf of criminals, knowingly or not.

concepts.shortDefinition: A form of security in which legal ownership of the asset is transferred to the creditor while the debtor keeps possession and use of it, subject to the debtor’s right to redeem by repaying the debt.
concepts.bodyHtml: A form of security in which legal ownership of the asset is transferred to the creditor while the debtor keeps possession and use of it, subject to the debtor’s right to redeem by repaying the debt. In Ireland, a legal mortgage of land can now only be created by way of charge.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that uses multi-party computation to split signing power into shares held by several parties.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that uses multi-party computation to split signing power into shares held by several parties. A provider that can sign, co-sign or block transactions is exercising control and may be a virtual asset service provider; one that only licenses software generally is not.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose signing key is split between several parties using multi-party computation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose signing key is split between several parties using multi-party computation. It still uses elliptic curves, so it is not quantum-safe.

concepts.shortDefinition: A stablecoin issued by affiliated entities in more than one jurisdiction, so that the same token is issued under different regulatory regimes, often with separate reserves.
concepts.bodyHtml: A stablecoin issued by affiliated entities in more than one jurisdiction, so that the same token is issued under different regulatory regimes, often with separate reserves. It raises the question of whether holders in each jurisdiction have equal rights to redeem and equal access to the reserves.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund whose portfolio is divided among several portfolio managers, each with a mandate to manage a portion, selected and overseen by a principal manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund whose portfolio is divided among several portfolio managers, each with a mandate to manage a portion, selected and overseen by a principal manager. Also called a manager of managers fund. The sub-managers are delegates of the ManCo or AIFM.

concepts.shortDefinition: A cryptographic technique in which several parties each hold a share of a key and sign jointly, without the full key ever existing in one place.
concepts.bodyHtml: A cryptographic technique in which several parties each hold a share of a key and sign jointly, without the full key ever existing in one place. In practice the vendor's policy engine often becomes the real control point, which is invisible on-chain.

concepts.shortDefinition: The FSB's term for a firm or group that combines a broad range of crypto services, typically around a trading platform.
concepts.bodyHtml: The FSB's term for a firm or group that combines a broad range of crypto services, typically around a trading platform.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet that requires signatures from several keys (for example three of five) to approve a transaction.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet that requires signatures from several keys (for example three of five) to approve a transaction. Multisig and multi-party computation add little protection if every signer relies on the same compromised screen, as the Bybit hack showed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The peer assessment of a jurisdiction against the FATF standards, by FATF or a regional body, rating technical compliance and effectiveness and setting recommended actions tracked through follow-up.
concepts.bodyHtml: The peer assessment of a jurisdiction against the FATF standards, by FATF or a regional body, rating technical compliance and effectiveness and setting recommended actions tracked through follow-up.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank that holds only safe, liquid assets against its deposits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank that holds only safe, liquid assets against its deposits. A fiat-backed stablecoin issuer works in a similar way, with tokens as liabilities and reserves as assets, but usually keeps the interest and has no deposit insurance or lender of last resort.

concepts.shortDefinition: The national regulator in each EEA Member State that authorises and supervises funds and their managers, such as the CBI in Ireland and the CSSF in Luxembourg.
concepts.bodyHtml: The national regulator in each EEA Member State that authorises and supervises funds and their managers, such as the CBI in Ireland and the CSSF in Luxembourg.

concepts.term: National Institute of Standards and Technology
concepts.sortKey: national institute of standards and technology

concepts.shortDefinition: A Member State’s rules allowing AIFs not entitled to the AIFMD passport, such as non-EEA AIFs, to be marketed to professional investors in that state.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Member State’s rules allowing AIFs not entitled to the AIFMD passport, such as non-EEA AIFs, to be marketed to professional investors in that state. Since AIFMD II it is not available where the third country is listed as high-risk for AML purposes or as non-cooperative for tax purposes.

concepts.shortDefinition: A country's assessment of its money laundering and terrorist financing risks, required by FATF Recommendation 1.
concepts.bodyHtml: A country's assessment of its money laundering and terrorist financing risks, required by FATF Recommendation 1. It identifies the higher-risk sectors, including virtual asset service providers, and informs how firms and supervisors allocate resources.

concepts.shortDefinition: In a native model the blockchain is the legal register of a fund; in a mirrored model the token reflects an off-chain register, which prevails if they differ.
concepts.bodyHtml: In a native model the blockchain is the legal register of a fund; in a mirrored model the token reflects an off-chain register, which prevails if they differ.

concepts.shortDefinition: The built-in currency of a blockchain, used to pay fees, such as BTC on Bitcoin or ETH on Ethereum.
concepts.bodyHtml: The built-in currency of a blockchain, used to pay fees, such as BTC on Bitcoin or ETH on Ethereum.

concepts.shortDefinition: A security created on the ledger, so the token entry is the legal record of ownership.
concepts.bodyHtml: A security created on the ledger, so the token entry is the legal record of ownership. One record; the risk sits in the ledger, the code and the keys. It needs a law that recognises the ledger entry.

concepts.shortDefinition: An error in the calculation of a fund’s NAV, for example from a wrong price, a missed trade or corporate action or an incorrect fee accrual.
concepts.bodyHtml: An error in the calculation of a fund’s NAV, for example from a wrong price, a missed trade or corporate action or an incorrect fee accrual. Errors above the materiality (tolerance) threshold must be corrected, investors and the fund compensated and the regulator informed. In Luxembourg, CSSF Circular 24/856 sets the thresholds.

concepts.shortDefinition: An incident that nearly caused a loss, such as an attack stopped by a second signer.
concepts.bodyHtml: An incident that nearly caused a loss, such as an attack stopped by a second signer. Near misses are early warnings and are usually reported to senior management and the board.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that operates through an account at another exchange, so that the host exchange's customer is a business with its own customers.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that operates through an account at another exchange, so that the host exchange's customer is a business with its own customers.

concepts.shortDefinition: The value of a fund’s assets less its liabilities.
concepts.bodyHtml: The value of a fund’s assets less its liabilities. The NAV per unit or share, the price at which investors usually deal, is the NAV divided by the number of units or shares in issue.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The value of a fund per unit, used for dealing. In a tokenised fund it is often pushed on-chain by an oracle; who calculates and pushes it is a valuation question.

concepts.shortDefinition: Offsetting amounts owed between two parties so that only the net balance is payable, as with payments under swaps or margin on futures and options.
concepts.bodyHtml: Offsetting amounts owed between two parties so that only the net balance is payable, as with payments under swaps or margin on futures and options. The Irish Netting of Financial Contracts Act 1995 preserves contractual netting in an insolvency.

concepts.term: New York State Department of Financial Services
concepts.sortKey: new york state department of financial services

concepts.shortDefinition: A computer that runs a blockchain's software, keeps a copy of the ledger and checks transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A computer that runs a blockchain's software, keeps a copy of the ledger and checks transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal owner that holds an asset in its name for a beneficial owner and acts only on the beneficial owner’s instructions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal owner that holds an asset in its name for a beneficial owner and acts only on the beneficial owner’s instructions.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, a financial instrument, such as most UCITS, that may be sold on an execution-only basis without assessing the client.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, a financial instrument, such as most UCITS, that may be sold on an execution-only basis without assessing the client. Structured UCITS and most AIFs are complex.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF established outside the EEA.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF established outside the EEA. It may be marketed to EEA investors only under the NPPRs of the relevant Member States, subject to AIFMD conditions, because the third-country passport has not been activated.

concepts.shortDefinition: Non-fungible token: a unique token recording ownership of a specific item or right.
concepts.bodyHtml: Non-fungible token: a unique token recording ownership of a specific item or right. Genuinely unique NFTs are generally outside MiCA.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF that national rules permit to be sold to retail investors, such as an Irish RIAIF or a Luxembourg Part II UCI.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF that national rules permit to be sold to retail investors, such as an Irish RIAIF or a Luxembourg Part II UCI. Also called a non-UCITS retail scheme.

concepts.shortDefinition: The procedure for using a marketing passport: the fund or its manager submits a standard notification file to its home regulator, which checks it and transmits it to each host regulator (within 10 working days for a UCITS and 20 for an AIF).
concepts.bodyHtml: The procedure for using a marketing passport: the fund or its manager submits a standard notification file to its home regulator, which checks it and transmits it to each host regulator (within 10 working days for a UCITS and 20 for an AIF). Marketing may begin once the home regulator confirms transmission.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm subject to AML/CFT law: customer due diligence, monitoring, record keeping and suspicion reporting.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm subject to AML/CFT law: customer due diligence, monitoring, record keeping and suspicion reporting. VASPs and MiCA CASPs are obliged entities.

concepts.shortDefinition: The point where crypto-assets are converted into fiat money, through redemption with an issuer or a sale on an exchange.
concepts.bodyHtml: The point where crypto-assets are converted into fiat money, through redemption with an issuer or a sale on an exchange. Off-ramps are key control points for anti-money-laundering checks.

concepts.shortDefinition: The offering document used for funds marketed by private placement to professional investors, such as hedge and private equity funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: The offering document used for funds marketed by private placement to professional investors, such as hedge and private equity funds. Also called a private placement memorandum.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund centre outside the main onshore markets, such as the Cayman Islands, attractive to some managers for tax neutrality and flexible regulation (see Annex (vi)).
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund centre outside the main onshore markets, such as the Cayman Islands, attractive to some managers for tax neutrality and flexible regulation (see Annex (vi)).

concepts.shortDefinition: An account in which a nominee, such as a platform or distributor, holds units for many underlying investors, so that the fund’s register shows only the nominee.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account in which a nominee, such as a platform or distributor, holds units for many underlying investors, so that the fund’s register shows only the nominee.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet holding the assets of many customers together, with each customer's share recorded on the firm's internal ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet holding the assets of many customers together, with each customer's share recorded on the firm's internal ledger.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recorded on a blockchain (on-chain) or recorded elsewhere (off-chain), such as on a firm's internal ledger or a traditional register.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recorded on a blockchain (on-chain) or recorded elsewhere (off-chain), such as on a firm's internal ledger or a traditional register.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund’s annual operating costs, such as the management fee and service providers’ fees, expressed as a percentage of its average NAV, excluding transaction costs and performance fees.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund’s annual operating costs, such as the management fee and service providers’ fees, expressed as a percentage of its average NAV, excluding transaction costs and performance fees. Sometimes called the TER.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that issues new units or shares when investors subscribe and cancels them when investors redeem, so that its capital varies over time.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that issues new units or shares when investors subscribe and cancels them when investors redeem, so that its capital varies over time. A UCITS must be open-ended.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm’s ability to identify and prepare for, respond to, recover from and learn from operational disruption, so that it can keep providing its important services.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm’s ability to identify and prepare for, respond to, recover from and learn from operational disruption, so that it can keep providing its important services. DORA covers its ICT dimension.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The ability to keep important services within tolerance through disruption: identify services, set tolerances, map dependencies, test severe scenarios.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of loss from inadequate or failed internal processes, people and systems, or from external events, including the failure of service providers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of loss from inadequate or failed internal processes, people and systems, or from external events, including the failure of service providers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A layer 2 that posts transaction data to layer 1 and treats it as valid unless someone proves fraud during a challenge period of about seven days.
concepts.bodyHtml: A layer 2 that posts transaction data to layer 1 and treats it as valid unless someone proves fraud during a challenge period of about seven days.

concepts.shortDefinition: A derivative giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call option) or sell (put option) an asset at a predetermined price (the exercise or strike price) within a set period, in return for a premium.
concepts.bodyHtml: A derivative giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call option) or sell (put option) an asset at a predetermined price (the exercise or strike price) within a set period, in return for a premium.

concepts.shortDefinition: A service that brings outside data, such as prices, onto a blockchain for smart contracts to use.
concepts.bodyHtml: A service that brings outside data, such as prices, onto a blockchain for smart contracts to use. A manipulated oracle can drain a protocol.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of buy and sell orders at different prices, matched by a matching engine.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of buy and sell orders at different prices, matched by a matching engine.

concepts.shortDefinition: A share representing part-ownership of a company, carrying rights to dividends if declared and usually to vote.
concepts.bodyHtml: A share representing part-ownership of a company, carrying rights to dividends if declared and usually to vote. Ordinary shareholders are paid after preferred stockholders and are last to be paid in a liquidation. Also called common stock.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under CP86, the role, taken by an independent director of an Irish FMC, of keeping the FMC’s organisational structure and resources under review.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under CP86, the role, taken by an independent director of an Irish FMC, of keeping the FMC’s organisational structure and resources under review.

concepts.shortDefinition: An over-the-counter broker that negotiates large crypto trades directly between parties, off exchange.
concepts.bodyHtml: An over-the-counter broker that negotiates large crypto trades directly between parties, off exchange. OTC and peer-to-peer desks are common cash-out routes for illicit funds where the client is not properly identified; a UNODC report (January 2024) found USDT on Tron favoured by underground banking networks in East and Southeast Asia.

concepts.shortDefinition: The use of a third party, whether a group company or an external provider, to perform activities that the regulated entity would otherwise perform itself.
concepts.bodyHtml: The use of a third party, whether a group company or an external provider, to perform activities that the regulated entity would otherwise perform itself. It must not impair internal controls or regulatory supervision, and contracts must be in writing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Traded bilaterally between two parties rather than on an exchange or other trading venue.
concepts.bodyHtml: Traded bilaterally between two parties rather than on an exchange or other trading venue. OTC derivatives are subject to EMIR clearing, risk mitigation and reporting requirements.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Trading directly between two parties, or through a broker or desk, rather than on an exchange's order book.

concepts.shortDefinition: Bitcoin output types that put a public key directly on-chain: early pay-to-public-key outputs, and Taproot (2021).
concepts.bodyHtml: Bitcoin output types that put a public key directly on-chain: early pay-to-public-key outputs, and Taproot (2021). Both are exposed to a long-exposure quantum attack.

concepts.term: Packaged retail and insurance-based investment product
concepts.shortDefinition: An investment whose return depends on the performance of underlying assets and that is packaged for retail investors, including UCITS and AIFs, structured products and unit-linked insurance.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment whose return depends on the performance of underlying assets and that is packaged for retail investors, including UCITS and AIFs, structured products and unit-linked insurance. A KID must be provided before a retail investor buys one.
concepts.sortKey: packaged retail and insurance-based investment product

concepts.term: Packaged retail and insurance-based investment products
concepts.sortKey: packaged retail and insurance-based investment products

concepts.shortDefinition: The exclusions applying to EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks, which add to the CTB exclusions companies above set revenue thresholds from coal, oil, gas and carbon-intensive electricity generation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The exclusions applying to EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks, which add to the CTB exclusions companies above set revenue thresholds from coal, oil, gas and carbon-intensive electricity generation. A fund using environmental, impact or sustainability terms in its name must apply them).

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg fund authorised under Part II of the Law of 17 December 2010: an AIF that may be sold to retail investors and is supervised by the CSSF.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg fund authorised under Part II of the Law of 17 December 2010: an AIF that may be sold to retail investors and is supervised by the CSSF. It is the Luxembourg counterpart of the Irish RIAIF.

concepts.shortDefinition: A coin backed partly by reserves and partly by the protocol's own token, such as IRON (about 75% USDC, 25% TITAN).
concepts.bodyHtml: A coin backed partly by reserves and partly by the protocol's own token, such as IRON (about 75% USDC, 25% TITAN). In June 2021 the token part collapsed and holders recovered only the USDC share.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investor’s interest in a limited partnership.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investor’s interest in a limited partnership. LPs do not issue units or shares, but for regulatory purposes partnership interests are treated as units or shares. Also called a participation.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment approach that seeks to track a financial index or other benchmark by holding all or a representative sample of its constituents, or through derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment approach that seeks to track a financial index or other benchmark by holding all or a representative sample of its constituents, or through derivatives.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a fund or manager authorised in one Member State to operate in another without further authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a fund or manager authorised in one Member State to operate in another without further authorisation. UCITS have a product passport and a management company passport; AIFMs have a passport to manage EEA AIFs in other Member States and to market AIFs to professional investors across the EEA.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The right of a firm authorised in one EU member state to serve clients across the EU. Under MiCA, one authority's licensing decision therefore affects every other member state, a point highlighted by ESMA's July 2025 peer review of CASP authorisation in Malta.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund’s historical returns.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund’s historical returns. Marketing communications may show it only on complete 12-month periods, generally for the preceding 10 years, with the statement that past performance does not predict future returns, and a KID must refer to it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A power to stop deposits, withdrawals or trading at once, often skipping the timelock.
concepts.bodyHtml: A power to stop deposits, withdrawals or trading at once, often skipping the timelock. It protects users but can also lock them in.

concepts.shortDefinition: A local agent, formerly required in many host Member States, that made payments to investors and accepted orders.
concepts.bodyHtml: A local agent, formerly required in many host Member States, that made payments to investors and accepted orders. Under the CBDF package a UCITS no longer needs a physical paying agent in each host Member State.

concepts.shortDefinition: The GENIUS Act's term for a token used for payment or settlement that the issuer must redeem for a fixed amount of money.
concepts.bodyHtml: The GENIUS Act's term for a token used for payment or settlement that the issuer must redeem for a fixed amount of money. It excludes national currency, deposits and securities.

concepts.shortDefinition: A large balance moved through a series of hops, shaving off smaller amounts at each one while the change moves on.
concepts.bodyHtml: A large balance moved through a series of hops, shaving off smaller amounts at each one while the change moves on. A classic tracing pattern.

concepts.shortDefinition: Directly between users, without an intermediary.
concepts.bodyHtml: Directly between users, without an intermediary.

concepts.shortDefinition: The peg is the promised fixed value against a reference asset; par is that value — £1 or US$1 per token.
concepts.bodyHtml: The peg is the promised fixed value against a reference asset; par is that value — £1 or US$1 per token. A stablecoin is a promise to pay par, not a property of the token.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, a client automatically treated as a professional client, such as a bank, investment firm, insurer, pension fund or large company.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, a client automatically treated as a professional client, such as a bank, investment firm, insurer, pension fund or large company.

concepts.shortDefinition: The steps, such as registration, needed to make a security interest fully effective against the debtor and third parties – for example registering the creditor as holder of mortgaged shares.
concepts.bodyHtml: The steps, such as registration, needed to make a security interest fully effective against the debtor and third parties – for example registering the creditor as holder of mortgaged shares.

concepts.shortDefinition: A variable fee paid to the manager when a fund’s return exceeds a reference point, such as a benchmark or a high-water mark (the highest NAV previously reached).
concepts.bodyHtml: A variable fee paid to the manager when a fund’s return exceeds a reference point, such as a benchmark or a high-water mark (the highest NAV previously reached). ESMA guidelines require, among other things, that it normally crystallise no more than once a year and that past underperformance be recovered first.

concepts.shortDefinition: The four illustrations in a PRIIPs KID – stress, unfavourable, moderate and favourable – of what an investor might get back after costs at the end of one year and of the RHP, based on past returns).
concepts.bodyHtml: The four illustrations in a PRIIPs KID – stress, unfavourable, moderate and favourable – of what an investor might get back after costs at the end of one year and of the RHP, based on past returns).

concepts.shortDefinition: The boundary of regulation: which activities and firms need a licence.
concepts.bodyHtml: The boundary of regulation: which activities and firms need a licence.

concepts.shortDefinition: The annual and half-yearly reports a fund must publish, containing financial statements, service providers’ reports, investment performance and changes to the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The annual and half-yearly reports a fund must publish, containing financial statements, service providers’ reports, investment performance and changes to the fund. A UCITS publishes its annual report within four months and its half-yearly report within two months; an AIFM’s annual report is due within six months.

concepts.shortDefinition: A blockchain on which only approved participants can validate or, in some cases, read or transact.
concepts.bodyHtml: A blockchain on which only approved participants can validate or, in some cases, read or transact. Participants are known, and governance sits in the rulebook or consortium agreement as well as in the code.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token whose contract lets only approved wallets hold it and lets the issuer freeze, block or recover it — common in tokenised funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token whose contract lets only approved wallets hold it and lets the issuer freeze, block or recover it — common in tokenised funds. Wrapped or bridged versions may lose the restrictions.

concepts.shortDefinition: A blockchain that anyone can join, read, transact on and validate without approval or identity checks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A blockchain that anyone can join, read, transact on and validate without approval or identity checks. There is no single operator to hold to account, so regulation focuses on the firms at the on- and off-ramps.

concepts.shortDefinition: A derivative with no expiry date, kept close to the spot price by periodic funding payments between longs and shorts.
concepts.bodyHtml: A derivative with no expiry date, kept close to the spot price by periodic funding payments between longs and shorts.

concepts.shortDefinition: Tricking someone into revealing credentials or approving a transaction, often through a fake website or message.
concepts.bodyHtml: Tricking someone into revealing credentials or approving a transaction, often through a fake website or message.

concepts.shortDefinition: An index-tracking ETF that holds all, or a representative sample, of the securities in the index.
concepts.bodyHtml: An index-tracking ETF that holds all, or a representative sample, of the securities in the index.

concepts.shortDefinition: A long-running investment-romance scam in which victims are groomed into "investing" in a fake platform.
concepts.bodyHtml: A long-running investment-romance scam in which victims are groomed into "investing" in a fake platform.

concepts.shortDefinition: The first stage of money laundering, in which illicit cash or value enters the financial system.
concepts.bodyHtml: The first stage of money laundering, in which illicit cash or value enters the financial system.

concepts.shortDefinition: The three classic stages of money laundering - getting illicit proceeds into the financial system, moving them to hide their origin, and bringing them back looking clean.
concepts.bodyHtml: The three classic stages of money laundering - getting illicit proceeds into the financial system, moving them to hide their origin, and bringing them back looking clean. On-chain, all three can happen within minutes.

concepts.shortDefinition: An online service through which investors or their advisers buy, hold and sell funds from many managers, often on an execution-only basis.
concepts.bodyHtml: An online service through which investors or their advisers buy, hold and sell funds from many managers, often on an execution-only basis. Units are usually held through a nominee account. Also called a fund supermarket.

concepts.shortDefinition: A form of security in which the creditor takes possession or control of an asset, but not title to it.
concepts.bodyHtml: A form of security in which the creditor takes possession or control of an asset, but not title to it. It is the main form of security over financial assets in Luxembourg and other civil law countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: The rules (limits, whitelists, quorum, screening) that decide whether a transaction may be signed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The rules (limits, whitelists, quorum, screening) that decide whether a transaction may be signed. Whoever administers it can, in effect, sign.

concepts.shortDefinition: Two projects on settling tokenised transactions in central bank money.
concepts.bodyHtml: Two projects on settling tokenised transactions in central bank money. Pontes is the Eurosystem's initiative to link distributed ledger platforms to its payment systems, so that DLT transactions can settle in euro central bank money. Project Agorá, led by the BIS with central banks and commercial banks, explores how tokenised commercial bank deposits and wholesale central bank money can work together on a shared platform for cross-border payments.

concepts.shortDefinition: A company in which a private equity fund invests.
concepts.bodyHtml: A company in which a private equity fund invests.

concepts.shortDefinition: The file an ETF publishes each dealing day listing the basket of securities and cash it will accept or deliver for the creation or redemption of a creation unit.
concepts.bodyHtml: The file an ETF publishes each dealing day listing the basket of securities and cash it will accept or deliver for the creation or redemption of a creation unit.

concepts.shortDefinition: Managing a fund’s investments by deciding which assets to buy, hold and sell.
concepts.bodyHtml: Managing a fund’s investments by deciding which assets to buy, hold and sell. With risk management it makes up investment management; an AIFM must itself perform at least one of the two.

concepts.shortDefinition: Cryptographic algorithms designed to resist attack by quantum computers.
concepts.bodyHtml: Cryptographic algorithms designed to resist attack by quantum computers.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, a senior role, such as director of a fund or FMC or designated person, that may be filled only with the CBI’s prior approval under the fitness and probity regime.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, a senior role, such as director of a fund or FMC or designated person, that may be filled only with the CBI’s prior approval under the fitness and probity regime.

concepts.shortDefinition: The information that must be given to an investor before investing, such as the prospectus or offering memorandum, the PRIIPs KID, the AIFMD Article 23 disclosures and the SFDR pre-contractual template.
concepts.bodyHtml: The information that must be given to an investor before investing, such as the prospectus or offering memorandum, the PRIIPs KID, the AIFMD Article 23 disclosures and the SFDR pre-contractual template.

concepts.shortDefinition: Providing information on investment strategies or ideas to potential professional investors to test their interest in an AIF that is not yet established, or not yet notified for marketing in that Member State.
concepts.bodyHtml: Providing information on investment strategies or ideas to potential professional investors to test their interest in an AIF that is not yet established, or not yet notified for marketing in that Member State. Investors cannot subscribe, and a subscription within 18 months is treated as resulting from marketing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Shares giving holders priority over ordinary shareholders for dividends, often at a fixed rate that is not guaranteed, and for repayment of capital in a liquidation.
concepts.bodyHtml: Shares giving holders priority over ordinary shareholders for dividends, often at a fixed rate that is not guaranteed, and for repayment of capital in a liquidation. Also called preference shares.

concepts.shortDefinition: Primary: minting and redemption with the issuer, by onboarded firms, in banking hours.
concepts.bodyHtml: Primary: minting and redemption with the issuer, by onboarded firms, in banking hours. Secondary: trading among holders on exchanges and on-chain, 24/7. Most holders exit by selling, not redeeming.

concepts.shortDefinition: The market in which securities are first issued, with the proceeds going to the issuer.
concepts.bodyHtml: The market in which securities are first issued, with the proceeds going to the issuer. For an ETF, the primary market is where APs create and redeem shares directly with the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank or broker that provides hedge funds with financing, securities lending, clearing and settlement, and custody of assets used as collateral.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank or broker that provides hedge funds with financing, securities lending, clearing and settlement, and custody of assets used as collateral. For an EEA AIF it acts as a delegate of the fund depositary where it holds the fund’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: The most significant negative effects of investment decisions on sustainability factors, such as greenhouse gas emissions.
concepts.bodyHtml: The most significant negative effects of investment decisions on sustainability factors, such as greenhouse gas emissions. Managers disclose whether they consider them at firm level and for each fund. PAIs look outwards, at the fund’s effect on the environment and society.

concepts.shortDefinition: The manager of a multi-manager fund that selects the sub-managers, allocates mandates among them, monitors their performance and compliance and reviews the fund’s overall strategy.
concepts.bodyHtml: The manager of a multi-manager fund that selects the sub-managers, allocates mandates among them, monitors their performance and compliance and reviews the fund’s overall strategy.

concepts.shortDefinition: The order in which secured creditors are paid from a debtor’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The order in which secured creditors are paid from a debtor’s assets. For registrable security it is usually determined by the order of registration, so failing to register may mean being paid after later creditors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The CBI’s risk-based supervisory framework, which assigns firms an impact rating that determines the intensity of supervision and, for FMCs, stricter director location rules for higher-impact firms.
concepts.bodyHtml: The CBI’s risk-based supervisory framework, which assigns firms an impact rating that determines the intensity of supervision and, for FMCs, stricter director location rules for higher-impact firms.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto asset that hides sender, receiver or amount at protocol level (Monero; Zcash shielded transfers).
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto asset that hides sender, receiver or amount at protocol level (Monero; Zcash shielded transfers). The EU AML Regulation bars CASPs from handling such coins from 10 July 2027.

concepts.shortDefinition: A blockchain on which one organisation controls access and validation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A blockchain on which one organisation controls access and validation. In practice it operates like any other core IT system of that organisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lending to companies by non-bank investors, such as AIFs, either by originating loans directly or by buying existing loans.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lending to companies by non-bank investors, such as AIFs, either by originating loans directly or by buying existing loans. Loans are not securities and are generally illiquid.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund, usually closed-ended and structured as a limited partnership, that invests in unquoted companies (its portfolio companies), often to finance management buyouts or buy-ins, and holds them for several years before exiting.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund, usually closed-ended and structured as a limited partnership, that invests in unquoted companies (its portfolio companies), often to finance management buyouts or buy-ins, and holds them for several years before exiting.

concepts.shortDefinition: The cryptographic key that controls a crypto-asset on a distributed ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: The cryptographic key that controls a crypto-asset on a distributed ledger. Whoever holds it controls the asset, so safekeeping of crypto-assets depends on control of private keys.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A secret number that controls a blockchain address. Whoever holds it can sign transactions and so move the assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Marketing a fund to a limited number of selected, usually professional, investors without a public offering.
concepts.bodyHtml: Marketing a fund to a limited number of selected, usually professional, investors without a public offering.

concepts.shortDefinition: The MiFID II rules requiring the manufacturer of a product, such as a fund manager, to define a target market for it, and distributors to set their own target market and distribution strategy, so that products are sold to the investors for whom they are designed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The MiFID II rules requiring the manufacturer of a product, such as a fund manager, to define a target market for it, and distributors to set their own target market and distribution strategy, so that products are sold to the investors for whom they are designed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The right of a UCITS authorised in one Member State to be marketed to the public in other Member States without further authorisation, following notification.
concepts.bodyHtml: The right of a UCITS authorised in one Member State to be marketed to the public in other Member States without further authorisation, following notification.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investor, such as a bank, insurer, pension scheme, large company or high net worth individual, considered to have the expertise to assess the risks of an investment and therefore given less regulatory protection.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investor, such as a bank, insurer, pension scheme, large company or high net worth individual, considered to have the expertise to assess the risks of an investment and therefore given less regulatory protection. Under MiFID II some are professional clients per se and others may elect to be treated as professional clients.

concepts.shortDefinition: Financing weapons of mass destruction and their delivery; countering it is the 'CPF' in AML/CFT/CPF.
concepts.bodyHtml: Financing weapons of mass destruction and their delivery; countering it is the 'CPF' in AML/CFT/CPF. Sanctions freezing is strict (FATF R.7); since October 2020 R.1 and R.2 also require a PF risk assessment.

concepts.shortDefinition: Hidden instructions in a web page, message or data feed that steer an AI agent, for example to pay a different address.
concepts.bodyHtml: Hidden instructions in a web page, message or data feed that steer an AI agent, for example to pay a different address.

concepts.shortDefinition: Demonstrating control of a wallet by signing a message chosen by the person checking.
concepts.bodyHtml: Demonstrating control of a wallet by signing a message chosen by the person checking. It proves that the firm can sign with the key, not who owns the assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A public demonstration, often using a Merkle tree, that a platform holds assets at least equal to customer balances at a point in time.
concepts.bodyHtml: A public demonstration, often using a Merkle tree, that a platform holds assets at least equal to customer balances at a point in time. It does not show liabilities in full.

concepts.shortDefinition: A consensus mechanism in which validators lock up (stake) coins for the right to propose and attest to blocks, and can lose them for misbehaving.
concepts.bodyHtml: A consensus mechanism in which validators lock up (stake) coins for the right to propose and attest to blocks, and can lose them for misbehaving.

concepts.shortDefinition: A consensus mechanism in which miners compete to solve computational puzzles to add blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: A consensus mechanism in which miners compete to solve computational puzzles to add blocks.

concepts.shortDefinition: The authenticated instructions, defined in the depositary agreement, on which the fund depositary may act to move a fund’s assets and cash.
concepts.bodyHtml: The authenticated instructions, defined in the depositary agreement, on which the fund depositary may act to move a fund’s assets and cash.

concepts.shortDefinition: Scaling regulatory requirements to a firm's size, clients and complexity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Scaling regulatory requirements to a firm's size, clients and complexity. Proportionality changes how much evidence or capital is required, not whether a risk must be controlled.

concepts.shortDefinition: A ManCo set up by a fund promoter within its own group to manage the group’s own funds, usually delegating portfolio management to a group investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: A ManCo set up by a fund promoter within its own group to manage the group’s own funds, usually delegating portfolio management to a group investment manager. Sometimes called a group ManCo.

concepts.shortDefinition: The regulator-approved document setting out the details of a fund, including its objective and policies, restrictions, fees, service providers, dealing arrangements, risks and LMTs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The regulator-approved document setting out the details of a fund, including its objective and policies, restrictions, fees, service providers, dealing arrangements, risks and LMTs. It is the main document for investors deciding whether to invest and the rulebook for the fund’s operation.

concepts.shortDefinition: A document setting out the features specific to one sub-fund of an umbrella fund, read together with the core prospectus.
concepts.bodyHtml: A document setting out the features specific to one sub-fund of an umbrella fund, read together with the core prospectus.

concepts.shortDefinition: A company whose assets and liabilities are divided into legally segregated cells, so that the liabilities of one cell cannot be met from the assets of another.
concepts.bodyHtml: A company whose assets and liabilities are divided into legally segregated cells, so that the liabilities of one cell cannot be met from the assets of another. Widely used for insurance and investment fund structures.

concepts.shortDefinition: Voting at a company’s general meeting by instructing another person (a proxy) to vote on the shareholder’s behalf.
concepts.bodyHtml: Voting at a company’s general meeting by instructing another person (a proxy) to vote on the shareholder’s behalf. It is how funds usually exercise their voting rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: A public chain lets anyone run a node and transact; a permissioned ledger limits who can take part.
concepts.bodyHtml: A public chain lets anyone run a node and transact; a permissioned ledger limits who can take part. Regulated tokens on public chains usually restrict holders through a whitelist.

concepts.shortDefinition: A key derived from the private key that others use to verify signatures.
concepts.bodyHtml: A key derived from the private key that others use to verify signatures. Addresses are derived from it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Inflating a token's price through promotion or fake volume, then selling to the buyers drawn in.
concepts.bodyHtml: Inflating a token's price through promotion or fake volume, then selling to the buyers drawn in. A rug pull is a related fraud in which a project team raises money, drains the liquidity and disappears.

concepts.shortDefinition: Shorthand for the day a quantum computer can break today's public-key cryptography.
concepts.bodyHtml: Shorthand for the day a quantum computer can break today's public-key cryptography. Nobody can date it.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Ireland, an investor eligible to invest in a QIAIF, such as a professional investor or an informed investor, who must generally subscribe at least €100,000.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Ireland, an investor eligible to invest in a QIAIF, such as a professional investor or an informed investor, who must generally subscribe at least €100,000.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish AIF reserved for qualifying investors subscribing at least €100,000.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish AIF reserved for qualifying investors subscribing at least €100,000. It is largely free of CBI investment and borrowing restrictions and can be authorised on a fast-track basis on the business day after filing.

concepts.notes: former name of the Irish QIAIF

concepts.shortDefinition: The UK FSMA regime's term for a cryptoasset seeking a stable value by reference to fiat, with the issuer holding backing assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The UK FSMA regime's term for a cryptoasset seeking a stable value by reference to fiat, with the issuer holding backing assets. Systemic coins are also regulated by the Bank of England.

concepts.shortDefinition: An LMT that limits or alters investors’ redemptions: a redemption gate, an extension of the notice period or redemption in kind.
concepts.bodyHtml: An LMT that limits or alters investors’ redemptions: a redemption gate, an extension of the notice period or redemption in kind. ESMA guidelines recommend that managers select at least one.

concepts.shortDefinition: Computing that uses quantum effects.
concepts.bodyHtml: Computing that uses quantum effects. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break the signature schemes used by most blockchains today.

concepts.shortDefinition: The basic unit of a quantum computer.
concepts.bodyHtml: The basic unit of a quantum computer. Many noisy physical qubits are combined, by error correction, into each reliable logical qubit.

concepts.shortDefinition: Physical assets with intrinsic worth, such as real estate, land, commodities, precious metals, equipment and natural resources.
concepts.bodyHtml: Physical assets with intrinsic worth, such as real estate, land, commodities, precious metals, equipment and natural resources. They are generally less liquid than securities. UCITS may not invest in them directly.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund that invests in, or obtains exposure to, property, directly, through property companies or synthetically through derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund that invests in, or obtains exposure to, property, directly, through property companies or synthetically through derivatives. Because property is illiquid, open-ended real estate funds face a liquidity mismatch.

concepts.shortDefinition: A listed company or fund that invests mainly in income-producing property and qualifies for special tax treatment if it meets conditions on its assets, sources of profit and distribution of income.
concepts.bodyHtml: A listed company or fund that invests mainly in income-producing property and qualifies for special tax treatment if it meets conditions on its assets, sources of profit and distribution of income.

concepts.shortDefinition: A traditional asset, such as a bond, fund, property or commodity, represented by a token.
concepts.bodyHtml: A traditional asset, such as a bond, fund, property or commodity, represented by a token.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person, usually an accountant, appointed by a secured creditor to take possession of and sell secured property to repay the debt owed to that creditor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person, usually an accountant, appointed by a secured creditor to take possession of and sell secured property to repay the debt owed to that creditor. A receiver is distinct from a liquidator.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum period for which an investor is advised to hold an investment to have a reasonable prospect of achieving its objective.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum period for which an investor is advised to hold an investment to have a reasonable prospect of achieving its objective. For a fund it is usually several years, and it is stated in the PRIIPs KID.

concepts.shortDefinition: Checking that two records agree.
concepts.bodyHtml: Checking that two records agree. For a crypto firm, this means its books, its customers' balances and the assets held on-chain.

concepts.shortDefinition: A difference between the blockchain, the register and the cash or assets.
