concepts.bodyHtml: A difference between the blockchain, the register and the cash or assets. Each break needs to be explained and resolved; tokens without backing dilute other holders.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which an investor in an open-ended fund sells units or shares back to the fund and receives their current value, usually in cash; the units or shares are then cancelled.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which an investor in an open-ended fund sells units or shares back to the fund and receives their current value, usually in cash; the units or shares are then cancelled.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Exchanging a token for the underlying asset or money from the issuer, for example a stablecoin for dollars at par.

concepts.shortDefinition: A pre-set fee paid into the fund by redeeming investors to cover the dealing costs their redemptions cause.
concepts.bodyHtml: A pre-set fee paid into the fund by redeeming investors to cover the dealing costs their redemptions cause. It is an anti-dilution LMT.

concepts.shortDefinition: An LMT that temporarily limits redemptions on a dealing day to a set percentage of the fund (often 10%), scaling back all requests pro rata and carrying the balance forward.
concepts.bodyHtml: An LMT that temporarily limits redemptions on a dealing day to a set percentage of the fund (often 10%), scaling back all requests pro rata and carrying the balance forward. Unlike a suspension, the fund continues to deal.

concepts.shortDefinition: Meeting a redemption by transferring the investor’s pro rata share of the fund’s assets instead of cash.
concepts.bodyHtml: Meeting a redemption by transferring the investor’s pro rata share of the fund’s assets instead of cash. Also called an in specie redemption, it is usually limited to professional investors; subscriptions may likewise be made in specie.

concepts.shortDefinition: The record that decides legal ownership.
concepts.bodyHtml: The record that decides legal ownership. It may be on-chain, off-chain with an on-chain mirror, or hybrid; the documents must name it and say how it is corrected.

concepts.shortDefinition: The register that UCITS ManCos and AIFMs must keep under DORA of all their contracts with ICT third-party service providers, which is submitted to the regulator.
concepts.bodyHtml: The register that UCITS ManCos and AIFMs must keep under DORA of all their contracts with ICT third-party service providers, which is submitted to the regulator.

concepts.shortDefinition: The register of unitholders or shareholders that records who owns a fund’s units or shares.
concepts.bodyHtml: The register of unitholders or shareholders that records who owns a fund’s units or shares. It is maintained by the TA and may be kept using DLT; the register shows the legal owner, which may be a nominee.

concepts.shortDefinition: The person named in the terms of a tokenised security, or in law, who keeps its register of holders and can correct it.
concepts.bodyHtml: The person named in the terms of a tokenised security, or in law, who keeps its register of holders and can correct it.

concepts.shortDefinition: Recording a security interest on a public or other register to give notice of it, to complete the creditor’s title or to establish priority.
concepts.bodyHtml: Recording a security interest on a public or other register to give notice of it, to complete the creditor’s title or to establish priority. Most charges created by an Irish company must be registered with the Companies Registration Office (or, for an ICAV, the CBI) within 21 days.

concepts.shortDefinition: A multilateral trading system authorised under MiFID II and operated by a market operator, such as a stock exchange’s main market.
concepts.bodyHtml: A multilateral trading system authorised under MiFID II and operated by a market operator, such as a stock exchange’s main market. SRD II applies to asset managers investing in shares traded on an EEA regulated market.

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU legislative act that applies directly in all Member States without transposition, such as the MMFR, the PRIIPs Regulation, SFDR and DORA.
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU legislative act that applies directly in all Member States without transposition, such as the MMFR, the PRIIPs Regulation, SFDR and DORA.

concepts.shortDefinition: Locating or booking an activity wherever the rules or supervision are lightest.
concepts.bodyHtml: Locating or booking an activity wherever the rules or supervision are lightest. Uneven implementation of international standards across countries creates the opportunity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The minimum financial resources (own funds) that a ManCo or AIFM must hold under regulation, partly to cover liability risks.
concepts.bodyHtml: The minimum financial resources (own funds) that a ManCo or AIFM must hold under regulation, partly to cover liability risks. An AIFM must also hold additional own funds or professional indemnity insurance.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk of failing to identify and comply with the regulatory requirements of each market in which a fund or manager operates, or of failing to adapt to new regulation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk of failing to identify and comply with the regulatory requirements of each market in which a fund or manager operates, or of failing to adapt to new regulation.

concepts.shortDefinition: Detailed technical rules drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as delegated regulations, for example on LMTs, loan origination, ELTIFs and the SFDR templates.
concepts.bodyHtml: Detailed technical rules drafted by an ESA and adopted by the Commission as delegated regulations, for example on LMTs, loan origination, ELTIFs and the SFDR templates.

concepts.shortDefinition: Re-using assets received as collateral, or held for clients, for the firm's own purposes such as lending.
concepts.bodyHtml: Re-using assets received as collateral, or held for clients, for the firm's own purposes such as lending.

concepts.shortDefinition: A person or firm connected to a firm or its owners, such as a founder's own project or token.
concepts.bodyHtml: A person or firm connected to a firm or its owners, such as a founder's own project or token. Dealings with related parties need independent approval and disclosure.

concepts.shortDefinition: The policy that UCITS ManCos and AIFMs must have for the pay of their key staff, consistent with sound risk management and not encouraging excessive risk-taking.
concepts.bodyHtml: The policy that UCITS ManCos and AIFMs must have for the pay of their key staff, consistent with sound risk management and not encouraging excessive risk-taking.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction in which a fund sells securities and agrees to buy them back at a set price on a future date, in effect borrowing cash against the securities.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction in which a fund sells securities and agrees to buy them back at a set price on a future date, in effect borrowing cash against the securities.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that investors lose confidence in a fund or its manager and redeem their holdings, for example after errors, breaches or misconduct.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that investors lose confidence in a fund or its manager and redeem their holdings, for example after errors, breaches or misconduct.

concepts.shortDefinition: A stablecoin issuer's board-approved policy setting eligible reserve assets, liquidity tiers, maturities, concentration limits, encumbrance, segregation, reconciliation and governance.
concepts.bodyHtml: A stablecoin issuer's board-approved policy setting eligible reserve assets, liquidity tiers, maturities, concentration limits, encumbrance, segregation, reconciliation and governance.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors that does not require CSSF approval but must be managed by an authorised EEA AIFM.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors that does not require CSSF approval but must be managed by an authorised EEA AIFM. Its offering document must state that it is not supervised in Luxembourg.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk that remains after controls are applied.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk that remains after controls are applied. Credit for controls depends on evidence that they work.

concepts.shortDefinition: Re-using staked assets, or liquid staking tokens, to secure additional services, in return for extra rewards and extra slashing risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: Re-using staked assets, or liquid staking tokens, to secure additional services, in return for extra rewards and extra slashing risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: An EU legislative package, politically agreed on 18 December 2025 but not yet applicable, that would strengthen VfM requirements, revise the inducement rules and amend the PRIIPs KID.
concepts.bodyHtml: An EU legislative package, politically agreed on 18 December 2025 but not yet applicable, that would strengthen VfM requirements, revise the inducement rules and amend the PRIIPs KID.

concepts.shortDefinition: A member of the general public investing on their own account.
concepts.bodyHtml: A member of the general public investing on their own account. Retail investors receive the highest level of regulatory protection and may usually subscribe freely only to more tightly regulated funds, such as UCITS.

concepts.shortDefinition: An Irish AIF that may be sold to retail investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: An Irish AIF that may be sold to retail investors. It is subject to CBI investment and borrowing restrictions that are less onerous than those for UCITS, and must be managed by an authorised AIFM. Luxembourg’s equivalent is the Part II UCI.

concepts.shortDefinition: The use by a recipient, for its own account, of assets it has received as collateral or holds for a client, such as a prime broker reusing a hedge fund’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The use by a recipient, for its own account, of assets it has received as collateral or holds for a client, such as a prime broker reusing a hedge fund’s assets. Under the SFTR it requires the provider’s prior consent, and a fund must disclose any such right.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction in which a fund buys securities and agrees to sell them back at a set price on a future date, in effect lending cash against collateral.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction in which a fund buys securities and agrees to sell them back at a set price on a future date, in effect lending cash against collateral.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment made at the investor’s own exclusive initiative, without marketing by the manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment made at the investor’s own exclusive initiative, without marketing by the manager. It is not marketing, so no notification is needed, but regulators interpret it narrowly.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: Serving a client at the client's own exclusive initiative. Under MiCA Article 61 and ESMA's guidelines (December 2024), any solicitation by the firm defeats it, and the firm must be able to evidence that the client approached it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The withdrawal of a fund’s regulatory authorisation by its regulator, usually on application once all its assets have been returned to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The withdrawal of a fund’s regulatory authorisation by its regulator, usually on application once all its assets have been returned to investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: Returns paid to holders of a stablecoin, usually by platforms out of the income earned on the reserves.
concepts.bodyHtml: Returns paid to holders of a stablecoin, usually by platforms out of the income earned on the reserves. Many regimes prohibit stablecoin issuers from paying interest to holders, while rewards offered by third parties such as exchanges are more contested. Paying yield on a payment stablecoin can change its regulatory character.

concepts.shortDefinition: An offer by a company to its existing shareholders of the right to buy new shares in proportion to their holdings, usually at a discount.
concepts.bodyHtml: An offer by a company to its existing shareholders of the right to buy new shares in proportion to their holdings, usually at a discount. It is a voluntary corporate action.

concepts.shortDefinition: Keeping a fund’s assets identifiable and separate from the assets of the entity holding them, such as the fund depositary, so that they are protected if that entity becomes insolvent.
concepts.bodyHtml: Keeping a fund’s assets identifiable and separate from the assets of the entity holding them, such as the fund depositary, so that they are protected if that entity becomes insolvent.

concepts.shortDefinition: The combination of the return a fund targets and the level of investment risk it takes to achieve it, which drives its asset selection and target market.
concepts.bodyHtml: The combination of the return a fund targets and the level of investment risk it takes to achieve it, which drives its asset selection and target market.

concepts.shortDefinition: A board's statement of how much risk the firm is willing to take, with limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: A board's statement of how much risk the firm is willing to take, with limits. Limits that are routinely breached and waived without escalation suggest the appetite is not being applied.

concepts.shortDefinition: Investment in entities to support their launch, development or listing, such as private equity and venture capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: Investment in entities to support their launch, development or listing, such as private equity and venture capital. A SICAR invests exclusively in risk capital, and a RAIF that does so is not subject to risk-spreading.

concepts.shortDefinition: The function that identifies, measures, monitors and manages the risks to which a fund is exposed, such as market, liquidity, credit and counterparty risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: The function that identifies, measures, monitors and manages the risks to which a fund is exposed, such as market, liquidity, credit and counterparty risk. It must be independent of portfolio management, in some cases functionally and hierarchically.

concepts.shortDefinition: The AIFMD II requirement that an AIF retain 5% of the notional value of each loan it originates and then transfers, generally until maturity for loans of up to eight years and for at least eight years otherwise.
concepts.bodyHtml: The AIFMD II requirement that an AIF retain 5% of the notional value of each loan it originates and then transfers, generally until maturity for loans of up to eight years and for at least eight years otherwise.

concepts.shortDefinition: An overnight interest rate benchmark based on actual transactions, such as €STR (euro), SONIA (sterling) and SOFR (US dollar), which has replaced interbank offered rates such as LIBOR in derivatives and loans.
concepts.bodyHtml: An overnight interest rate benchmark based on actual transactions, such as €STR (euro), SONIA (sterling) and SOFR (US dollar), which has replaced interbank offered rates such as LIBOR in derivatives and loans.

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle, applied to Luxembourg Part II funds, SIFs and RAIFs, that a fund must diversify its investments, under rules less stringent than the UCITS diversification limits.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle, applied to Luxembourg Part II funds, SIFs and RAIFs, that a fund must diversify its investments, under rules less stringent than the UCITS diversification limits.

concepts.shortDefinition: A layer 2 that executes transactions off the main chain and posts compressed data and proofs back to it.
concepts.bodyHtml: A layer 2 that executes transactions off the main chain and posts compressed data and proofs back to it. Optimistic rollups rely on a challenge window; zero-knowledge rollups post validity proofs.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fraud in which the developers of a token or protocol take the investors' funds and disappear.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fraud in which the developers of a token or protocol take the investors' funds and disappear.

concepts.shortDefinition: The fund depositary’s duty to hold in custody all financial instruments that can be held in custody and, for other assets, to verify the fund’s ownership and keep a record.
concepts.bodyHtml: The fund depositary’s duty to hold in custody all financial instruments that can be held in custody and, for other assets, to verify the fund’s ownership and keep a record. The fund depositary may delegate custody to a sub-custodian but remains liable for the assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Good-practice custody rule: customer assets identifiable and recorded in the customer's name, with no use or lending without explicit, prior, written consent (and collateral for lending).
concepts.bodyHtml: Good-practice custody rule: customer assets identifiable and recorded in the customer's name, with no use or lending without explicit, prior, written consent (and collateral for lending).

concepts.term: Same activity, same risk, same regulation
concepts.shortDefinition: Equivalent activities face equivalent requirements, whatever the label or technology.
concepts.bodyHtml: Equivalent activities face equivalent requirements, whatever the label or technology. The language of the FSB and IOSCO; it stops a race to the bottom between centres.
concepts.sortKey: same activity, same risk, same regulation

concepts.shortDefinition: Restrictive measures imposed by the EU, the UN or other authorities against countries, entities or persons.
concepts.bodyHtml: Restrictive measures imposed by the EU, the UN or other authorities against countries, entities or persons. A fund must not make assets available to, or deal with, sanctioned persons, so investors, counterparties and investments are screened and holdings may have to be frozen.

concepts.shortDefinition: A compromise between a company and its creditors, approved by the court, that binds all creditors.
concepts.bodyHtml: A compromise between a company and its creditors, approved by the court, that binds all creditors. In Irish examinership the examiner prepares one for the company’s survival.

concepts.term: SCS (société en commandite simple) and SCSp (société en commandite spéciale)
concepts.shortDefinition: The Luxembourg limited partnership vehicles used for AIFs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Luxembourg limited partnership vehicles used for AIFs. The SCS has legal personality; the SCSp does not. The SCSp is widely used for private equity, real estate and infrastructure funds, either unregulated or as a RAIF, SIF, Part II UCI or SICAR.
concepts.sortKey: scs (société en commandite simple) and scsp (société en commandite spéciale)

concepts.shortDefinition: A private equity fund that buys existing interests in other private equity funds from investors wishing to sell them.
concepts.bodyHtml: A private equity fund that buys existing interests in other private equity funds from investors wishing to sell them.

concepts.shortDefinition: The market in which securities are traded between investors after they have been issued, providing liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: The market in which securities are traded between investors after they have been issued, providing liquidity. ETF shares are traded on the secondary market on exchanges or OTC.

concepts.shortDefinition: A transaction in which securities are used to borrow cash or other securities, such as securities lending, repo and reverse repo transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: A transaction in which securities are used to borrow cash or other securities, such as securities lending, repo and reverse repo transactions.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2015/2365, which requires securities lending, repo and similar transactions to be reported to a trade repository (for funds, by the ManCo or AIFM), their use to be disclosed in the prospectus and periodic reports, and collateral to be re-used only with prior consent.
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2015/2365, which requires securities lending, repo and similar transactions to be reported to a trade repository (for funds, by the ManCo or AIFM), their use to be disclosed in the prospectus and periodic reports, and collateral to be re-used only with prior consent.

concepts.shortDefinition: Lending securities from a fund’s portfolio to a borrower, such as a bank or broker, for a fee, against collateral worth more than the securities lent.
concepts.bodyHtml: Lending securities from a fund’s portfolio to a borrower, such as a bank or broker, for a fee, against collateral worth more than the securities lent.

concepts.shortDefinition: A financial instrument, such as a share or bond, issued by a company, financial institution or government to raise capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: A financial instrument, such as a share or bond, issued by a company, financial institution or government to raise capital.

concepts.shortDefinition: A right given to a creditor over a debtor’s asset to secure payment of a debt, allowing the creditor to look to the asset if the debt is not paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: A right given to a creditor over a debtor’s asset to secure payment of a debt, allowing the creditor to look to the asset if the debt is not paid. Common forms are the mortgage, charge, pledge and lien.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token carrying share, debt or derivative rights.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token carrying share, debt or derivative rights. It is a security under securities law, whatever it is called; in the EU, MiCA excludes financial instruments.

concepts.shortDefinition: Money committed by seed investors, often the promoter itself, to a new fund at launch so that it can begin investing and grow to a viable size.
concepts.bodyHtml: Money committed by seed investors, often the promoter itself, to a new fund at launch so that it can begin investing and grow to a viable size. Seed investors may receive a seed or founder share class on favourable terms.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of 12 or 24 words from which a wallet's private keys can be regenerated.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of 12 or 24 words from which a wallet's private keys can be regenerated. Whoever has it controls the wallet.

concepts.shortDefinition: The statutory principle, in Ireland and Luxembourg, that the liabilities of one sub-fund of an umbrella can be met only out of that sub-fund’s assets and not those of other sub-funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: The statutory principle, in Ireland and Luxembourg, that the liabilities of one sub-fund of an umbrella can be met only out of that sub-fund’s assets and not those of other sub-funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: Keeping client assets separate from a firm's own assets, both in the records and, ideally, in separate wallets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Keeping client assets separate from a firm's own assets, both in the records and, ideally, in separate wallets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Holding reserves apart from the issuer's own assets, on trust for holders, so that they go to holders if the issuer fails.
concepts.bodyHtml: Holding reserves apart from the issuer's own assets, on trust for holders, so that they go to holders if the issuer fails. The FCA requires a statutory trust.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet whose keys are held by the user, not by a service provider.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet whose keys are held by the user, not by a service provider. Transfers to and from self-hosted wallets are subject to risk-based anti-money-laundering controls under the Travel Rule.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate ManCo and is itself authorised as, and subject to the rules for, a ManCo.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate ManCo and is itself authorised as, and subject to the rules for, a ManCo. Also called an internally managed fund; a corporate fund of this type is known as a self-managed investment company (SMIC). Self-management is now uncommon.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate ManCo and is itself authorised and regulated as a ManCo.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund that has not appointed a separate ManCo and is itself authorised and regulated as a ManCo. Such funds are now uncommon.

concepts.shortDefinition: The element of the Irish IAF that requires firms to map responsibilities to senior individuals.
concepts.bodyHtml: The element of the Irish IAF that requires firms to map responsibilities to senior individuals. It has applied since 1 July 2024 only to credit institutions, insurers and certain investment firms, not to FMCs.

concepts.shortDefinition: The individuals who effectively conduct a ManCo’s business.
concepts.bodyHtml: The individuals who effectively conduct a ManCo’s business. They must be of good repute and sufficiently experienced, and since 16 April 2026 at least two must be employed or engaged full-time and resident in the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bespoke arrangement, usually for an institutional investor, under which a manager manages assets for that investor alone rather than pooling them in a fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bespoke arrangement, usually for an institutional investor, under which a manager manages assets for that investor alone rather than pooling them in a fund. Also called a segregated mandate.

concepts.shortDefinition: The operator that orders transactions on a layer 2.
concepts.bodyHtml: The operator that orders transactions on a layer 2. A single sequencer is a central point of control and failure.

concepts.shortDefinition: A third party appointed by a fund or its ManCo to perform tasks supporting its management, administration or marketing, such as the administrator, TA, distributor, external valuer or auditor.
concepts.bodyHtml: A third party appointed by a fund or its ManCo to perform tasks supporting its management, administration or marketing, such as the administrator, TA, distributor, external valuer or auditor.

concepts.shortDefinition: The counterbalancing of mutual debts between two parties so that only the net amount is payable.
concepts.bodyHtml: The counterbalancing of mutual debts between two parties so that only the net amount is payable. It may arise by contract or by implication and can operate like a form of security. In derivatives it is often called netting, and the Irish Netting of Financial Contracts Act 1995 preserves contractual netting in an insolvency.

concepts.shortDefinition: The completion of a transaction by the exchange of cash for securities or for units or shares.
concepts.bodyHtml: The completion of a transaction by the exchange of cash for securities or for units or shares. EU securities trades on trading venues settle two business days after the trade (T+2) until 11 October 2027, when the cycle shortens to one (T+1).

concepts.shortDefinition: The point at which a transfer cannot be reversed.
concepts.bodyHtml: The point at which a transfer cannot be reversed. On public blockchains it is probabilistic or protocol-defined, not legal.

concepts.shortDefinition: The European Commission’s proposal of 20 November 2025, not yet law, to revise SFDR by replacing Articles 8 and 9 with three product categories – “transition”, “ESG basics” and “sustainable” – each requiring at least 70% of investments to meet the category’s objective).
concepts.bodyHtml: The European Commission’s proposal of 20 November 2025, not yet law, to revise SFDR by replacing Articles 8 and 9 with three product categories – “transition”, “ESG basics” and “sustainable” – each requiring at least 70% of investments to meet the category’s objective).

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard disclosure templates in the SFDR Delegated Regulation: pre-contractual templates annexed to the prospectus of Article 8 and 9 funds (Annexes II and III) and periodic templates included in their annual reports (Annexes IV and V), applying since 1 January 2023.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard disclosure templates in the SFDR Delegated Regulation: pre-contractual templates annexed to the prospectus of Article 8 and 9 funds (Annexes II and III) and periodic templates included in their annual reports (Annexes IV and V), applying since 1 January 2023.

concepts.shortDefinition: A category of units or shares in the same fund or sub-fund, sharing the same portfolio but differing in features such as currency, fees, minimum investment, investor type or distribution policy.
concepts.bodyHtml: A category of units or shares in the same fund or sub-fund, sharing the same portfolio but differing in features such as currency, fees, minimum investment, investor type or distribution policy. Assets are not segregated between share classes.

concepts.shortDefinition: The four principles in ESMA’s opinion on UCITS share classes: a common investment objective reflected by a common pool of assets; non-contagion between classes; pre-determination of all features before a class is set up; and transparency of differences between classes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The four principles in ESMA’s opinion on UCITS share classes: a common investment objective reflected by a common pool of assets; non-contagion between classes; pre-determination of all features before a class is set up; and transparency of differences between classes. Share classes may hedge only currency risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU directive that requires asset managers investing in shares traded on EEA regulated markets to publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis and report annually on how they have applied it, including how they voted.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU directive that requires asset managers investing in shares traded on EEA regulated markets to publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis and report annually on how they have applied it, including how they voted.

concepts.shortDefinition: A quantum algorithm that would break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, letting an attacker derive a private key from a public key.
concepts.bodyHtml: A quantum algorithm that would break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, letting an attacker derive a private key from a public key.

concepts.shortDefinition: Selling an asset the seller does not own, usually by borrowing it, in the expectation of buying it back later at a lower price.
concepts.bodyHtml: Selling an asset the seller does not own, usually by borrowing it, in the expectation of buying it back later at a lower price. In the EU it is governed by the Short Selling Regulation. A UCITS may not short sell physically and can obtain short exposure only through derivatives.

concepts.shortDefinition: The EU regulation governing short selling of shares and sovereign debt, which requires significant net short positions to be reported to regulators and, for shares, larger ones to be disclosed publicly.
concepts.bodyHtml: The EU regulation governing short selling of shares and sovereign debt, which requires significant net short positions to be reported to regulators and, for shares, larger ones to be disclosed publicly.

concepts.shortDefinition: An MMF whose portfolio must have a WAM of no more than 60 days and a WAL of no more than 120 days.
concepts.bodyHtml: An MMF whose portfolio must have a WAM of no more than 60 days and a WAL of no more than 120 days. It may be a public debt CNAV, LVNAV or VNAV MMF.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg corporate fund with fixed capital.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg corporate fund with fixed capital. It cannot be a UCITS.

concepts.term: SICAR (société d’investissement en capital à risque)
aliases: société d’investissement en capital à risque
concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg vehicle for investment in risk capital, such as private equity and venture capital, reserved for well-informed investors and requiring CSSF approval.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg vehicle for investment in risk capital, such as private equity and venture capital, reserved for well-informed investors and requiring CSSF approval. It is not subject to risk-spreading.
concepts.sortKey: sicar (société d’investissement en capital à risque)

concepts.shortDefinition: The main Luxembourg corporate fund, whose capital always equals its net assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The main Luxembourg corporate fund, whose capital always equals its net assets. It can be a UCITS, a Part II fund, a SIF or a RAIF, may be self-managed or appoint a ManCo or AIFM, and may be an umbrella with segregated compartments.

concepts.shortDefinition: An agreement between a fund or its manager and a particular investor giving that investor terms different from those of other investors, for example on fees or reporting.
concepts.bodyHtml: An agreement between a fund or its manager and a particular investor giving that investor terms different from those of other investors, for example on fees or reporting. The revised AIF Rulebook requires side letters to be disclosed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The separation, in exceptional circumstances, of assets that have become illiquid or hard to value, or whose legal or economic features have changed significantly, from the rest of a fund’s assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: The separation, in exceptional circumstances, of assets that have become illiquid or hard to value, or whose legal or economic features have changed significantly, from the rest of a fund’s assets. It is an LMT available to AIFs, including Irish RIAIFs, but not to UCITS.

concepts.shortDefinition: Fund tools that separate illiquid assets or limit redemptions in stress.
concepts.bodyHtml: Fund tools that separate illiquid assets or limit redemptions in stress. Without them, early redeemers leave others holding the illiquid assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A separate chain with its own validators, linked to a main chain by a bridge (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A separate chain with its own validators, linked to a main chain by a bridge (e.g. Polygon PoS, Liquid). Not a true layer 2.

concepts.shortDefinition: Dealing at one price for both subscriptions and redemptions, usually based on mid-market asset values.
concepts.bodyHtml: Dealing at one price for both subscriptions and redemptions, usually based on mid-market asset values.

concepts.shortDefinition: A review by an independent expert, required by a regulator, to examine an issue at a firm, make recommendations and oversee their implementation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A review by an independent expert, required by a regulator, to examine an issue at a firm, make recommendations and oversee their implementation. In the UK, the FCA can require one under section 166 of FSMA.

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of stake, the destruction of part of a validator's stake as a penalty for provably dishonest behaviour, such as double signing.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of stake, the destruction of part of a validator's stake as a penalty for provably dishonest behaviour, such as double signing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Code deployed on a blockchain that runs automatically when called and that can hold and move assets.
concepts.bodyHtml: Code deployed on a blockchain that runs automatically when called and that can hold and move assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: Independent assurance reports on a service provider's controls.
concepts.bodyHtml: Independent assurance reports on a service provider's controls. SOC 1 covers controls relevant to financial reporting; SOC 2 covers security and availability. A Type I report covers the design of controls at a date; a Type II report tests how they operated over a period.

concepts.shortDefinition: Manipulating people — fake recruiters, support calls, phishing, bribes — to gain access.
concepts.bodyHtml: Manipulating people — fake recruiters, support calls, phishing, bribes — to gain access. The usual first step in large thefts.

concepts.shortDefinition: A wallet app on a phone or computer that holds the key, often with an encrypted cloud backup.
concepts.bodyHtml: A wallet app on a phone or computer that holds the key, often with an encrypted cloud backup. Because the device is online, it is normally a hot wallet.

concepts.shortDefinition: A non-transferable token tied to a wallet, used as a badge or credential.
concepts.bodyHtml: A non-transferable token tied to a wallet, used as a badge or credential. Public, permanent and hard to revoke.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal entity set up for a specific, limited purpose, such as holding an investment or originating loans, often used by AIFs to structure investments.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal entity set up for a specific, limited purpose, such as holding an investment or originating loans, often used by AIFs to structure investments.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A company set up to hold an asset; tokens are often shares in, or claims on, the SPV rather than the asset itself.

concepts.shortDefinition: A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors, with no restriction on eligible assets but subject to risk-spreading, which requires prior CSSF approval.
concepts.bodyHtml: A Luxembourg AIF reserved for well-informed investors, with no restriction on eligible assets but subject to risk-spreading, which requires prior CSSF approval.

concepts.shortDefinition: A court order requiring a party to carry out its obligations under a contract as agreed.
concepts.bodyHtml: A court order requiring a party to carry out its obligations under a contract as agreed.

concepts.shortDefinition: The gap between the price charged and a reference mid-price.
concepts.bodyHtml: The gap between the price charged and a reference mid-price. "Zero commission" usually means the money is in the spread.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset designed to keep a stable value against a reference asset, usually a currency.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset designed to keep a stable value against a reference asset, usually a currency. It may be backed by reserves, by crypto collateral or by an algorithm.

concepts.shortDefinition: The FSB's term for the whole set of firms around a coin — issuer, reserve manager, custodian banks, distributors, market makers, wallet providers and blockchains.
concepts.bodyHtml: The FSB's term for the whole set of firms around a coin — issuer, reserve manager, custodian banks, distributors, market makers, wallet providers and blockchains. A failure at any of them can break the coin.

concepts.shortDefinition: Doubt about reserves leads holders to sell or redeem at once, forcing reserve sales and a fall below par.
concepts.bodyHtml: Doubt about reserves leads holders to sell or redeem at once, forcing reserve sales and a fall below par. Usually without deposit insurance or a lender of last resort; transparency speeds it up.

concepts.shortDefinition: The owner of tokens who puts them behind a validator and shares the rewards and penalties.
concepts.bodyHtml: The owner of tokens who puts them behind a validator and shares the rewards and penalties. Clients of a staking service bear slashing and lock-up risk unless the contract says otherwise.

concepts.shortDefinition: Locking up coins to help secure a proof of stake network, in return for rewards.
concepts.bodyHtml: Locking up coins to help secure a proof of stake network, in return for rewards.

sectorNotes.defi: In DeFi, staking also describes locking tokens in a protocol's smart contracts to earn a share of fees or incentives, often through liquid staking or restaking protocols. This adds smart-contract risk to the network's own penalties.

concepts.shortDefinition: A firm that runs validators using other people's tokens, for a fee.
concepts.bodyHtml: A firm that runs validators using other people's tokens, for a fee. Custodians and exchanges often provide staking, which brings outsourcing and concentration risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: A provider pools customers' tokens, stakes them with validators and passes on rewards less a commission.
concepts.bodyHtml: A provider pools customers' tokens, stakes them with validators and passes on rewards less a commission. It may need a VASP licence depending on the facts and for whom it is done.

concepts.shortDefinition: A price that no longer reflects an asset’s current value because the asset has not traded recently, for example because it has been suspended, delisted or become illiquid.
concepts.bodyHtml: A price that no longer reflects an asset’s current value because the asset has not traded recently, for example because it has been suspended, delisted or become illiquid. Valuation procedures must deal with it.

concepts.shortDefinition: The simplest fund structure: a single fund with no structural connection to any other fund, with its own prospectus, service contracts and authorisation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The simplest fund structure: a single fund with no structural connection to any other fund, with its own prospectus, service contracts and authorisation.

concepts.shortDefinition: An MMF that may hold assets with longer maturities than a short-term MMF, subject to a WAM of no more than six months and a WAL of no more than 12 months.
concepts.bodyHtml: An MMF that may hold assets with longer maturities than a short-term MMF, subject to a WAM of no more than six months and a WAL of no more than 12 months. It must be a VNAV MMF.

concepts.shortDefinition: The responsible oversight of the companies in which a fund invests, including monitoring, engagement and voting, to protect and enhance long-term value for investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The responsible oversight of the companies in which a fund invests, including monitoring, engagement and voting, to protect and enhance long-term value for investors. Under SRD II asset managers must publish an engagement policy on a comply-or-explain basis, and UCITS ManCos and AIFMs must have a strategy for exercising voting rights.

concepts.shortDefinition: A regulated exchange on which shares, bonds, ETFs and other securities are listed and traded.
concepts.bodyHtml: A regulated exchange on which shares, bonds, ETFs and other securities are listed and traded. Listed funds must comply with its rules and filing obligations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The automated passing of orders, prices and settlement instructions between systems without manual re-keying, which reduces errors and costs.
concepts.bodyHtml: The automated passing of orders, prices and settlement instructions between systems without manual re-keying, which reduces errors and costs.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund, such as a structured UCITS, whose return is determined by a pre-set formula linked to the performance of assets or indices, often with capital protection provided through derivatives.
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund, such as a structured UCITS, whose return is determined by a pre-set formula linked to the performance of assets or indices, often with capital protection provided through derivatives. Structured UCITS are complex products under MiFID II.

concepts.shortDefinition: Splitting transfers into smaller amounts to stay below an alert, enhanced due diligence or Travel Rule threshold.
concepts.bodyHtml: Splitting transfers into smaller amounts to stay below an alert, enhanced due diligence or Travel Rule threshold. A classic FATF red-flag indicator.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity to which a fund depositary delegates the custody of some of a fund’s assets, often in a particular market.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity to which a fund depositary delegates the custody of some of a fund’s assets, often in a particular market. The fund depositary remains liable for the assets; a prime broker holding a hedge fund’s assets acts as sub-custodian.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: A firm appointed by the custodian that holds keys or wallets. A technology vendor that can sign, block or recover transactions is acting as a sub-custodian in substance.

concepts.shortDefinition: The further delegation of a delegated function or task by a delegate, such as an investment manager appointing a sub-investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: The further delegation of a delegated function or task by a delegate, such as an investment manager appointing a sub-investment manager. It is subject to the same conditions as delegation and to the ManCo’s consent and oversight.

concepts.shortDefinition: A separate compartment of an umbrella fund with its own portfolio, investment policy and assets and liabilities, described in its own prospectus supplement.
concepts.bodyHtml: A separate compartment of an umbrella fund with its own portfolio, investment policy and assets and liabilities, described in its own prospectus supplement. Also called a compartment.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIFM whose assets under management do not exceed the AIFMD thresholds of €100 million, or €500 million for unleveraged AIFs with no redemption rights for five years.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIFM whose assets under management do not exceed the AIFMD thresholds of €100 million, or €500 million for unleveraged AIFs with no redemption rights for five years. It must register and report to its regulator but is not subject to the full AIFMD unless it opts in. Also called an exempt AIFM.

concepts.shortDefinition: The process by which an investor puts money (or, exceptionally, assets) into a fund and receives newly issued units or shares in return.
concepts.bodyHtml: The process by which an investor puts money (or, exceptionally, assets) into a fund and receives newly issued units or shares in return.

concepts.shortDefinition: The annual tax (taxe d’abonnement) paid by Luxembourg funds on their NAV, generally 0.05%, reduced to 0.01% for MMFs, SIFs and institutional share classes, with exemptions for some fund types.
concepts.bodyHtml: The annual tax (taxe d’abonnement) paid by Luxembourg funds on their NAV, generally 0.05%, reduced to 0.01% for MMFs, SIFs and institutional share classes, with exemptions for some fund types. It is a cost borne by investors.

concepts.shortDefinition: The human and technical resources a ManCo must have in its home state to control the funds it manages and oversee its delegates.
concepts.bodyHtml: The human and technical resources a ManCo must have in its home state to control the funds it manages and oversee its delegates. Since 16 April 2026, at least two persons conducting its business must be employed or engaged full-time and resident in the EEA.

concepts.shortDefinition: A venue that takes over the clients and liquidity of a sanctioned or closed exchange, as Grinex did for Garantex.
concepts.bodyHtml: A venue that takes over the clients and liquidity of a sanctioned or closed exchange, as Grinex did for Garantex. Sanctions screening needs to follow successor venues and their tokens.

concepts.shortDefinition: The MiFID II assessment that a firm giving investment advice or managing a portfolio must carry out of a client’s knowledge and experience, financial situation, objectives and sustainability preferences, so that only suitable funds are recommended.
concepts.bodyHtml: The MiFID II assessment that a firm giving investment advice or managing a portfolio must carry out of a client’s knowledge and experience, financial situation, objectives and sustainability preferences, so that only suitable funds are recommended.

concepts.shortDefinition: The risk measure in the PRIIPs KID that ranks a product on a scale from 1 (lower risk) to 7 (higher risk), combining market risk and credit risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: The risk measure in the PRIIPs KID that ranks a product on a scale from 1 (lower risk) to 7 (higher risk), combining market risk and credit risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: The Travel Rule takes effect at different times in different countries, so a counterparty may be unable to send or receive the required information.
concepts.bodyHtml: The Travel Rule takes effect at different times in different countries, so a counterparty may be unable to send or receive the required information. Firms must decide, and record, how they handle such transfers.

concepts.shortDefinition: A ManCo authorised both as a UCITS ManCo and as an AIFM, allowing a single fund management group to manage both its UCITS and its AIFs; also called a universal ManCo.
concepts.bodyHtml: A ManCo authorised both as a UCITS ManCo and as an AIFM, allowing a single fund management group to manage both its UCITS and its AIFs; also called a universal ManCo. Each fund or umbrella is still either a UCITS or an AIF. Super ManCos are common in Ireland and Luxembourg.

concepts.shortDefinition: A standing arrangement for the supervisors of a cross-border group to share information and coordinate, backed by MoUs.
concepts.bodyHtml: A standing arrangement for the supervisors of a cross-border group to share information and coordinate, backed by MoUs. Essential when the keys, reserves or operations sit abroad.

concepts.shortDefinition: The regular reporting of information by managers to their NCA, such as AIFMD reporting on each AIF’s exposures, leverage and liquidity.
concepts.bodyHtml: The regular reporting of information by managers to their NCA, such as AIFMD reporting on each AIF’s exposures, leverage and liquidity. From 16 April 2027, enhanced reporting under AIFMD II includes delegation arrangements.

concepts.shortDefinition: The compromise of a supplier - a device, firmware, software library, reseller or vendor - that reaches every one of its customers.
concepts.bodyHtml: The compromise of a supplier - a device, firmware, software library, reseller or vendor - that reaches every one of its customers. Examples include the Ledger Connect Kit attack (2023) and the Bybit hack through Safe{Wallet} (2025).

concepts.shortDefinition: The temporary halting of subscriptions and redemptions, permitted only in exceptional circumstances where justified in investors’ interests.
concepts.bodyHtml: The temporary halting of subscriptions and redemptions, permitted only in exceptional circumstances where justified in investors’ interests. It is a tool of last resort, and the regulator must be notified without delay.

concepts.shortDefinition: A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit where a firm knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing (FATF Recommendation 20).
concepts.bodyHtml: A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit where a firm knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing (FATF Recommendation 20). The threshold is low. A useful crypto report names the typology and attaches addresses, transaction hashes and the trace.

concepts.shortDefinition: Environmental, social and employee matters, respect for human rights, and anti-corruption and anti-bribery matters.
concepts.bodyHtml: Environmental, social and employee matters, respect for human rights, and anti-corruption and anti-bribery matters.

concepts.shortDefinition: A client’s choice, which MiFID II advisers and portfolio managers must ask about in the suitability assessment, for a minimum proportion of Taxonomy-aligned investments, a minimum proportion of sustainable investments, or consideration of PAIs).
concepts.bodyHtml: A client’s choice, which MiFID II advisers and portfolio managers must ask about in the suitability assessment, for a minimum proportion of Taxonomy-aligned investments, a minimum proportion of sustainable investments, or consideration of PAIs).

concepts.shortDefinition: An environmental, social or governance event or condition that, if it occurs, could cause an actual or a potential material negative impact on the value of an investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: An environmental, social or governance event or condition that, if it occurs, could cause an actual or a potential material negative impact on the value of an investment. It looks inwards, at the effect of ESG events on the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: The requirement, since 1 August 2022 under the amended UCITS and AIFMD delegated rules, for UCITS ManCos and AIFMs to integrate sustainability risks into their organisation, risk management, due diligence and conflicts of interest processes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The requirement, since 1 August 2022 under the amended UCITS and AIFMD delegated rules, for UCITS ManCos and AIFMs to integrate sustainability risks into their organisation, risk management, due diligence and conflicts of interest processes.

concepts.shortDefinition: Regulation (EU) 2019/2088, applying since 10 March 2021, which requires financial market participants, including UCITS ManCos and AIFMs, to disclose how they integrate sustainability risks and consider PAIs, at entity and product level.
concepts.bodyHtml: Regulation (EU) 2019/2088, applying since 10 March 2021, which requires financial market participants, including UCITS ManCos and AIFMs, to disclose how they integrate sustainability risks and consider PAIs, at entity and product level. Funds are commonly classified under it as Article 6, 8 or 9 funds).

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the SFDR, an investment in an economic activity that contributes to an environmental or social objective, does not significantly harm any such objective, and whose investee companies follow good governance practices.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the SFDR, an investment in an economic activity that contributes to an environmental or social objective, does not significantly harm any such objective, and whose investee companies follow good governance practices.

concepts.shortDefinition: A derivative in which two parties exchange payment streams, such as fixed for floating interest or the return on an index for a fixed or floating rate.
concepts.bodyHtml: A derivative in which two parties exchange payment streams, such as fixed for floating interest or the return on an index for a fixed or floating rate. Synthetic ETFs use swaps to obtain an index’s return.

concepts.shortDefinition: Adjusting a fund’s NAV by a swing factor, upwards on net subscriptions and downwards on net redemptions, so that dealing costs fall on the investors who trade.
concepts.bodyHtml: Adjusting a fund’s NAV by a swing factor, upwards on net subscriptions and downwards on net redemptions, so that dealing costs fall on the investors who trade. Under partial swing pricing the adjustment applies only when net flows exceed a set threshold. It is an anti-dilution LMT.

concepts.shortDefinition: Redeeming units or shares in one sub-fund or share class and using the proceeds to buy units or shares in another of the same umbrella, usually without initial charges.
concepts.bodyHtml: Redeeming units or shares in one sub-fund or share class and using the proceeds to buy units or shares in another of the same umbrella, usually without initial charges. Also called exchanging or converting.

concepts.shortDefinition: An index-tracking ETF that obtains the return of the index through derivatives, such as swaps, rather than holding the securities, and so is exposed to counterparty risk.
concepts.bodyHtml: An index-tracking ETF that obtains the return of the index through derivatives, such as swaps, rather than holding the securities, and so is exposed to counterparty risk.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token that aims for a stable value by holding crypto-assets and an offsetting short position in perpetual futures, so that price moves cancel out ("delta-neutral"), rather than by holding cash (for example Ethena's USDe).
concepts.bodyHtml: A token that aims for a stable value by holding crypto-assets and an offsetting short position in perpetual futures, so that price moves cancel out ("delta-neutral"), rather than by holding cash (for example Ethena's USDe). Its yield comes from funding rates, which can turn negative.

concepts.shortDefinition: A sterling stablecoin that is, or is likely to become, so widely used for payments in the UK that its failure could threaten financial stability.
concepts.bodyHtml: A sterling stablecoin that is, or is likely to become, so widely used for payments in the UK that its failure could threaten financial stability. Systemic stablecoins are recognised by HM Treasury and regulated by the Bank of England; other stablecoins are regulated by the FCA.

concepts.shortDefinition: The type of end investor whose needs, characteristics, objectives and sustainability-related objectives a fund is designed to meet.
concepts.bodyHtml: The type of end investor whose needs, characteristics, objectives and sustainability-related objectives a fund is designed to meet.

concepts.shortDefinition: Freezing designated persons' funds and making nothing available to them, without delay and with no risk-based discretion (FATF R.6 and R.7).
concepts.bodyHtml: Freezing designated persons' funds and making nothing available to them, without delay and with no risk-based discretion (FATF R.6 and R.7). Reports go to the sanctions authority by the route the national law sets.

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle that a fund itself should not create additional tax for investors, so that their tax liability depends on where they are resident.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle that a fund itself should not create additional tax for investors, so that their tax liability depends on where they are resident. Irish and Luxembourg funds are generally exempt from tax on their income and gains.

concepts.shortDefinition: Treatment of a fund under which its income and gains are taxed as if they accrued directly to its investors rather than to the fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: Treatment of a fund under which its income and gains are taxed as if they accrued directly to its investors rather than to the fund. Contractual funds and limited partnerships are generally tax-transparent.

concepts.shortDefinition: An agreement between two countries that allocates taxing rights and reduces taxes on income flowing between them, to mitigate double taxation.
concepts.bodyHtml: An agreement between two countries that allocates taxing rights and reduces taxes on income flowing between them, to mitigate double taxation. Fund domiciles develop networks of them.

concepts.shortDefinition: An investment in an economic activity that qualifies as environmentally sustainable under the EU Taxonomy.
concepts.bodyHtml: An investment in an economic activity that qualifies as environmentally sustainable under the EU Taxonomy. Article 8 and 9 funds disclose their minimum and actual proportion of such investments).

concepts.shortDefinition: Whether a country's laws and rules meet each FATF Recommendation.
concepts.bodyHtml: Whether a country's laws and rules meet each FATF Recommendation. It is necessary but not sufficient; countries with strong technical ratings can still be grey-listed for weak effectiveness.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short document summarising the key terms of a fund being offered to professional investors, such as its strategy, minimum commitment, investment period, drawdowns, fees and management team.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short document summarising the key terms of a fund being offered to professional investors, such as its strategy, minimum commitment, investment period, drawdowns, fees and management team.

concepts.shortDefinition: One topic examined across many firms, such as critical wallet providers, to find shared weaknesses and set sector expectations.
concepts.bodyHtml: One topic examined across many firms, such as critical wallet providers, to find shared weaknesses and set sector expectations.

concepts.shortDefinition: The AIFMD mechanism under which non-EEA AIFMs and AIFs could be marketed across the EEA under a passport.
concepts.bodyHtml: The AIFMD mechanism under which non-EEA AIFMs and AIFs could be marketed across the EEA under a passport. It requires activation by the European Commission and has not been switched on, so non-EEA AIFs rely on NPPRs.

concepts.shortDefinition: An independent ManCo, not part of the promoter’s group, that acts as ManCo for the funds of many unrelated promoters and typically delegates portfolio management back to the promoter as investment manager.
concepts.bodyHtml: An independent ManCo, not part of the promoter’s group, that acts as ManCo for the funds of many unrelated promoters and typically delegates portfolio management back to the promoter as investment manager.

concepts.shortDefinition: A governance model in which business functions own and manage risk (first line), the risk management and compliance functions oversee it (second line) and internal audit provides independent assurance (third line).
concepts.bodyHtml: A governance model in which business functions own and manage risk (first line), the risk management and compliance functions oversee it (second line) and internal audit provides independent assurance (third line).

concepts.shortDefinition: A daily comparison of on-chain balances (ideally from the firm's own node), the internal ledger and client statements, with every difference logged and resolved.
concepts.bodyHtml: A daily comparison of on-chain balances (ideally from the firm's own node), the internal ledger and client statements, with every difference logged and resolved.

concepts.shortDefinition: A built-in delay before an approved smart contract change takes effect, giving users notice so that changes are visible before they apply.
concepts.bodyHtml: A built-in delay before an approved smart contract change takes effect, giving users notice so that changes are visible before they apply.

concepts.shortDefinition: Telling a customer or anyone else that a suspicious activity report has been made or that an investigation is under way.
concepts.bodyHtml: Telling a customer or anyone else that a suspicious activity report has been made or that an investigation is under way. It is a criminal offence in most countries.

concepts.shortDefinition: A way of providing collateral in which full ownership passes to the receiver, who must return equivalent assets when the obligation is discharged, as under an English law Credit Support Annex.
concepts.bodyHtml: A way of providing collateral in which full ownership passes to the receiver, who must return equivalent assets when the obligation is discharged, as under an English law Credit Support Annex.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The client hands over ownership and holds only a claim, so it queues as a creditor on insolvency (Celsius Earn, January 2023).

concepts.shortDefinition: A unit recorded on a blockchain - either a native coin built into the protocol (such as bitcoin or ether) or a token issued by a smart contract.
concepts.bodyHtml: A unit recorded on a blockchain - either a native coin built into the protocol (such as bitcoin or ether) or a token issued by a smart contract. Its legal rights, not its technology, decide which regulatory regime applies.

concepts.shortDefinition: Representing an asset, or a right in an asset, as a token on a distributed ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: Representing an asset, or a right in an asset, as a token on a distributed ledger.

sectorNotes.funds-asset-managers: Representing fund units or shares, or the assets a fund holds, as digital tokens recorded using DLT, such as a blockchain. The legal rights of investors are unchanged.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bank's deposit liability recorded on a ledger.
concepts.bodyHtml: A bank's deposit liability recorded on a ledger. Banking law applies; digital fiat is excluded from the virtual-asset definition.

concepts.shortDefinition: A money-market fund whose units are issued as tokens and used as on-chain cash or collateral, for example BlackRock's BUIDL, launched in March 2024.
concepts.bodyHtml: A money-market fund whose units are issued as tokens and used as on-chain cash or collateral, for example BlackRock's BUIDL, launched in March 2024.

concepts.shortDefinition: A measure of a fund’s annual operating costs as a percentage of its average NAV, commonly quoted for ETFs.
concepts.bodyHtml: A measure of a fund’s annual operating costs as a percentage of its average NAV, commonly quoted for ETFs. It is broadly equivalent to the OCF.

concepts.shortDefinition: The value of assets deposited in a DeFi protocol or network.
concepts.bodyHtml: The value of assets deposited in a DeFi protocol or network.

concepts.shortDefinition: The difference between the return of an index fund, such as an index ETF, and the return of the index it tracks, over a period.
concepts.bodyHtml: The difference between the return of an index fund, such as an index ETF, and the return of the index it tracks, over a period. Tracking error is the volatility of this difference.

concepts.shortDefinition: The volatility of the tracking difference, which is the gap between an index fund’s return and the return of its index.
concepts.bodyHtml: The volatility of the tracking difference, which is the gap between an index fund’s return and the return of its index. Managers of passive funds seek to keep both low.

concepts.shortDefinition: An entity that centrally collects and maintains records of derivatives or securities financing transactions reported under EMIR or the SFTR, for use by regulators.
concepts.bodyHtml: An entity that centrally collects and maintains records of derivatives or securities financing transactions reported under EMIR or the SFTR, for use by regulators.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under MiFID II, a regulated market, multilateral trading facility or organised trading facility on which financial instruments are traded.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under MiFID II, a regulated market, multilateral trading facility or organised trading facility on which financial instruments are traded.

concepts.shortDefinition: An instruction to move value from one address to another.
concepts.bodyHtml: An instruction to move value from one address to another. Once confirmed, a blockchain transaction is usually final, with no recall and no chargeback.

concepts.shortDefinition: The costs of buying and selling a fund’s portfolio assets, such as brokerage, spreads and taxes.
concepts.bodyHtml: The costs of buying and selling a fund’s portfolio assets, such as brokerage, spreads and taxes. They reduce returns but are not part of the management fee and are excluded from the OCF, though included in the KID.

concepts.shortDefinition: Reviewing customers' transactions, manually or automatically, to detect unusual or suspicious activity.
concepts.bodyHtml: Reviewing customers' transactions, manually or automatically, to detect unusual or suspicious activity.

concepts.shortDefinition: The contract appointing a TA, describing its services, such as processing application forms, subscriptions and redemptions, confirming deals and maintaining the register and paying dividends.
concepts.bodyHtml: The contract appointing a TA, describing its services, such as processing application forms, subscriptions and redemptions, confirming deals and maintaining the register and paying dividends.

concepts.shortDefinition: The entity, often the fund administrator, that maintains the register of investors and processes subscriptions, redemptions, transfers and switches, including the AML and customer due diligence checks on investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The entity, often the fund administrator, that maintains the register of investors and processes subscriptions, redemptions, transfers and switches, including the AML and customer due diligence checks on investors.

sectorNotes.digital-assets-web3: The firm that keeps the register of a fund's or issuer's holders and processes transfers; in BUIDL, Securitize. Franklin Templeton runs its own for BENJI.

concepts.shortDefinition: Negotiable securities such as shares, bonds and other debt securities.
concepts.bodyHtml: Negotiable securities such as shares, bonds and other debt securities. They are the core eligible asset of a UCITS.

concepts.shortDefinition: FATF Recommendation 16 as applied to virtual assets: originator and beneficiary information must travel with a transfer between VASPs.
concepts.bodyHtml: FATF Recommendation 16 as applied to virtual assets: originator and beneficiary information must travel with a transfer between VASPs.

concepts.shortDefinition: A short-term debt instrument issued by a government, sold at a discount to its face value and paying no interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: A short-term debt instrument issued by a government, sold at a discount to its face value and paying no interest. It is a money market instrument.

concepts.shortDefinition: Assets stay at a custodian, pledged to an exchange that mirrors the balance for trading.
concepts.bodyHtml: Assets stay at a custodian, pledged to an exchange that mirrors the balance for trading. Exposure shrinks to the unsettled amount; the legal terms decide who can release the collateral.

concepts.shortDefinition: The standard against which an external auditor gives its opinion on financial statements.
concepts.bodyHtml: The standard against which an external auditor gives its opinion on financial statements. It is not defined, but is generally understood to mean that the accounting policies are appropriate and comply with accounting standards (“true”) and that the accounts do not distort or mislead (“fair”).

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal arrangement under which a trustee holds property as legal owner for the benefit of beneficiaries, who are the beneficial owners.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal arrangement under which a trustee holds property as legal owner for the benefit of beneficiaries, who are the beneficial owners. It is recognised by common law systems. Luxembourg recognises foreign trusts and has its own fiduciary contract, the fiducie.

concepts.shortDefinition: The document constituting a unit trust or other trust, which sets out the terms on which the assets are held and managed and the rights and obligations of the trustee, the manager and the beneficiaries.
concepts.bodyHtml: The document constituting a unit trust or other trust, which sets out the terms on which the assets are held and managed and the rights and obligations of the trustee, the manager and the beneficiaries.

concepts.shortDefinition: A legal owner of property who holds it on behalf of, and carries out active duties for, beneficial owners.
concepts.bodyHtml: A legal owner of property who holds it on behalf of, and carries out active duties for, beneficial owners. In a unit trust, the fund depositary acts as trustee and is the legal owner of the fund’s assets.

concepts.shortDefinition: A recognised pattern of criminal use, such as scams, ransomware, hacks, sanctions evasion, darknet markets or terrorist financing.
concepts.bodyHtml: A recognised pattern of criminal use, such as scams, ransomware, hacks, sanctions evasion, darknet markets or terrorist financing.

concepts.shortDefinition: Directive 2009/65/EC (the UCITS IV recast, as amended), the EU framework for UCITS.
concepts.bodyHtml: Directive 2009/65/EC (the UCITS IV recast, as amended), the EU framework for UCITS. It sets product rules, management company rules, depositary rules and disclosure rules, and gives UCITS a product passport and UCITS ManCos a management passport.

concepts.shortDefinition: The 2009 recast of the UCITS Directive, which facilitated cross-border marketing, introduced the management company passport, fund mergers and master-feeder structures, and replaced the simplified prospectus with the KIID.
concepts.bodyHtml: The 2009 recast of the UCITS Directive, which facilitated cross-border marketing, introduced the management company passport, fund mergers and master-feeder structures, and replaced the simplified prospectus with the KIID.

concepts.shortDefinition: Directive 2014/91/EU, applying from 18 March 2016, which harmonised depositary eligibility, duties and liability, introduced remuneration policies for UCITS ManCos and harmonised administrative sanctions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Directive 2014/91/EU, applying from 18 March 2016, which harmonised depositary eligibility, duties and liability, introduced remuneration policies for UCITS ManCos and harmonised administrative sanctions.

concepts.shortDefinition: The name commonly given to the amendments made to the UCITSD by AIFMD II from 16 April 2026, covering LMTs, delegation reporting, substance and additional services.
concepts.bodyHtml: The name commonly given to the amendments made to the UCITSD by AIFMD II from 16 April 2026, covering LMTs, delegation reporting, substance and additional services.

concepts.shortDefinition: An account in the name of an Irish umbrella fund through which subscription and redemption monies pass before shares are issued or redemption proceeds are paid.
concepts.bodyHtml: An account in the name of an Irish umbrella fund through which subscription and redemption monies pass before shares are issued or redemption proceeds are paid. Investors whose money is in it may rank as unsecured creditors of the fund.

concepts.shortDefinition: A single fund vehicle containing several sub-funds, each with its own investment policy and portfolio, governed by one constitutional document.
concepts.bodyHtml: A single fund vehicle containing several sub-funds, each with its own investment policy and portfolio, governed by one constitutional document. An umbrella is authorised under one regime, so it cannot mix UCITS and AIF sub-funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: A crypto-asset, such as bitcoin, that is not backed by any asset or issuer and whose value depends only on supply and demand.
concepts.bodyHtml: A crypto-asset, such as bitcoin, that is not backed by any asset or issuer and whose value depends only on supply and demand.

concepts.term: Undertaking for collective investment in transferable securities
concepts.shortDefinition: An open-ended fund authorised under the UCITS Directive that raises capital from the public, invests in transferable securities and other eligible liquid assets subject to diversification rules, and entrusts its assets to an independent fund depositary.
concepts.bodyHtml: An open-ended fund authorised under the UCITS Directive that raises capital from the public, invests in transferable securities and other eligible liquid assets subject to diversification rules, and entrusts its assets to an independent fund depositary. A UCITS can be marketed to retail investors throughout the EEA under a passport.
concepts.sortKey: undertaking for collective investment in transferable securities

concepts.shortDefinition: Costs charged to a fund or its investors that are not justified by, or are disproportionate to, the service provided.
concepts.bodyHtml: Costs charged to a fund or its investors that are not justified by, or are disproportionate to, the service provided. UCITS ManCos and AIFMs must prevent them.

concepts.shortDefinition: A fund constituted under a trust deed between a ManCo and a trustee (the fund depositary), which is the legal owner of the assets on behalf of the investors (unitholders).
concepts.bodyHtml: A fund constituted under a trust deed between a ManCo and a trustee (the fund depositary), which is the legal owner of the assets on behalf of the investors (unitholders). A unit trust has no legal personality. Irish unit trusts are established under the Unit Trusts Act 1990 or, for UCITS, the UCITS Regulations.

concepts.shortDefinition: An insurance-based investment product whose value is linked to units of underlying funds.
concepts.bodyHtml: An insurance-based investment product whose value is linked to units of underlying funds. It is a PRIIP and an indirect route through which investors gain exposure to funds.

concepts.shortDefinition: The instruments evidencing an investor’s interest in a fund: units in a unit trust or contractual fund, shares in a corporate fund.
concepts.bodyHtml: The instruments evidencing an investor’s interest in a fund: units in a unit trust or contractual fund, shares in a corporate fund. The terms are often used interchangeably; interests in a limited partnership are partnership interests.

concepts.shortDefinition: An AIF that is not itself authorised or supervised by a regulator, such as a Luxembourg SCSp not established as a SIF or RAIF.
concepts.bodyHtml: An AIF that is not itself authorised or supervised by a regulator, such as a Luxembourg SCSp not established as a SIF or RAIF. Its manager may still be regulated under the AIFMD.

concepts.shortDefinition: A creditor with no security over the debtor’s assets, who ranks behind secured and preferential creditors in a liquidation.
concepts.bodyHtml: A creditor with no security over the debtor’s assets, who ranks behind secured and preferential creditors in a liquidation. A fund with cash at a failed bank, and investors whose money is in umbrella cash collection accounts, may rank as unsecured creditors.

concepts.shortDefinition: A smart contract whose logic can be replaced while its address and balances stay the same, usually through a proxy contract.
concepts.bodyHtml: A smart contract whose logic can be replaced while its address and balances stay the same, usually through a proxy contract. Whoever controls the upgrade key can change every rule, which is why multi-party approval and time locks matter.

concepts.shortDefinition: In proof of stake, a participant who stakes coins and runs software to propose and attest to blocks.
concepts.bodyHtml: In proof of stake, a participant who stakes coins and runs software to propose and attest to blocks.

concepts.shortDefinition: The time at which a fund’s assets are valued to calculate the NAV for a dealing day.
concepts.bodyHtml: The time at which a fund’s assets are valued to calculate the NAV for a dealing day.

concepts.shortDefinition: A statistical estimate of the maximum loss a portfolio is likely to suffer over a given period at a given confidence level.
concepts.bodyHtml: A statistical estimate of the maximum loss a portfolio is likely to suffer over a given period at a given confidence level. A UCITS using VaR is normally limited to an absolute VaR of 20% of NAV or a relative VaR of twice that of a reference portfolio.

concepts.shortDefinition: The stages through which a fund is created, invested, distributed and operated, each of which is regulated – the fund as a product, the investment of its portfolio, its distribution to investors and its ongoing operation.
concepts.bodyHtml: The stages through which a fund is created, invested, distributed and operated, each of which is regulated – the fund as a product, the investment of its portfolio, its distribution to investors and its ongoing operation.

concepts.shortDefinition: The principle that a product’s costs are justified and proportionate to the benefits it delivers to investors.
concepts.bodyHtml: The principle that a product’s costs are justified and proportionate to the benefits it delivers to investors. The EU Retail Investment Strategy, not yet applicable, would require manufacturers of retail investment products to assess it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A corporate fund whose share capital always equals its NAV, rising when investors subscribe and falling when they redeem.
concepts.bodyHtml: A corporate fund whose share capital always equals its NAV, rising when investors subscribe and falling when they redeem. Examples include the ICAV, the Irish investment company, the Luxembourg SICAV and the UK OEIC.

concepts.shortDefinition: An MMF that values its assets at market prices (mark-to-market or mark-to-model), so that its share price varies.
concepts.bodyHtml: An MMF that values its assets at market prices (mark-to-market or mark-to-model), so that its share price varies. Standard MMFs must be VNAV.

concepts.shortDefinition: Equity finance for young, unlisted, high-growth companies.
