concepts.bodyHtml: Equity finance for young, unlisted, high-growth companies. EuVECAs and SICARs are vehicles for it).

concepts.shortDefinition: A digitally signed attestation (e.g.
concepts.bodyHtml: A digitally signed attestation (e.g. 'KYC passed') held by the user and checked by the firm; W3C standard v2.0 (May 2025). It proves who signed, not how well they checked.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the FATF definition, a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the FATF definition, a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and used for payment or investment. It excludes digital representations of fiat currencies, securities and other financial assets covered elsewhere in the FATF Recommendations.

concepts.shortDefinition: Under the FATF definition, a person who, as a business, carries out one or more of five activities for or on behalf of another person - exchange between virtual assets and fiat, exchange between virtual assets, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services related to an issuer's offer or sale.
concepts.bodyHtml: Under the FATF definition, a person who, as a business, carries out one or more of five activities for or on behalf of another person - exchange between virtual assets and fiat, exchange between virtual assets, transfer, safekeeping or administration, and services related to an issuer's offer or sale. Defined by what it does, not what it calls itself.

concepts.shortDefinition: The CSSF’s approval stamp on the offering document of a Luxembourg UCITS, Part II fund or SIF.
concepts.bodyHtml: The CSSF’s approval stamp on the offering document of a Luxembourg UCITS, Part II fund or SIF.

concepts.shortDefinition: Software or hardware that stores keys and lets a user see balances and sign transactions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Software or hardware that stores keys and lets a user see balances and sign transactions. The assets themselves stay on the blockchain.

concepts.shortDefinition: Online, but every movement needs human approvals and policy checks.
concepts.bodyHtml: Online, but every movement needs human approvals and policy checks. Usually refills the hot wallet within hours.

concepts.shortDefinition: A security giving the holder the right to buy a company’s shares at a specified price within a set period.
concepts.bodyHtml: A security giving the holder the right to buy a company’s shares at a specified price within a set period.

concepts.shortDefinition: Trading with oneself, or with colluding parties, to create the false appearance of volume or price movement.
concepts.bodyHtml: Trading with oneself, or with colluding parties, to create the false appearance of volume or price movement.

concepts.shortDefinition: The average length of time to legal maturity of all the assets of an MMF, weighted by their relative holdings.
concepts.bodyHtml: The average length of time to legal maturity of all the assets of an MMF, weighted by their relative holdings.

concepts.shortDefinition: The average length of time to legal maturity or, if shorter, to the next interest rate reset, of all the assets of an MMF, weighted by their relative holdings.
concepts.bodyHtml: The average length of time to legal maturity or, if shorter, to the next interest rate reset, of all the assets of an MMF, weighted by their relative holdings.

concepts.shortDefinition: In Luxembourg, an investor eligible to invest in a SIF or RAIF: an institutional or professional investor, or another investor who confirms in writing that they are well informed and either invests at least €100,000 (since the Law of 21 July 2023) or has their expertise certified by a regulated entity.
concepts.bodyHtml: In Luxembourg, an investor eligible to invest in a SIF or RAIF: an institutional or professional investor, or another investor who confirms in writing that they are well informed and either invests at least €100,000 (since the Law of 21 July 2023) or has their expertise certified by a regulated entity.

concepts.shortDefinition: An exchange or wallet system operated by a technology provider under another firm's brand.
concepts.bodyHtml: An exchange or wallet system operated by a technology provider under another firm's brand. The regulated firm remains responsible, so it needs visibility of, and control over, the platform and a way to exit it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A list of approved addresses or users.
concepts.bodyHtml: A list of approved addresses or users. Withdrawal whitelists restrict where funds can be sent; token whitelists restrict who can hold a token, which is common in tokenised funds. A whitelist is only as strong as the approvals needed to add an address.

concepts.shortDefinition: Central bank money on a ledger for use between financial institutions.
concepts.bodyHtml: Central bank money on a ledger for use between financial institutions. The safest settlement asset, but so far experimental (EIB 2021, Project Venus).

concepts.shortDefinition: Tax deducted at source from payments such as dividends or interest.
concepts.bodyHtml: Tax deducted at source from payments such as dividends or interest. In Ireland, investors who are not tax resident may receive fund distributions without it.

concepts.shortDefinition: A token on one blockchain that represents an asset held on another, such as wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum, backed by a custodian or a bridge.
concepts.bodyHtml: A token on one blockchain that represents an asset held on another, such as wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum, backed by a custodian or a bridge. It is a different claim from the original and may not carry the original's controls or regulatory status.

concepts.shortDefinition: The return on an asset, such as interest, staking rewards or trading fees, usually expressed as an annual percentage.
concepts.bodyHtml: The return on an asset, such as interest, staking rewards or trading fees, usually expressed as an annual percentage.

concepts.shortDefinition: A bond that pays no interest but is issued at a discount to its face value, the investor’s return being the difference between the issue price and the amount repaid.
